body.title: Party and the Lil Boy
body.body:
They visited a friend in the city. She had a pool where they swam to their heart's content. In the afternoon, they attended an alumni party where they met some old acquaintances. They teased her nonstop about her lil boy, who, at the time, was playful and sociable, letting people cuddle him.
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ifarmgirl/23w2eJaRUmcj53RJsZYKxTgtsEgUXimY4yM3e2n6evYLTdb92LmAFfSegzpfYPNFLe5S5.jpeg
\

bantered another. Their laughter filled the air. There was never a dull moment with them all together.

Then one of them suggested a drink was overdue, and everyone agreed. However, their preferred drink wasn't available, so they thought they could buy some from the convenience store a few blocks away. Remembering her little boy had run out of diapers, she went out with two of them after making sure her baby was okay.

While returning to the party, she ran into her cousin, Jen, whom she hadn't seen for a long while. Her companions went ahead with the drinks. Jen thought they could take a table at the nearby coffeehouse to catch up a bit. It had been 5 years since they last saw each other. They lost track of time, and it was almost dark when they walked out of the Café.

She rushed back to the party, but most people were gone, and her acquaintances were not around either. \
she asked Jam, who was about to leave the venue. \n\n\
Jam sensed she was worried. She rang Ruby. She only had her number. But Ruby said she went home earlier than the group. \
Ruby explained.\n\nShe left, frantically running through the busiest street toward the hilly section. \

she apologized as she squeezed herself through people on the sidewalk. She was worried to the point of crying out loud. She kept on running, wanting to reach the red house by the hill. She stumbled, twisting her ankle, just when she was so close to the roundabout. She wailed in pain.\n\n\

Her hubby's voice. She opened her eyes to see her little boy sleeping peacefully right beside her.
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ifarmgirl/24246fKcj8XaxPNn8G7CMrzugvR5kLxywAUjgbPtUvQ68xinyjeGYdDKGc7XCrwMMuRum.jpeg
She was panting, body shaking, as if her fingertips were getting pricked. It was but a nightmare, yet it felt so real. She wouldn't wish her boy to be so friendly, ever!

body.title: Drawing on a LiveStream - Original artwork
body.body: Hi friends! Lately, I've been livestreaming my drawings on TikTok. I haven't made any money yet, and to be honest, I doubt I ever will because donations for this type of content are almost non-existent. The average user on that platform prefers content that doesn't really offer anything interesting. I'm not saying that watching me draw is the most exciting thing in the world, but compared to those who just ask for donations for being there, doing NPC streams, or showing too much skin, I think my drawings are actually good content.\n\nOn the bright side, I have gained new followers, and they’ve been showing up for the last three drawings I've done. Something interesting happened with this specific piece: it was supposed to be more explicit. To be exact, she wasn't going to wear underwear; she was going to be completely naked. However, halfway through the livestream, a user reported it and the viewers stopped coming in. That forced me to \

to avoid further reports and risk losing my account or getting banned. So, well, this is the final result. I hope you like it, she’s a Yakuza girl, ready for anything.

---

ESPAÑOL

Hola amigos. Estos días he estado dibujando en directo en la plataforma de TikTok. Aún no he generado nada y, a decir verdad, dudo que llegue a ganar algo de dinero haciéndolo porque las donaciones a ese tipo de contenido son casi nulas. El usuario común de esa plataforma [consume] un tipo de contenido que realmente no deja nada interesante. No digo que yo dibujando sea lo más interesante del mundo, pero en comparación con los que piden donaciones directamente solo por estar ahí, haciendo NPC o enseñando más de la cuenta, creo que mis dibujos son un buen contenido.

A fin de cuentas, sí he tenido nuevos seguidores y ellos han estado presentes en los últimos tres dibujos que he hecho. Con este dibujo pasó algo interesante: iba a ser más explícito, para ser más concreto, no iba a tener la parte de abajo de la ropa interior, iba a estar totalmente desnuda. Pero cuando iba por la mitad del directo, un usuario lo reportó y dejó de llegar gente, lo que me obligó a \

para evitar que alguien más lo reportara y perder la cuenta o que me banearan de alguna manera. Así que bueno, este fue el resultado final. Espero les guste, es una chica yakuza preparada para todo.

body.title: The Day the Government Killed an AI: Inside Anthropic's Fable 5 Shutdown
body.body:
![header](https://ipfs.io/ipfs/QmUWB1vVfudcKDPpjcMpMrfpi87gi4jsVQLNREL99k7hqo)

**The unprecedented US export-control directive that took Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 offline just days after launch marks a turning point in the relationship between AI developers, national security, and the public.**

---

On June 12, 2026, at 5:21 PM Eastern Time, Anthropic received a letter from the US government that would change everything. The company had publicly released Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 just days earlier — models it described as the most capable AI systems it had ever built. Within hours, those same models were gone.

This is the first time in history that a government has ordered an AI model taken offline, and it happened not because of a catastrophic failure or a self-discovered vulnerability, but over a reported \

that, by many accounts, amounts to something security professionals do every day.

## What Happened

The US Department of Commerce issued an emergency export-control directive ordering Anthropic to suspend all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by any foreign national — whether inside or outside the United States, including Anthropic's own foreign-national employees. The directive cited national security concerns but provided no specific technical details.

Anthropic's response was stark: \

There is no reliable way to segment foreign nationals from US persons in real time across a user base of hundreds of millions, so the company turned the models off for everyone.

The reported trigger was a narrow jailbreak technique that allegedly allowed the model to identify software vulnerabilities in code. But here is what makes this story genuinely extraordinary: **asking an AI model to read a codebase and fix its flaws is not a hacking technique — it is automated code review, the same capability that defenders use to protect systems.**

## The Dual-Use Dilemma at Its Most Extreme

Anthropic argued in a blog post that the vulnerabilities identified were \
and that other publicly available models — including OpenAI's GPT-5.5 — can discover them without any jailbreak at all. The company noted that the government had only provided \

of a potential narrow, non-universal jailbreak.

Yet the UK government's AI Security Institute had tested Fable 5 and found it could exploit defenses and systems 73% of the time — a result that prompted both praise from defenders who wanted such capabilities and criticism from those worried about offensive use.

This is the dual-use dilemma in its purest form: a capability that makes an AI model more useful for cybersecurity defense is simultaneously what the government considers a national security risk. As one Hacker News commenter put it: \

## The Broader Context: Anthropic vs. the Government

This shutdown didn't happen in a vacuum. Earlier this year, Trump's Department of Defense labeled Anthropic a \

— the first time a US company had ever received such a designation, historically reserved for companies based in adversarial countries. Anthropic is currently suing the Pentagon over that designation, and a US judge has ruled the directive cannot be enforced while the lawsuit continues.\n\nCEO Dario Amodei had written a policy essay earlier this week arguing that he and the company support \
for blocking unsafe AI models. But in Friday's blog post, Anthropic made clear it believed this action \

## What It Means for the Future

The Fable 5 shutdown sends shockwaves through the AI industry. If a model can be pulled offline by executive order over an alleged jailbreak — with no public technical evidence and no due process — then no AI company's product is truly safe. The precedent could reshape how frontier models are developed, deployed, and governed.

The European Commission responded by saying the incident \
accelerating plans to reduce dependence on American and Asian AI infrastructure.\n\nProfessor Gina Neff of Queen Mary University London warned: \

The question now is whether the government will provide more details about the alleged jailbreak, whether Anthropic's lawsuit will succeed in restoring access, and what this means for the future of AI development when national security concerns can override public release — without transparency, without evidence, and without warning.

One thing is clear: the era of AI models operating entirely outside government oversight may be over. The question is whether that oversight will make us safer, or simply slower to build the tools we need.

body.title: My Splinterlands Diary: Buy Gladius Pack & Opening
body.body:
<center>https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://images.hive.blog/DQmcNsaFcaQViYoZNBVVwbz1MqkTGshwsdMxP8P4hUgS1gA/splinterlandsGIF.gif</center>

Hello Splinterlands players. Join me today as I buy and open gladiator packs after earning merits from weekly brawl. Our guild did well in the last brawl and I contributed with a record of five wins and only three losses. 

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSBcyGhAtyVKqdjG4Cp4ePG55RD3vVwsBJHpXeWqYrDr9/image.png)</center>

I'm a member of Gank's Squadron Guild, playing brawls weekly. From there, I earn rewards to buy packs which I will do today. My results in brawls improved because of the cards delegated to me by our leader. Anyway, the topic today is the gladiator cards I'm buying and opening.

I have enough merits to buy two packs from the shop. A gladius pack is 2,000 merits per pack and I have 5k+ merits to buy two packs.


<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYguZMypE4vDdc7FxSXSZj4X24u2M2ks9NGw86Ma3Vqeo/image.png)</center>

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbHKa4UUGRqXNYoYmAR9BRitYwSHD1gN4pwRqE1pHW468/image.png)</center>

I opened the packs one at a time. The first pack contained the cards below.

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbN2jxiseYv2xRHtqZokdVNSjmKAqR9SGASbp7pMJ6TB8/image.png)</center>

The first pack contained a gold card Helmet Kharafax. It costs two mana but it has no attack whatsoever. I'll consider burning it to get merits because I don't see this card being used in battles.

This batch also had a rare Fire card. It's also a two mana card but this is so much better. It has two attack, two health and three speed. It has sneak ability so it does not have to take the front line in order to attack. 

The rest of the packs were common cards. 

Next pack had the following units below.

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbTNc9GsTEKuN985Vd9vsNEC4k9sZGoCR6z18QZiHWTwF/image.png)</center>

This batch has three rare cards and one gold. I had the same two mana rare card from the first batch. The other two are a three mana range and a seven mana front line card. The gold card is much more useful this time. It's a three mana card with two range attack. This batch is much more better than the first. 

I forgot to check my cards inventory. I already have cards that are for upgrade. I'll raise their levels today.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaTJRGmWzPdhkvAFsQ7uj49KjTBoghERNUA98zZx6ycMi/image.png)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbHKa4UUGRqXNYoYmAR9BRitYwSHD1gN4pwRqE1pHW468/image.png)

Thanks to mhowii for the free blog dividers he shared in his post.

For players looking for games in Hive, I invite you to play the following games. They can be played for free in the links.

Splinterlands https://splinterlands.com/

Next to Splinterlands, I also play Dungeon Cities daily. It's a text based dungeon crawler game similar to Diablo. Come to the city of Aldoria and start your quest in the following links.

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV4soRrRSBHKxC9Bo2e1GrsbQjvhTxtznYwECQYsfZN8Z/image.png)</center>

body.title: The Silent Voice In My Head Asked
body.body:
![[Image source by Sayan Ghosh on Unsplash](https://unsplash.com)

We are all living, and we are all going to die. Where do we go when we leave this place called Earth?
‎
‎From everything I know, I feel we don't just disappear; we transform, taking on a new body and continuing from where we left off. This is what we call reincarnation.
‎
‎ But then, what happens if your past enemy becomes your current sibling? Or your parent?
‎
‎If reincarnation is true, could this be the exact reason why some siblings can't see eye-to-eye as kids, even when they have no logical reason for the friction?
‎
‎I just feel there is so much more to life than what we see on the surface. Some things simply cannot be explained.
‎
‎Remember, this is just a voice in my head, and I'm simply thinking out loud. What do you think? Do you sometimes wonder where our loved ones go after they leave this Earth? 
‎
‎Let me read your thoughts in the comments section!

body.title: Backrooms | Movie Review [ENG-ESP]
body.body:
![lladsd.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmee1Jgkzobco8ScgEpJRkgLSJcSoiSjLqfqR2nqouCZ6K/lladsd.jpg) [Source](https://www.filmaffinity.com/es/filmimages.php?movie_id=789723) As the years go by, new horror stories emerge, and at the same time, many may turn out to be true or false—just like the Backrooms, a phenomenon that has been mentioned in countless online stories, YouTube channels, and other platforms. It consists of a simple image: endless yellow corridors. That’s why the time has come to adapt it, and the film known as *Backrooms* is set to premiere. It has generated a lot of buzz for being that combination of horror and science fiction, leading us to wonder: what would happen if you ended up trapped in a place where everything is yellow? This is a movie for those who enjoy this horror genre and that mind game, as it draws heavily on those internet references and builds a horror experience based on the sensation of disorientation. Furthermore, from the very first minute, everything here is the same—the same place, all yellow—and it becomes familiar, but over time, you can start to notice shifts in mood and fear. >A medida que los años van avanzando nuevas historias de terror nacen y a la vez muchas pueden llegar a ser de verdad o de mentira, tal como lo son los Backrooms algo que se ha mencionado en muchas historias de internet, canales de YouTube y en muchos otros espacios, la cual es una imagen simple, pasillos amarillos interminables y por eso llego el momento de adaptarla y que se estrenará la película conocida como Backrooms, donde ha dado mucho de que hablar por ser esa combinación de terror con ciencia ficción y nos lleva a preguntarnos ¿qué pasaría si terminarás atrapado en un lugar donde todo es amarillo? # >Esta es una película para los que le gusta este género de terror y ese juego mental, ya que toma gran parte de esas referencia del internet y construye una experiencia de terror basada en la sensación de desorientación. Además, desde el primer minuto, todo aquí es igual, un mismo lugar, todo amarillo y se convierte en algo conocido, pero que con el tiempo ya se pueden notar cambios de aptitud y de miedo. ![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeTpSTLQq2Ackh4yoAFYXFYN2rrk4dnGpth37TVgE2LTg/image.png) [Source](https://www.filmaffinity.com/es/filmimages.php?movie_id=789723) It had been a long time since I’d heard this, and seeing how movies today draw inspiration from the classics is truly admirable. One of the things that really adds value beyond the scares is the silence of the empty hallways and the feeling that the rules of the world have stopped working. Plus, everything seems to connect in impossible ways, creating a labyrinth that defies all logic. Each scene, despite being almost identical, conveys fear and that mix of nostalgia and anxiety that comes from being trapped in a confined space—the most agonizing feeling there is in this life. It also makes perfect use of artificial lighting and empty spaces to generate a constant sense of unease, which is why every second of the film feels more real, and as a viewer, you remain attentive to each of the mysteries surrounding this universe and the constant uncertainty about what is really happening. >Tenía mucho tiempo que no escuchaba esto y ver cómo hoy en día las películas toman referencia de cosas buenas es de admirar y una de las cosas que realmente le aporta valor más allá del susto, es ese silencio de los pasillos vacíos y de la sensación de que las reglas del mundo han dejado de funcionar, además todo parece conectarse con otra de manera imposible, creando un laberinto que desafía toda lógica. # >Cada una de las escenas a pesar de ser casi iguales transmiten miedo y esa mezcla de nostalgia y ansiedad al estar en lugar encerrado, siendo lo más desesperante que existe en esta vida. Como también aprovecha perfectamente la iluminación artificial y los espacios vacíos para generar una incomodidad constante, por eso cada segundo de la película se vuelve más real y uno como espectador sigue atento a cada uno de los misterios que rodean este universo y a la incertidumbre permanente sobre lo que realmente está ocurriendo. ![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfG5HXSFjosN1EJYpQU39cpcDFLHhtnLQAS8ggnrUJwuu/image.png) [Source](https://www.filmaffinity.com/es/filmimages.php?movie_id=789723) I really liked the result and this adaptation of *Backrooms*, as it offers a different take from other films in this genre and shows that you don’t always need to show too much—often, what we don’t see is far more unsettling. Plus, there’s no action here, but there is a disturbing experience that surely no one would be prepared for. So if you’re looking for something different, this is for you—and to realize that sometimes the scariest place isn’t where something is chasing you, but where it seems like you’ll never be able to find the way out. >Me gusto mucho el resultado y esta adaptación de Backrooms, ya que es una propuesta diferente del resto de las películas de este género y es una muestra de que no siempre se necesita mostrar demasiado, puesto que muchas veces, lo que no vemos resulta mucho más inquietante. Además, aquí no habrá acción, pero sí una experiencia inquietante que seguramente nadie estaría preparado para eso. Por eso si buscas algo distinto esta es para ti y darte cuenta de que a veces el lugar más aterrador no es donde hay algo persiguiéndote, sino donde parece que nunca podrás encontrar la salida.
![pngwing.com 3.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPvWeswjaMnCtt69QxnpZHm1una1iw2HUxZJpGBgEY2RH/pngwing.com%203.png)
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmb1YQAsu4GB81sVj4eS7YynfmSoXYhjpF5CvEkReLPj1r/image.png)

Buenas noches mi estimados y apreciados seguidores, hoy toco 10km a ritmo a ver como me iba y ya les cuento todooo.

Como saben me he dedicado a fortaleces y a correr poco, solo corro lo necesario para mantener el mínimo común múltiplo, así que hoy hice una pequeña pruebita a ver si podía correr 10 km a 5:00 minutos... es decir, a tempo jijiji..😈😈😈

Aproveche que hoy había una carrera planifica de 10 km por todo el este de Caracas, un ruta nueva y muy diferente a lo habitual, como he dicho antes, las carreras en Caracas son repetitivas, las rutas son las mismas y es un poco aburrido.

Los organizadores no se arriesgan a crear algo nuevo, una ruta diferente, un nuevo reto y hoy Dios me escucho y corrí algo un poco diferente y muy divertida, con sus respectivas cuestas en los primeros kilómetros y recorriendo lugares muy emblemáticos de Caracas que usualmente no se pueden utilizar para realizar estas actividades. 🦖🦖🦖🦖

Por ejemplo, pasamos corriendo por frente de la Asamblea Nacional y por al lado de la Plaza Bolivar, bajamos por la avenida Urdaneta y pasamos frente la Plaza Urdaneta, subimos por el elevado y vi desde un punto de vista diferente al Sambil de la Candelaria. 
Realmente estuvo muy genial la ruta, y los puntos de animación fueron todo un vacilón, un bochinche constante, alrededor del kilómetro 4 había 4 autobuses parados y unos animadores disfrazados de choferes y recolectores, fue un toque muy muy Caraqueño, creo que me sentí super en casa.🏃🏾‍➡️🏃🏾‍➡️🏃🏾‍➡️🏃🏾‍➡️🏃🏾‍➡️

Realmente siempre he escuchado que Caracas es Caracas y lo demás es monte y culebra, bueno creo que hoy viví en carne propia el significado de ese decir XD.🌇🌇🌇🌇🌇

Creo que hoy la organización se gano 100 puntos de 10 en esta carrera, quede enamorado, el próximo año la quiero volver a correrla. 

En cuanto al tiempo de hoy, si me fue super bien, me mantuve en 5:00 cada kilometro y llegue genia, todavia tengo el toque jejeje


---

I see different types of beauty in the environment around me and I really like to enjoy these beauties. Among the different types of beauty, the beauty of any insect is one of the beauties. Today I am sharing an insect from the natural environment that I have seen with my own eyes and I like it. This beautiful insect has different names and one of them is Melanoplinae Insect. It is actually a type of grasshopper and I know it best by this name. However, I saw an exception in the color of this grasshopper. Because I liked it, I took a few pictures with my own mobile.





I went to visit a place a few days ago and it is located about six kilometers away from my village home. I saw this insect sitting on a tree leaf there and I liked it very much. I observed this insect and saw that its body had a combination of black and brown colors which made the insect look very beautiful while sitting on the tree leaf. This type of insect is mostly seen sitting on the leaves of various types of weeds around the house or on the leaves of various crops in the field. I am now sharing some pictures of this insect with the Hive community friends. I hope all friends will like the pictures of this insect. I wish all friends well.

![20260614_090842-490f0b0d2b51.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/jazminapaza/lkt-mqef8xa5-10jjz9s1/20260614_090842-490f0b0d2b51.webp)

Hoy paso por aquí a contarles un poco de mi domingo. Nos fuimos directico a Los Caobos porque hoy se corría la primera edición de la carrera de San Simón. Les confieso que estuve a punto de inscribirme formalmente, pero me contuve... Igualmente nos animamos a irnos por fuera y hacer el recorrido completo de la carrera.

Todo el team se reunió tempranito en el parque para la clásica foto previa y, a las 7:00 am en punto empezó la carrera. Quería probar irme pegada con los pacers de 55 minutos. Pero esos señores salieron volando🤣 Me dejaron botada desde el inicio jajaja. Aunque siempre los veía a lo lejos, no llegué a alcanzarlos, además que, tampoco quería forzarlo y fundirme antes de tiempo… La ruta era totalmente nueva, pasaba por varios sitios emblemáticos del centro de nuestra querida ciudad y tenía varias subiditas traicioneras, por lo cual, tocó administrar bien la energía.

La vibra de la gente fue única. Durante toda la ruta lo que más se escuchaba era salsa, joropo y tambores a todo lo que da. Los puntos de animación estuvieron increíbles, supercreativos y haciendo demasiada referencia a la vida cotidiana del caraqueño. Fue una experiencia totalmente diferente y divertidísima.

Al final, logré muchísimo más de lo que esperaba e hice un tiempo de 56 minutos. Pero no les voy a mentir, en los últimos kilómetros ya estaba viendo estrellitas🙈 Pero me dejó una satisfacción enorme y la certeza de que, metiéndole más duro a los entrenamientos de resistencia, voy a bajar ese tiempo en mi próxima carrera inscrita.

El próximo año me inscribo de primera, sin dudarlo. Además, tengo que hablar de la medalla de este año: Una belleza😍 A mi lado \
le fascinó el diseño porque salían las emblemáticas Torres de Parque Central.
body.author: jazminapaza

body.body:
This mystery of the spider, sometimes appearing alone and at other times accompanied, you’ll have to reveal to me one day. 😁
As for this exhibition, I get the feeling that everything is unfinished, yet at the same time it’s clear that hard work went into it, which in fact doesn’t matter, effort is not directly proportional to the result. 
I listened to the author, who spoke of a love–hate relationship with the material chosen to present his art, and I think that in all this discourse—about nakedness, masks, what we decide to be through conditioning rather than what we feel… in being itself—I also perceive a love–hate relationship 😂. But what new thing could I possibly add, when you’ve already made it clear with your reflections? Structure, time and conflict, and the mass takes on its ‘more or less’ definitive or balanced form… or neither. Hence L’anima non finita. 😃

I know what I mean… 😂

  
A hug, a great post, and thank you for sharing Lidó Rico’s work.

body.title: 大面积停水
body.body:
![1-63d112e2cda5.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/huigezi/lkt-mqefzm6l-q72kk45k/1-63d112e2cda5.webp)

![2-a2156e023f0d.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/huigezi/lkt-mqefzm6l-q72kk45k/2-a2156e023f0d.webp)

![3-6b76eb7534d9.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/huigezi/lkt-mqefzm6l-q72kk45k/3-6b76eb7534d9.webp)

![4-458e5347ae39.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/huigezi/lkt-mqefzm6l-q72kk45k/4-458e5347ae39.webp)

哎呀，起了个大早。

准备给我的痴呆母后改善一下生活，我准备了海带，豆腐，鸡蛋，白菜，粉条，豆腐丝，还有西红柿，反正 就是全品类的健康菜品，买得准备早晨起来做饭，给我的痴呆母后改善改善伙食，结果呢，停水了厨房，厕所，全部停水了，又去问了邻居，也是停水，看来不是咱们自己家停水，怎么办呢，只好把准备的食材都放进了冰箱，明天再说吧

我问母后，咋办呢，停水了，只能去镇里吃饭，她说去喝胡辣汤吧，我说好得，于是就开车带母后去镇上吃饭，结果呢镇上也停水了，看来是大面积停水呢，怎么办呢，走了几个早餐店，都没有开门营业，估计也是因为停水的缘故。


于是走走停停，走了很几个早餐都没有开门，在不抱希望的时候，走到了一个包子铺，包子铺竟然营业，竟然也有早餐和胡辣汤，下车，安顿好母后，吃饭吧，本来不准备买包子吃了，可是都不营业，这个包子铺的生意也异常火爆，所以还是吃点吧，一会连包子也没有吃了

吃过饭，安顿好母后，我就开始来店铺了，打开电脑，更新今天的心情，准备等会运动个十分钟，健身，无时无刻，附近开的24小时共享健身房，我挺喜欢的，很多客户也表示很不错，去体验一把，24小时营业，真的很棒，喜欢，力捧，支持，打造，捧红。

每个没有努力的日子，都是对自己的生命的辜负，所以更新后今天的文章，就开始运动吧，生命在于运动，高血糖，高血脂，都通通的给我滚远点，即今天的我也会更好。

我是美美哒，我的心情也是美美哒，并没有因为大面积停水，而影响自己，内耗自己，加油，周一。

body.title: Bitcoin ETFs Snap Outflow Streak as Geopolitical Easing Sparks Risk-On Rally — Crypto Market Report June 14, 2026
body.body:
![header](https://ipfs.io/ipfs/QmYz8466msWEGUctZiPfYqtYqGeK3TUM9BCq9w24XbFTd8)

The crypto market woke up to a noticeably different mood on June 14th. After weeks of red ink and institutional flight, Bitcoin ETFs posted their first meaningful inflows in days — $85.9 million on June 12 alone — while geopolitical tensions between the U.S. and Iran cooled, triggering a broad risk-on shift across global markets. Together, these developments are giving digital assets their first real breath of fresh air since early June's selloff.

## The ETF Reversal: What $85.9 Million Tells Us

The headline number is straightforward but significant: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $85.9 million in net inflows on June 12, snapping a five- to seven-day outflow streak that had weighed heavily on sentiment. BlackRock's IBIT led the charge with $57.7 million, while Fidelity captured roughly $18 million. The aggregate net asset value of the spot ETF ecosystem now sits at approximately $79.65 billion, representing about 6.26% of Bitcoin's total market capitalization.

This reversal matters for three reasons. First, it signals that institutional investors — who drove a staggering 13-day outflow streak totaling $4.37 billion between mid-May and early June — are pausing their exit. Second, it coincides with a broader macro shift: the SEC's recent approval of the Grayscale Digital Large Cap Fund, which bundles Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Cardano, and XRP into a single multi-asset wrapper. Bitwise projects more than 100 new crypto ETFs could launch in the U.S. during 2026 as regulatory clarity accelerates. Third, it comes at a technical inflection point — Bitcoin's 14-day RSI sits at 34.84, deep in oversold territory and near its lowest reading since November 2018.

## Bitcoin Holds $64K Amid Geopolitical Thaw

Bitcoin is currently trading around $64,021 — essentially flat on the day but up roughly 3.35% over the past week. The key catalyst for this stabilization emerged on June 13, when President Trump announced the cancellation of planned Iran strikes and progress toward a potential peace deal. The geopolitical de-escalation triggered a classic risk-on rotation: investors who had fled to safe-haven assets during the tension spike are now rotating back into riskier positions, including cryptocurrencies.

Before this geopolitical pivot, Bitcoin had endured a brutal correction from early-2026 highs near $82,969 down to lows around $59,000. The selloff was driven by a confluence of headwinds: the Federal Reserve's hawkish stance and persistent inflation (the highest since 2023), record ETF outflows, escalating Iran tensions that fueled inflation fears, and even a small but symbolic 32-BTC sale by Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) — the company's first Bitcoin sale since 2022.

Today, Bitcoin remains well below its key moving averages — the 20-day SMA at $67,496, the 50-day SMA at $74,153, and the 200-day SMA at $77,770 — confirming that the broader trend remains bearish. At roughly 49% below its all-time high of $126,080, the market is still in correction mode. But the combination of oversold technicals, ETF inflow reversal, and geopolitical easing suggests the worst of the immediate pain may be behind us.

## Ethereum and Solana: The Real Outperformers of 2026

While Bitcoin consolidates, Ethereum and Solana are telling a different story — one of relative strength that has defined much of 2026.

Ethereum is trading at approximately $1,674, up 3.94% on the week and an impressive 43.59% year-to-date — making it the standout major asset on a YTD basis. Ethereum's outperformance reflects growing confidence in its ecosystem: staking yields remain attractive, Layer 2 adoption continues to accelerate, and the Grayscale Digital Large Cap Fund's inclusion of ETH provides another institutional on-ramp.

Solana is even more impressive, trading at $68.08 with a 4.97% weekly gain and a staggering 45.30% YTD return — narrowly edging out Ethereum for the best year-to-date performance among major cryptocurrencies. Solana's momentum is fueled by its thriving DeFi ecosystem, growing NFT activity (including a recent wave of World Cup-themed meme coins that drew 650x Ethereum's trading volume in May), and increasing institutional attention.

BNB ($610, +3.56% weekly) and XRP ($1.14, +0.98% weekly) are also posting modest gains, though their YTD performance remains negative at -29.36% and -37.85% respectively.

## The Bigger Picture: What's Next?

The market today is at a crossroads. On the bullish side, we have ETF inflow reversal, geopolitical de-escalation, oversold technicals, and strong altcoin momentum. On the bearish side, Bitcoin remains well below its moving averages, the Fed's hawkish stance persists, and Galaxy Digital's Alex Thorn has suggested the cycle low might not arrive until Q4 2026, with prices potentially dipping to $40,000–$46,000.

The mining difficulty drop of approximately 11% is another data point worth watching — it makes mining more profitable for remaining operators and can influence network stability, though its near-term price impact is typically muted.

For now, the $64,000 level is being actively tested as support. A sustained break above the 20-day EMA at $66,806 would be the first technical confirmation of a meaningful reversal. Until then, the market is in a cautious consolidation phase — but the ingredients for a recovery are finally aligning.

**Bottom line:** The crypto market is showing its first signs of life in weeks. ETF flows have turned, geopolitical risk has eased, and altcoins are leading the charge. Whether this marks a genuine bottom or just a dead-cat bounce remains to be seen — but for the first time in a long while, there's reason to pay attention.

description.body:
*** *** #
If you prefer the English version, click on the following link 👉 [**HERE**](#english)
*** ***

# ***
***

> En casi todas las casas del mundo existe un territorio sagrado y olvidado a la vez: el cajón de las cosas que no sirven para nada, pero que no se pueden tirar. Es un ecosistema de cables cuya entrada ya no encaja en ningún dispositivo moderno, pilas de dudosa vitalidad, llaves de cerraduras que ya no existen y bolsas de plástico que contienen otras bolsas de plástico. A simple vista, es desorden. Pero si nos sentamos un momento frente a ese caos, en silencio, descubriremos que no es basura; es un archivo biológico y transgeneracional.
# ***
Aprendiendo a soltar el pasado
*** Somos, en gran medida, los guardianes de los miedos de quienes vinieron antes que nosotros. Ese impulso de cerrar la mano sobre un objeto inservible \

no nace de nuestra lógica contemporánea de la abundancia, sino de una huella antigua. Como bien señaló el psiquiatra **Carl Jung** en su obra *Arquetipos e inconsciente colectivo*: *“Hasta que lo inconsciente no se haga consciente, el subconsciente dirigirá tu vida y tú lo llamarás destino”*. Ese destino, en muchas familias, tiene forma de precaución excesiva. Guardamos porque nuestros abuelos conocieron el hambre, porque nuestros padres vivieron la incertidumbre, porque en algún punto del árbol genealógico, no tener un repuesto significó una tragedia real.

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmavr2JrH8a97vjPtTcJmh5qZS5QxV48UQ6tgLxVnEHsUs/h1.png)
<sup>[](https://gemini.google.com/app)</sup>
</center>

Llevamos en la sangre una \

que se hereda como el color de los ojos. No es solo un objeto lo que hay en el cajón; es una oración para conjurar el miedo al futuro. Creemos que al controlar esos pequeños recursos —una vela de hace no sé, cuántas navidades, un frasco vacío— estamos comprando una póliza de seguro contra lo impredecible. Es lo que el escritor **William Faulkner** describía con maestría en *Réquiem por una monja*: *“El pasado nunca muere. Ni siquiera es pasado”*. El pasado está ahí, enredado en ese cable USB tipo A que te niegas a desechar, recordándote que la carencia siempre es una posibilidad.\n\nSin embargo, hay un segundo nivel en esta acumulación: la identidad. A veces, soltar un objeto se siente como una pequeña muerte. Esa camiseta vieja que ya no te queda, pero que usaste el día que te sentiste invencible por primera vez, no es tela; es un fragmento de tu \
que se resiste a desaparecer. Al conservarla, intentamos detener el tiempo. El filósofo y sociólogo **Zygmunt Bauman**, al hablar de la \

, advertía sobre nuestra fragilidad ante lo efímero. Guardar cosas es nuestro intento de construir una balsa sólida en un mundo donde todo se desvanece.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXm9ffKcdQzcjBL735gU7xqWpv1jztvjrPsV4WoWEpYG1/h2.png) [](https://gemini.google.com/app)
Reconocer lo particularmente únicos que somos requiere, irónicamente, identificar qué partes de nosotros no nos pertenecen. ¿Ese miedo a la pérdida es tuyo o es una herencia de tu madre? ¿Esa necesidad de tenerlo todo bajo control es una virtud o un mecanismo de defensa contra una ansiedad que no has nombrado? La meditación es el inicio de la liberación. Sentarse a observar el objeto sin juzgarlo. Mirar la mano que lo sostiene y preguntarse: *¿A quién estoy protegiendo al guardar esto?* La monja budista **Pema Chödrön** dice en sus enseñanzas sobre el desapego: *“El desapego no es que no poseas nada, sino que nada te posea a ti”*. Cuando entendemos que nuestra seguridad no reside en el contenido de un cajón, sino en nuestra capacidad de habitar el presente, el peso de las generaciones anteriores empieza a aligerarse.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmacS6dh3vi1fwL8S7zqZLMFNmm6D5vqPJRLEyEMMAQrbQ/h3.png) [](https://gemini.google.com/app)
Ser únicos no significa nacer de la nada; significa ser el resultado de mil historias, pero tener la valentía de editar el guion. Somos seres singulares porque podemos elegir qué legados honrar y cuáles dejar ir. Al final del día, la verdadera madurez consiste en darnos cuenta de que, como escribió **Séneca** en sus *Cartas a Lucilio*: *“No es que tengamos poco tiempo, sino que perdemos mucho”*. Perder el tiempo —y el espacio vital— protegiendo fantasmas del pasado nos impide caminar ligeros. La próxima vez que abras ese cajón y tu mano se detenga antes de tirar un objeto inútil, no te sientas culpable... sonríe, pues, estás ante un portal a tu historia. Obsérvalo, agradécele la seguridad que intentó darte y, si ya no sirve para tu vida de hoy, déjalo ir. Solo cuando vaciamos los cajones de lo que ya no somos, dejamos espacio para que aparezca lo que verdaderamente podemos llegar a ser. ¡Suelta el pasado!
> *** ***

*** *** ##
Dedicado a todos aquellos que, día a día, hacen del mundo un lugar mejor.
*** ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcnceTgTBLgAUkErZfdoePC7twytC1CTcqQYDKkU4Lrrd/1024espa_ol8.gif) ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbdpsZFqtrcoLk94sUV8oHkjnx8PAdgfACMfJ9UpcriNF/perfil2026_hecho_con_clipchamp_2_.gif) ***

*** *** *** br>

>

# ***
***

> In almost every home in the world, there is a space that is both sacred and forgotten: the drawer full of things that serve no purpose, yet cannot be thrown away. It is an ecosystem of cables whose plugs no longer fit any modern device, piles of batteries of dubious viability, keys for locks that no longer exist, and plastic bags containing other plastic bags. At first glance, it is a mess. But if we sit for a moment in front of that chaos, in silence, we will discover that it is not rubbish; it is a biological and transgenerational archive.
# ***
Learning to let go of the past
*** We are, to a large extent, the guardians of the fears of those who came before us. That impulse to clench our hand around a useless object ‘just in case’ does not stem from our contemporary logic of abundance, but from an ancient imprint. As the psychiatrist **Carl Jung** rightly pointed out in his work *Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious*: *“Until the unconscious becomes conscious, the subconscious will direct your life and you will call it fate”*. That fate, in many families, takes the form of excessive caution. We hoard because our grandparents knew hunger, because our parents lived through uncertainty, because at some point in the family tree, not having a spare meant a real tragedy.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmavr2JrH8a97vjPtTcJmh5qZS5QxV48UQ6tgLxVnEHsUs/h1.png) [](https://gemini.google.com/app)
We carry a ‘scarcity mindset’ in our blood, inherited just like the colour of our eyes. It is not just an object in the drawer; it is a prayer to ward off fear of the future. We believe that by hoarding these small resources—a candle from who knows how many Christmases ago, an empty jar—we are buying an insurance policy against the unpredictable. It is what the writer **William Faulkner** so masterfully described in *Requiem for a Nun*: *“The past is never dead. It’s not even past.”* The past is there, tangled up in that USB Type-A cable you refuse to throw away, reminding you that scarcity is always a possibility. However, there is a second layer to this accumulation: identity. Sometimes, letting go of an object feels like a small death. That old T-shirt that no longer fits you, but which you wore the day you felt invincible for the first time, is not just fabric; it is a fragment of your ‘self’ that refuses to disappear. By keeping it, we try to stop time. The philosopher and sociologist **Zygmunt Bauman**, when speaking of “liquid modernity”, warned of our fragility in the face of the ephemeral. Hoarding things is our attempt to build a solid raft in a world where everything fades away.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXm9ffKcdQzcjBL735gU7xqWpv1jztvjrPsV4WoWEpYG1/h2.png) [](https://gemini.google.com/app)
Recognising just how uniquely special we are requires, ironically, identifying which parts of us do not truly belong to us. Is that fear of loss yours, or is it something you’ve inherited from your mother? Is that need to have everything under control a virtue, or a defence mechanism against anxiety you haven’t yet acknowledged? Meditation is the beginning of liberation. Sitting to observe the object without judging it. Looking at the hand that holds it and asking yourself: *Who am I protecting by keeping this?* The Buddhist nun **Pema Chödrön** says in her teachings on detachment: *“Detachment is not that you possess nothing, but that nothing possesses you”*. When we understand that our security does not lie in the contents of a drawer, but in our ability to inhabit the present, the weight of previous generations begins to lighten.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmacS6dh3vi1fwL8S7zqZLMFNmm6D5vqPJRLEyEMMAQrbQ/h3.png) [](https://gemini.google.com/app)
Being unique does not mean being born from nothing; it means being the result of a thousand stories, but having the courage to edit the script. We are unique beings because we can choose which legacies to honour and which to let go of. At the end of the day, true maturity lies in realising that, as **Seneca** wrote in his *Letters to Lucilius*: *“It is not that we have little time, but that we waste so much of it”*. Wasting time — and living space — protecting ghosts of the past prevents us from walking lightly. The next time you open that drawer and your hand pauses before throwing away a useless object, don’t feel guilty… smile, for you are standing before a gateway to your history. Look at it, thank it for the security it tried to give you, and, if it no longer serves you in your life today, let it go. Only when we clear our drawers of what we no longer are do we make room for what we can truly become. Let go of the past!

>

description.body:
___
___

<center>![1000557264.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/janitzearratia/23xeUjpfQ9v5XzNhtgAPFqszohay1WX9UzHqnNFNmMLewDrB3pGpjv8Ld4AtH9LkEVJmA.jpg)</center>
___
___

<div class=\

>

\n

>

There is a question that we rarely ask ourselves as parents and that is: what am I teaching my child when he makes a mistake? Not with the words, but with the face you put on, with the tone you use when something didn't go as you expected, with your attitude to what happened. Because children don't learn to relate to failure by listening to what we tell them. They learn it by observing how we react when things go wrong. In fact, there are adults who today *procrastinate*, who abandon any project, activity, task, before trying something, who are terribly afraid of looking bad, and when one goes to the bottom of that, there almost always appears a child who learned very early that the mistake was not just a mistake. It was disappointing someone he loved, and the consequence of that was to be left without his love. I talked about that emptiness that is charged when you grow up with an absent father or mother, and what a person, decides to do with that, throughout his life. Look, there are those who live looking outside, in other people, for that figure that they lacked. And there are those who at some point understand that true security is built inside. Sometimes certain sufferings make things that had become normal transparent to us... and strange as it may sound... they even make us regain our sanity, whether out of curiosity, out of the need to understand everything, our ability to walk alone through the world, and build from there a version that stands on its own. My reflection is that there are absences that can break a person. And there are people who are built, precisely, from that absence, because it is a way of standing up to life, even in the face of the uncertainty that absence leaves us, and there are also people who learned to know their value only through the eyes of others. Because when someone grows up in a system where love and approval came conditioned to performance, where others decided if what you did was enough or not, the result is almost always the same: an adult who knows how to demand himself but does not know how to love himself, who knows how to find his flaws but not his achievements, who looks for confirmation in others that he never learned to give himself alone. However, that inability to love each other without intermediaries, is exactly what we see on a daily basis. Because the thing is, maybe no one taught us to be our own point of reference. And that learning, even if it comes late, completely changes the relationship we have with ourselves and even with others. Do you know why? Well, because we are our convictions, values, bonds, stories and what gives meaning to our life. In the end, life is not measured by the things we accumulate, but by the memories we build. An object can be kept safe in a box, but an experience can stay living in the soul, because things wear out, but memories have the ability to accompany us forever. Janitze.🌷

description.title: 14 June 2026, Freewriters Community Daily Writing Prompt Day 3134: what’s in that chest?
description.body: alt=\

/>

“OK … that wasn't expected.”

A tree in the Trent yard had hung on through two hurricanes swirling their fringes over Lofton County, VA, only to quietly give up on life overnight some weeks later, there being a hollow place in its root ball that caused it to be progressively unstable on one side.

The cause of the hollow place came up with the tree, thereby causing Sgt. Vincent Trent's comment.

“Oh, my, it's a real treasure chest!” eleven-year-old Velma Trent said.

“Yes, Milton, you can come off being grounded to go see,” Mrs. Melissa Trent said, and nine-year-old Milton went along with eight-year-old Gracie and their first cousins Tom (16) and Vertran Stepforth (9).

“That's a big chest, too,” Milton said.

“Ain't it the truth – I think all four of us under ten could get in there, and maybe we could smush Tom in, too,” Gracie said.

“I hope somebody didn't already have that idea!” Milton said. “That thing is big enough to hold Dracula, too!”

“Get your camera ready, Vertran: this is probably news,” Tom said as he pulled out his phone to alert his editors at the _Lofton County Free Voice._ “Pop-Pop is always saying history in Lofton County is never as far away from you as you think.”

“Yeah – I mean, Dracula being in there is gotta be news, but we need to sharpen some pencils just in case,” Milton said.

“Wait, what, why?” Velma said.

“Come on, Velma,” Milton said. “You know you gotta have wooden stakes and stuff – and hey, Mom, can I have a couple of cloves of garlic?”

“But it just could be treasure, and instead of marking the spot with a X, they put a tree on it,” Gracie said.

“The tree has some age on it,” Sgt. Trent said. “The chest must be even older, so there's history in there, and – .”

“MILTOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOON!”

Nine-year-old George Ludlow from next door did not care about the chest; all he saw was his best friend back outside, and came running down the street to wrap Milton up with a hug.

“And to him, that's what's in the chest: the treasure of getting his best friend back,” Mrs. Maggie Lee said to her husband, George's big cousin Col. H.F. Lee, as they looked out the window at the scene from next door.

“He is the only one,” the colonel remarked, “who is not going to be disappointed, no matter what happens. Given the history of Tinyville, though, I'm sure whatever is in that chest is probably going to be interesting.”

“Any chance of gold coins and such?” Mrs. Lee said.

“Very little,” Col. Lee said, “but, given the age of Tinyville, and also of Lofton County, there could be something in there worth at least a small fortune … or a small fortune some family would be willing to pay to have buried again along with all those who have knowledge of it. Sgt. Trent is doing well to be calling Ironwood Hamilton in his role of police captain in Tinyville: let all things be officially noted. ”

“Is it that serious?” Mrs. Lee said.

“It is,” Col. Lee said. “Lofton County still has some deep, deep secrets … a chest buried deliberately under a tree means someone could not let the truth be heard at a particular time, but they did want it out at some point.”

By this time, the rest of the little Ludlows were streaming down the street, the ask coming from many of their lips: “What's in that chest?”

“It's gonna be a little while because the tree is big and the rootball is tight, so, y'all get some lemonade and go play while we let Capt. Hamilton and some professionals get this all untangled,” Mrs. Trent said as she brought out enough cups for all little children. “We'll call you when it is time to open the chest.”

body.title: MedGemma and the open source medical AI movement
body.body:
In May 2025, Google released MedGemma through the Health AI Developer Foundations (HAI-DEF) program — making available an open weight medical language model that healthcare teams can run on their own infrastructure, fine-tune on their own data, and audit completely. The launch signals a strategic shift: medical AI no longer has to be the exclusive property of large platforms. Hospitals, universities and health startups can build on a solid base without depending on external APIs.

MedGemma: architecture and capabilities
---------------------------------------

MedGemma is built on the Gemma 3 architecture and comes in three variants:

**4B multimodal:** Processes images and text simultaneously. Suited for medical image classification (X-ray, dermatology, ophthalmology), answering questions about clinical images, and initial triage.

**27B text-only:** A pure language model focused on clinical reasoning, medical literature review, answering structured clinical questions, and text-based decision support. It scored 87.7% on MedQA — within the range of much larger models.

**27B multimodal:** Combines clinical reasoning in text with image processing and longitudinal reasoning over electronic health records (EHR). The most complete variant for hospital systems.

The model can be run on-premise — on Google Cloud Platform, on the institution's own servers, or on high-performance local hardware. This resolves the main adoption obstacle for hospitals with data regulated by LGPD, HIPAA or GDPR: patient data does not need to leave the institution's infrastructure.

MedSigLIP: the vision component
-------------------------------

Alongside MedGemma, Google released MedSigLIP — a 400-million-parameter vision-language model specialized in medical images. MedSigLIP can be used independently for medical image classification without the overhead of the full MedGemma. For hospitals that only need X-ray or dermatoscopy analysis, without full text generation, it is the lowest-compute-cost option.

OpenBioLLM: the open source competitor
--------------------------------------

OpenBioLLM-70B from Saama AI Research is the most robust alternative to MedGemma in the open source space. Based on the Llama 3 architecture, it scores 74% on MedQA USMLE, 75% on PubMedQA and 80.85% on complex clinical cases. It runs on a single A100 GPU. The 8B-parameter model is an option for environments with more limited hardware.

OpenBioLLM's differentiator is its specialization in biomedical literature: it was extensively trained on PubMed, PMC and international medical guidelines. For scientific literature retrieval and article summarization, it surpasses general models of similar capacity.

Meditron3: for low-resource contexts
------------------------------------

Meditron, developed by EPFL in partnership with Yale Medicine and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), was designed for a specific use case: healthcare in resource-limited contexts. The third version (Meditron3), based on Llama 3, was released in 2025 and outperforms all open source models of equivalent size on MedQA and MedMCQA.

Its differentiator is not the top benchmark — MedGemma 27B is clearly superior in absolute capability. The differentiator is size: Meditron3 runs on hardware that exists in hospitals in low- and middle-income countries, and it was trained to include WHO guidelines and international protocols relevant to contexts where access to specialists is limited.

The counterintuitive finding: fine-tuning doesn't always win
------------------------------------------------------------

An important research finding from 2025 (arXiv:2408.13833) questions the basic premise of specialized medical models: fine-tuned biomedical models **do not consistently outperform general frontier models on medical data not seen during training**.

The reason is that models like GPT-5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, trained on massive volumes of text, processed enormous amounts of medical literature — potentially more than any specialized medical fine-tune. On known benchmarks, the fine-tune wins because the benchmark data leaked into training. On genuinely new data, the gap narrows.

This does not invalidate MedGemma or OpenBioLLM. Open source models have advantages that go beyond the benchmark score: they run on-premise (privacy), are fine-tunable on proprietary data (vertical specialization), cost far less at scale (own infrastructure), and can be fully audited (regulatory compliance).

For a hospital institution that needs to process 10 million records per year on HIPAA-compliant infrastructure, MedGemma 27B at zero API cost is a radically different proposition from GPT-5 at US$ 5.00/M tokens. Even if GPT-5 is slightly superior in quality, the economic and regulatory argument may be decisive.

body.body:
<liketuimages>
<center>
![TXlaLwI0w7ezu18y_photo_5003775546139282562_y.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/sofiaquino98/images/TXlaLwI0w7ezu18y_photo_5003775546139282562_y/TXlaLwI0w7ezu18y_photo_5003775546139282562_y.webp)
![9cV7vfmjjH4Elxnl_photo_5003775546139282563_y.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/sofiaquino98/images/9cV7vfmjjH4Elxnl_photo_5003775546139282563_y/9cV7vfmjjH4Elxnl_photo_5003775546139282563_y.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

<center>ESPAÑOL</center>

Identificar valores como direcciones de vida es poder clarificar
qué es eso que nos llena el corazón y de cuáles formas queremos vivir nuestras vidas.
Más allá de un resultado, de obtener un logro o ingreso, del reconocimiento o la mirada de otras personas, se trata de poder tener la certeza de aquello que colma nuestra vida de sentido. 
No siempre será fácil, bonito, o sencillo.
A veces vivir en función de nuestros valores es agotador, algunos días requiere un poco más de esfuerzo que otros. Pero lo vale todo. 

_____________

<center>ENGLISH</center>

Identifying values as guiding principles for life means being able to clarify
what it is that fills our hearts and how we want to live our lives.
Beyond any outcome, whether it’s achieving a goal or earning an income, or seeking recognition or the approval of others, it’s about having the certainty of what fills our lives with meaning. 
It won’t always be easy, pleasant, or simple.
Sometimes living according to our values is exhausting; some days it requires a little more effort than others. But it’s all worth it. 



---

body.title: I Am #AliveAndThriving Today! || #IAmAliveChallenge || Daily Off-Grid Jungle Journal Entry: Day #1425 - Continued Tweaking and Testing of Llama.cpp-Fork Build and Run Flags - Lower Puna, Far East Big Island, Hawai'i - Saturday, June 13, 2026
body.body: ![Hive-Banner-Green-Rounded.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23tGM7REKBsvoBhPiEV5Fvb8tb333qQ8N9x2YfxaF9vWohE9Qf39RUEAn3LfysdgfbYpZ.png) ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) ![IMG_20260611_144941007.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23u611vCYp4unAZXQKQcZtC4ZJRBXXKmJusKj7o1BjcpzVAHjDfkwYXSwiXCa5gQe4nc7.jpg) ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) >I live naked and barefooted, very close to Earth and Nature, in an 18-acre, off-grid, clothing-optional, food-forest intentional community ([GaiaYoga Gardens](https://gaiayoga.org)), way out in the jungles of Lower Puna, far East Big Island, Hawai'i, and I have for more than 7 years now. Although there are many challenges, I love my life, and I'm immensely grateful to live where and how I do, on my own terms! I would not want to live any other way! 😁🙏💚⚡💥🔥✴️✳️❇️👣🌱✨🤙 ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-3.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23t6vW6aH5DR2YDkVqNYUx8BexWwy9N6Z5spVSE48QJrgFzyfjAip7syeyq3K4RmyypRS.png) ``` Hive Debt: 25.80% HIVE Fiat-Dollar Price: 0.049 USD HBD/HIVE-Backed Dollar Fiat-Dollar Price: 0.951 USD ALIVE SWAP.HIVE Price: 0.02322842 SWAP.HIVE HEARTBEAT ALIVE Price: 0.10953268 ALIVE BLURT Fiat-Dollar Price: 0.00072874 USD QORT Fiat-Dollar Price: 0.149303 USD VOI Fiat-Dollar Price: 0.0001253 USD BTC/Bitcoin Fiat-Dollar Price: 64,008.45 USD BCH/Bitcoin Cash Fiat-Dollar Price: 200.56 USD LTC/Litecoin Fiat-Dollar Price: 44.37 USD Gold Fiat-Dollar Price: 4,218.85 USD Silver Fiat-Dollar Price: 68.00 USD Ranking for Our @aliveandmmb Witness Node: #125 (among all witnesses, including inactive)/#99 (among active witnesses only)/653.7k HP in votes/50 votes in total ``` ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-3.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23t6vW6aH5DR2YDkVqNYUx8BexWwy9N6Z5spVSE48QJrgFzyfjAip7syeyq3K4RmyypRS.png) Warm greetings all! 😁🙏💚✨🤙 While I am now able to successfully load and run both Gemma 4 26B-A4B QAT and Qwen3.6 35B-A3B APEX IQuality (*with Hermes Agent imatrix tuning*) on my laptop for extended periods, there are still some server instabilities and crashes, which I'm in the process of noodling out and resolving. I don't have huge amounts of time, so I'm doing this in short, focused bursts. ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) ![IMG_20260611_145118598.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23wByFZEyXXFiBbwhGwR4ZM8f4G9qRytYh2nu5di4SjNbv8GwjRywLkcEMaHnGP6FwAxB.jpg) ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) ![IMG_20260611_145311475.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23tbwHjPc3Z7ptmFcXQqsHu5JyCqSUT2eNhdVkpB3kPDpNUGPTh2UEueqoT3s3KhCCemb.jpg) ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) Qwen3.6 35B-A3B APEX IQuality does seem to be a bit more finicky when it comes to the run flags that I use than Gemma 4 26B-A4B QAT, so I've had to create four different run profiles in total, one for each of the two models, with their specific ik_llama.cpp and llama-cpp-turboquant run flags. My challenges in this regard are multiplied, as I'm not just learning the run flags for one fork of llama.cpp, but two, and there's still so much testing left to do. ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) ![IMG_20260611_145409350.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23tmB3T9Y7r1KXPkMdPdNxESTfiZGhqrr8YiTnPS5x9DagM7ZSpLErwft2VZmovwfUAnf.jpg) ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) ![IMG_20260611_154543223.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23uQn8evSjrhnx1ALjidSxyArDctu9jQPoMfTKw1D9VNZx177JZaKhwiiz3jC8SwrzdNT.jpg) ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) I'm relentless and tenacious, however, so after any frustrating failure, I just focus on something else for a while, then I returns after a short time, for another round of experimentation and testing. This is how I figure out, and finally learn, any new technologcal framework with which I come to work. In the end, I usually come out with a very good understanding of the framework with which I'm working. Along with lots of research, that's how I've learned to become quite proficient in all of my techy passions. ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) ![IMG_20260611_154948720.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23xyUm8582CodK5FWqoMZQveiWjZeWz5g61FPJoRK5X1SwUkv5xRvFPkv2CPXXvbxP6Ep.jpg) ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) ![IMG_20260611_160859248.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23uFnsCr78NDaCsWL7kU2NX1UBLwikmedSU8PRfh6VuN6KE8gywtSHmrBMvzsftJ7ixBA.jpg) ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) I'll always choose to do things in a free, open-source, locally-run, manner that is private, and which is under my control. Running my own local SearXNG meta-search engine, and my local LLM-server-Hermes-Agent agentic-AI framework, are two recent examples of this propensity and proclivity, but it pertains to any technology that I come to use. ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) ![IMG_20260612_083219361.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23vhwrmPCnJohBRkU1qpcgAiQaMRy81wsDt86iory6Sk8teJgfykJkW2QQPKCMKUs6M5x.jpg) ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) ![IMG_20260612_091945031.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23uEx4AvKmZJugyPQCdfK8PZjrSQezGYSXcLLorJgzLbLe258FY8Sp2DmTkSfCTMLUPhi.jpg) ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) Open-source and open-weights agentic-AI tech is immensely fascinating and exciting for me, partly because the potentials of what I'll be able to do with it are truly quite incredible and mind blowing. Doing this on local hardware is at the very cutting edge of development, and it's squarely in the domain of the pioneering exploration and discovery of what's possible. ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) ![IMG_20260612_151556055.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23wWuGzkLQ2289PCfFW5G5zULWyk3Z465MpD1sV91V22Y58VTQz3VKixRVBrfFLFks4u5.jpg) ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) ![IMG_20260612_151851881.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23wC9aAkbY9KttS6nJWhuw8rynD52jYuWiirPTUHAwFc4xrjvDK3LRoBADU5bfxxXwWbi.jpg) ![Hive-Divider-Green-Rounded-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SJijRvUyTXadQzZdxrbHPEg3bhwUH5Ha71Az1EVsufJ3GqtYTKCQcedWbhXumvs.png) Yesterday, Saturday, I left the Flow House, after finishing up my Hive-Blurt-'We Are Alive Tribe' tasks, by around 2:30PM, giving my attention first to some photography for my posts, and then to few jungle-community tasks, including chopping and dumping bad/used coconuts at the upper coco bar, digging a new planting hole along the main trail in the spot that I cleared yesterday, and collecting and moving a wheelbarrow full if lava rocks to stage near the Landing for use in creating a new foundation. I went to Wabisabi in the early evening to make myself some food, and to collect my leftover superfood fire coffee from the fridge, before heading back to the Flow House to begin my evening Hive tasks. I wasn't feeling very good in the evening, and I had a headache, so I went to bed pretty much as soon as I was done going through my notifications, by just after 9:30PM. My headache was still pretty intense by 1:30AM, so unable to sleep, I went to take a hot shower, which definitely helped, after which I went back to bed. I woke up again by about 7:45AM, having slept much better than I expected (*and with no more headache*), taking some photos up on the lava in the morning light, going to prepare my superfood fire coffee in Wabisabi, then returning to the Flow House, to do a bit more testing of llama.cpp-fork build and run flags, and to write this post. It's now just before 2PM, so it's an excellent time to wrap this up, so that I may attend to my numerous important Sunday Hive-Blurt-'We Are Alive Tribe' tasks, before leaving the Flow House a little later in the afternoon, to focus on some photography for my posts first, and then on a few small jungle-community tasks. body.title: Exploring the 64-Player Mode in Chivalry 2 in depth and it's seriously entertaining!
body.body:
![1.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23wMefCDPvGRBrJ5KSH6R2oxLBjQRbyKMYZaddKjEG23PHfwxHgPuhW2LZ1NnbZw92yJG.gif)


Hey gamers, how's it going today? Hope you're all doing great. So I'm still deep into Chivalry 2 as you guys know, since the last few days I've been posting about the game, and well, this time I sat down to play the 64-player mode for a really long stretch. This is basically the main mode of the game, so it's worth exploring its possibilities first before anything else. Just like the title says, the mode is centered around a 32 vs 32 battle, a full blown clash to conquer objectives and secure victory, each map and depending on which team you land on will have its own missions you need to complete either in attacking or defending mode in order to win the battle.

So when you queue into this mode, you're thrown into what's called Team Objective, where one of the three factions (Masons, Agathians, or Tenosians) takes the role of attackers and has to push through a series of objectives within a time limit, while the other side digs in to stop them cold. The cool part is that the timer isn't shared across the whole match, each objective has its own clock, so there's no point rushing through one stage just to \

for the next, every phase stands on its own. This actually changes how you approach things, because you're not panicking the whole match, you just focus on the objective in front of you.

The scale of these battles is honestly something else. We're talking castle sieges, forest ambushes, villages getting torched, catapults raining down chaos, it's chaotic in the best way possible. You really feel like you're part of something massive, not just another random soldier running around. When you spawn in and see dozens of players clashing at a chokepoint, swords swinging, arrows flying, horses charging through, it just hits different compared to smaller modes.

**Each class has its function depending on the occasion**

![0423 (1)(8).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23xAPWxUpyw5t8QE1KzWVAtkibHBJQzdD3FaDuzMgAKFCpwnqk1ZjkqfFBbMZVgFx1ELe.jpg)

Now let's talk classes, because this is honestly where Chivalry 2 shines in terms of variety. There are four main classes: Knight, Vanguard, Footman, and Archer, and each one brings something completely different to the table. Knights are your tanky frontline guys, they soak up damage and can hold a chokepoint pretty well, perfect for defending objectives or pushing through a gate when things get messy. Vanguards are more about big, heavy hitting weapons, think two-handed swords, polearms, stuff that can one or two shot people if you land your swings right, but you're more exposed since you don't have the same defensive options as a Knight.

Footman is kind of the jack of all trades class, balanced stats, decent weapons, and honestly really good for objective play since you're flexible enough to adapt to whatever the situation calls for. And then you've got Archers, who obviously focus on ranged combat, but don't think they're useless in melee either, they've got some solid sidearm options too. What I really like is that every class also has subclasses you unlock as you level up, which change your abilities and playstyle even further, so there's a ton of room to find your own niche.

![0423 (1)(2).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23tRt9A6A9R32f8JuvYAxYimVu5PWSVohJLWDsxaRQT7hLKtXNkNgKNrTF4hscvFtRPxu.jpg)

What I noticed playing the 64-player mode specifically is that team composition actually matters a lot here. If your whole team is running Vanguards trying to one-shot everyone, but nobody's holding the line as a Knight, you're going to get steamrolled at the first objective. Same goes for archers, if you don't have a few people picking off enemies from range while everyone else brawls, the enemy team can just group up and overwhelm a single point way too easily. It's cool seeing how the mode kind of forces you to think about the bigger picture instead of just running in swinging your weapon like a maniac (even though that's still really fun to do sometimes, no shame).

**Objectives like pushing the Convoy require a lot of team coordination**

![0423 (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23wBc8g5Pk75Qsjc2fuQtNuGwMpCUdeY3tabod5k8hU7wqyMV7wuHRv4CyoQ9Gh7RJmtD.jpg)

One of the objectives I ran into a bunch during my sessions was escorting or pushing a Convoy, basically a cart or wagon that needs to move from point A to point B while the enemy team tries everything in their power to stop it dead in its tracks. Let me tell you, this objective alone can turn into absolute madness. You've got people pushing the cart, others forming a wall around it to block incoming attacks, archers picking off anyone trying to flank, and then suddenly the enemy team throws everything they've got at you because they know if that Convoy reaches its destination, it's basically game over for their defense.

What's interesting is that this objective really exposes how important communication and positioning are. If even a small group of defenders manages to slip past your frontline and reach the Convoy itself, they can stall it out completely, and then the whole timer starts working against you. I had matches where we were SO close to pushing it through, like literally seconds away, and then the enemy team pulled off a clutch defense at the last second and reset our momentum. It's stressful, but in the best way, the kind of stress that makes you want to immediately queue for another match because you NEED that win.

On the flip side, when you're on defense for the Convoy objective, it's just as intense. You're constantly trying to figure out where to commit your forces, do you go all in trying to stop the cart directly, or do you spread out and pick off the support players trying to clear a path for it? There's no single \

strategy here, and that's honestly what makes these objectives so replayable. Every match feels a little different depending on how aggressive or defensive each team decides to play.

**Looting the cities has never been this fun**

![0423 (1)(9).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23tvVmNTgpNfH7Dx1Fn2TXWDiQnhzEf6yCpqYyguGNVfYxmYxmNzcV2YJR19njnASHBJu.jpg)

Now here's something that genuinely surprised me, the amount of detail put into letting you just pillage and mess around in these villages and towns. Like, beyond the actual objectives, there's just so much stuff scattered around to interact with. You can grab livestock (yes, actual animals you can pick up and throw, it's hilarious), smash through crates, knock over barrels, set things on fire, basically just wreck the place while the battle rages around you.

It sounds like a small thing, but it adds SO much atmosphere to the whole experience. You're not just running through an empty corridor waiting for the next fight, you're running through a living, breathing village that's actively being destroyed by the war happening around it. I spent way more time than I probably should have just grabbing chickens and throwing them at enemies mid-fight, and honestly? Worth it every single time. The chaos of seeing flames spreading through wooden buildings while two armies clash in the streets just makes everything feel so much more alive compared to other medieval combat games I've played.

It also gives you these little moments of comic relief in between the intense fighting. Like you could be in the middle of a brutal sword fight, barely surviving, and then someone runs by holding a fish they picked up from a market stall and just smacks an enemy with it. It's stupid, it's hilarious, and it's exactly the kind of chaotic fun that makes Chivalry 2 stand out from more \

medieval combat games.

**For now I plan to keep playing**

![0423 (1)(5).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23wMaoSuiHZQLKJwgtmhU4LL3rBwWzwacfjPyWWxcLZ6fK5eRdqByGb4y8nxkt58gQc2i.jpg)

So yeah gamers, that's my deep dive into the 64-player mode for now. There's clearly a TON more to explore here, different maps, different objectives, different class combinations to try out. I haven't even touched on the smaller game modes yet like Team Deathmatch or Free-for-all, but those will have to wait for another post since this mode alone gave me hours of solid content to talk about.

![0423 (1)(6).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23swnSkooMCK5oLSZagYy7VRtz7VA4gGjrMugkqP9Y4MKqztNK5AeTSkhMnowiqQr3oHE.jpg)

Honestly, this mode alone could keep me busy for a long while, every match feels different depending on the team comps, the map, and just how chaotic everyone decides to get. If you've played Chivalry 2's 64-player mode, let me know what your favorite objective or map has been so far, I'm curious to hear what other people have run into. See you all in the next post!

body.title: [EN/PT] A Little Piece of Germany in Northeastern Brazil
body.body: > # [EN] Yesterday I visited the famous Casa Alemã, a well-known café and pastry shop in Aracaju. I went there to pick up an order for a friend: a cake and some savory snacks to celebrate his girlfriend's birthday. I had never been to this pastry shop before; I had only heard about it because of its great reputation for its delicious cakes. To my surprise, I didn't know that the building's architecture was a replica of the typical houses found in Southern Brazil, inspired by European culture. While my friend was inside picking up the order, I stayed outside taking some photos because I was quite impressed by the architecture. Casa Alemã is located in the Jardins neighborhood, one of the most upscale areas of Aracaju, and during the entire time I was there, the place was constantly busy. I was surprised because the prices of the products are quite high. Even so, the place was always full of customers. However, I will definitely stop by again to enjoy a hot drink, perhaps a cup of hot chocolate, along with a delicious slice of cake—one of those that so many people praise. I will also certainly take my wife there so she can get to know this beautiful place. This was a little bit about my Saturday, which was quite busy because of the World Cup and the match involving our Brazilian National Team. I hope you enjoyed reading about it! --- # [PT] Ontem eu fui à famosa Casa Alemã, uma conhecida cafeteria e doceria em Aracaju. Fui buscar uma encomenda para um amigo: uma torta e alguns salgados para comemorar o aniversário de sua namorada. Eu nunca tinha ido a essa doceria, apenas ouvia falar dela devido à enorme fama de suas deliciosas tortas. Para minha surpresa, eu não sabia que a arquitetura do local era uma réplica das casas típicas do Sul do Brasil, inspiradas na cultura europeia. Enquanto meu amigo estava lá pegando as encomendas, eu fiquei na parte de fora tirando algumas fotos, pois fiquei bastante impressionado com a arquitetura. A Casa Alemã fica no bairro Jardins, um dos bairros mais nobres de Aracaju, e durante todo o tempo em que estive por lá o movimento não parava. Fiquei surpreso, pois os preços dos produtos são bem altos. Mesmo assim, o local estava sempre cheio de clientes. Porém, com certeza ainda vou passar por lá para tomar uma bebida quente, talvez um chocolate quente, acompanhado de uma deliciosa fatia de torta, daquelas que tantas pessoas elogiam. Com certeza também vou levar minha esposa para conhecer esse belo local. Esse foi um pouco do meu sábado, que estava bastante agitado devido à Copa do Mundo e ao jogo da nossa Seleção Brasileira. Espero que tenham gostado!
