body.title: A PEACEFUL SUNDAY
body.body:
Some Sundays are just meant for breathing. No alarms, no deadlines, no heel pain in my head. Just quiet. This Sunday was one of those days. After a week that felt like it ran a marathon on my body, I finally got what I had been craving: a peaceful Sunday.

I woke up at 2:00 PM. I know, that sounds late to most people. But when you’ve spent the whole week running on broken sleep, waking up at 2 PM feels like winning a small lottery. My body was tired in that deep, bone-level way where even your eyelids feel heavy. The week had been rough. Work stress, a scary heel pain that sent me for an X-ray, rainy nights, and just the general weight of responsibilities. By Friday night I had already decided: Saturday is for dance shows, but Sunday is for me. No plans, no guilt.

When I finally opened my eyes, the first thing I noticed was the light. It wasn’t the harsh white light of my phone screen or the tube light I fall asleep under sometimes. It was soft, natural daylight slipping through the curtains. I got up slowly, stretched, and walked to the window. The sky was clear blue. Not a single cloud. The temperature was moderate, that perfect Faisalabad kind of weather where it’s not humid and not too hot. Just right for standing on the balcony with your hair messy and not caring. I stood there for a few minutes and let my brain catch up with my body. I was actually rested. I could feel it. No headache, no rush of thoughts. Just calm.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZR2aC3pndTAUb7dkpt5m6itBYYWACayZDqLfLv84Fbzk/1781471902200.jpg)

I decided to start the day by doing something productive but low effort. I took out all my dresses for the coming week and started pressing them. It sounds boring, but there’s something very satisfying about it when you’re not in a hurry. I put on some music, not dance show music, just soft songs, and went one by one through my wardrobe. Shirt, dupatta, trouser. Fold, hang, repeat. With every piece I pressed, I felt like I was pressing the stress of last week out too. No wrinkles on the clothes, no wrinkles in my head. By the time I finished, my whole week felt sorted. That’s a small win, but on a peaceful Sunday, small wins are everything.

Once the clothes were done, my stomach reminded me that I hadn’t eaten since last night. And when you wake up at 2 PM, your breakfast and lunch kind of merge into one big meal. I wasn’t in the mood to cook. It was Sunday, my rest day, and cooking felt like work. So I did what any sensible person would do: I ordered KFC. Not just any order. I went all in. Mexican burgers, because I love that zesty kick. A Snack Bucket, because variety is happiness. A Mayo Bucket, because why pretend we don’t love extra sauce. And of course Coca Cola. For me, Coca Cola is mandatory with KFC. It’s not a meal without that fizz hitting the back of your throat after a spicy bite. I placed the order, and while waiting, I just sat on the sofa and enjoyed the quiet. No TV, no phone calls. Just the sound of the fan and the smell of fresh ironed clothes.

The food arrived in about 25 minutes. The rider handed me the bag and I swear the smell of hot fried chicken filled the whole room. I called my sister, and we set up on the dining table. We didn’t do anything fancy. No special plates. Just opened the boxes, passed the tissues, and dug in. The Mexican burger was as good as I remembered. Spicy, tangy, with that crunch from the lettuce and the soft bun. The Snack Bucket had those little hot wings and strips that disappear too fast when two people are eating. We fought over the last piece, like always. The Mayo Bucket was basically a small tub of happiness. We dipped everything in it. Fries, burger, even the chicken. And the Coca Cola was ice cold. That first sip after a spicy bite is unmatched. We didn’t talk much while eating. We were too focused. That’s how you know the food is good.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQdYrU7rDTGD45Auxy7dV5isk5Jhx7HPQpENzBc1iTXPE/1781471988261.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbf3CD8aYq2ew5ecvczrcDmT5t1Yd3oxyx7AuiwzwBRMt/1781471988352.jpg)

We finished everything slowly, taking our time. There was no rush to clear the table or run somewhere. We leaned back in the chairs, completely full, and just laughed at how much we had eaten. My stomach felt heavy in the best way. The kind of full that makes you want to nap again. I told my sister, “This is why Sundays should be a three day event.” She agreed.

Just when we thought the food chapter of the day was closed, there was a knock at the door. My friend arrived. She walked in, saw the empty KFC boxes, and said, “You guys started without me?” We told her we didn’t know she was coming. She smiled and said, “That’s okay. But now that I’m here, let’s go eat something chilled and sweet.” I was already full, but the idea of something cold on a perfect weather day was tempting. And honestly, when she said “chilled and sweet,” only one thing came to my mind: Matka Falooda.

If you’re from Faisalabad, you know Matka Falooda is not just a dessert. It’s an event. It comes in that little clay pot, layered with kulfi, falooda noodles, basil seeds, rose syrup, jelly, and crushed ice. It’s cold, sweet, and feels like a festival in your mouth. We all agreed immediately. We changed quickly, grabbed our bags, and headed out. The drive was short, but with the clear blue sky and the moderate breeze coming through the car windows, it felt like a scene from a movie. No traffic stress, no honking. Just a smooth Sunday drive.

We reached the Matka Falooda shop and it was already busy. Families, couples, groups of friends, everyone had the same idea. We found a table outside under a shade and ordered. I told them I was already full from KFC, so I just got one for myself to share bites. My sister and friend ordered their own. While we waited, we looked around. Kids were laughing, someone was trying to finish their falooda before it melted, and the uncle at the next table was arguing with his son about who got more kulfi. It was simple, everyday life, but it felt special because I was actually present enough to notice it.

The falooda arrived in those cute little matkas. The clay pot was cold to touch, with condensation on the outside. The top was loaded with a scoop of kulfi, drizzled with rose syrup, and sprinkled with chopped nuts. I took the first spoon and it was exactly what I needed. Cold, creamy, sweet, with the chewy falooda noodles and the sudden crunch of basil seeds. It was the opposite of the spicy KFC, and my taste buds loved the contrast. My sister, who has no concept of being full, also ordered a plate of spicy gol gappas. The moment the plate came, the smell of khatta pani hit our noses. I just watched her eat. She took one, filled it with chana and potato, dipped it in the spicy water, and popped the whole thing in her mouth. Her eyes watered immediately, but she kept going. I laughed and said, “You’re crazy. I’m still digesting a whole Snack Bucket.” She said, “Gol gappas have separate space in the stomach. Everyone knows that.” We all cracked up.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQAr25dFMULg5btYuGjkZQixAVjw54mHqKRfQMhJQG7AD/1781472099151.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcrZ2n5vKNhjFegZDdP7UuMPc7HFp7L6r7vLqrVfCu7wu/1781472099229.jpg)

We sat there for almost an hour. Not because we were eating the whole time, but because we were talking. About the week, about random things, about a dance performance we saw last night. No one checked their phone. No one said “we have to go.” The sun was starting to go down, and the sky turned that soft orange color that only happens on calm days. The breeze picked up a little, and it carried the smell of rose syrup and spicy water together. It was strange but nice.

On the way back home, we didn’t play music in the car. We just had the windows down and let the air come in. I felt light. Not just because the day was easy, but because my mind was quiet. The whole week I had been anxious about my heel, about work, about everything. But that Sunday, for a few hours, none of that existed. There was just sleep, and blue skies, and ironed clothes, and KFC, and Matka Falooda, and my sisters.

When we got home, it was around 7 PM. The house smelled like the rose syrup from the falooda that had spilled a little in the bag. I changed into comfortable clothes, made a cup of chai even though I had just had something cold, and sat on the balcony. The temperature was still perfect. Not hot, not cold. I could hear kids playing in the street and someone’s TV playing in the distance. I thought about how different this was from last Sunday. Last Sunday I was worried about my X-ray. This Sunday I was worried about whether I could finish my falooda. That’s progress.

I didn’t turn on the TV for a dance show that night. Usually Sunday night is India’s Best Dancer time, but I was too content to move. I just wanted to hold on to the peaceful feeling a little longer. I scrolled through my phone a bit, saw photos from the day, and smiled. My sister had taken a picture of me holding the Matka Falooda with ketchup still on the corner of my mouth from KFC. It was messy, but it was real. That’s what the day was. Messy, full, and real.

Before sleeping, I looked at the stack of ironed dresses for the week. Monday to Friday, all sorted. That gave me a small sense of control. I know the week ahead will be busy again. There will be work, and maybe more doctor visits, and stress I can’t predict. But now I had this Sunday in my memory. I had 2 PM sleep, and blue skies, and Mexican burgers, and Coca Cola, and clay pots, and laughter. When the week gets hard, I can come back to this day in my head.

I went to bed early, around 10 PM, which is rare for me. But I wasn’t tired. I was rested. There’s a difference. Tired means your body wants to shut down. Rested means your soul feels ready to try again. As I pulled the blanket up, I whispered to myself, “So, it was a peaceful Sunday.” And it really was.Some people need a vacation to feel peace. Some people need a whole trip to the mountains. Me, I just needed a late sleep, good weather, junk food, and my sisters. I didn’t do anything big. I didn’t achieve anything. I didn’t post it on Instagram. But I lived it. And sometimes, that’s enough.

So yes, it was a peaceful Sunday. The kind you don’t plan, but you’re grateful for when it happens. The kind that reminds you that life isn’t just about running. It’s also about stopping, eating a Matka Falooda, and watching the sky change color. And if you’re lucky, you get to do it with people who make the food taste better just by being there.

That was my Sunday. Full sleep, full stomach, full heart. I wouldn’t change a thing.

**How was Your Sunday?**

body.title: When One Life Ends, Let the Better One Begin
body.body:
<center> https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdsqQm5i9VQ3PUiYWgxNzwK18mpPVMAtPmx2AiGka7Nbm/17814716798222679262125167514063.png 
[Source](https://pixabay.com/photos/buildings-taiwan-taipei-101-1846728/) 
</center>


As one chapter closes, you are sure that another one will surely begin. And that's a good way to live life. And that's how life was planned.

Change is a small, constant rhythm in life. In one season you are up, in another season you might be down. But some people have been so good and life has favoured them so much that they are up at all times, all through life, from the beginning to the end.

Yet, when a part of your life ends, whether a relationship, a role, rhythm or personal identity, it really feels small. Ending can sometimes arrive with grief and confusion. It can also come with failure.

It is a usual thing, so you shouldn't expect less. It is also natural. The other half is arrival, the quiet one.

That one is very invincible and so many things doesn't grow in that phase of life. When you stand at that threshold, your work is simple and it's very hard at the same time. You shouldn't be afraid to accept blessing too.

Ending can also feel like losses. It pulls us towards what we know. And we have a way through it that we should say goodbye to routine.

Even some endings, they free us from something that is difficult and can lead to fear. Fear of the unknown is real. Also, fear of repeating the same mistake over and over again makes you look foolish to yourself.

There's also fear that the next thing might be more worse than the one of present. Fear is protective in its own sense. But it's fears of what has already happened before.

But if we let fear dominate us, growth becomes a thing of the past. When you look at the ending, it gives you enough time to prepare. Not punish yourself at it.

That's not the time to shift blame. Ending a life or a chapter in life is not the final end actually. It is the page of your life turning, sheet by sheet, chapter by chapter, book by book.

As ending prepares you, you are being thrown away from things that no longer serves its purpose. As time goes on, new blessings seem to come quickly. Blessings may appear rarely as grand fanfare.

They can sometimes come in small openings. A conversation that leads to projects and likes. Friendships that deepen a bit about what is right.

Then you have people on the same page with you in life. Acceptance means you are staying receptive of things. There are also practical steps to accepting new blessings as mistakes can cause failure.

Patience and ability to associate yourself with good people at every point in time can bring you blessings. You have to first allow her next grief. Whenever something bad happens, set grief about the thing before you move on to the next phase of life.

An uncured grief can lead to a wreckage of emotional life. You should also create some small experiences here and there that can cushion if any bad thing happens. Then give you enough positive energy to move to the next one.

Then you have to see failure in a different way. Different in such a way that failure should not be seen as an end. Failure is a work in progress.

Then always be grateful at all times. Those are the things that you need to cross from being a negative bad person to a positive right person.

body.title: If I Had A Million Dollars.
body.body: > What would you do if you suddenly woke up and discovered that you had won $1 million in your wallet, okay so this is one question that I do know that a lot of people would ask or think about at least at one point in their life because human imagination is wild. It just takes me back to a few days ago when I was talking with someone that if I found good amount of money this period , that I was sure of what I was going to use it to do. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmS7LBQDd9VEnreBAxynmpnMYrHPnQgbwJ6PiBSbxqKNtE/1781471600086.png) So for me, the first thing I know i would do is quit my job, and it is not because I hate working or anything, nope, but because I would want some alone time to think properly without the pressure of everyday responsibilities hanging on my head. We have seen situations where alot of people receive life changing amounts of money and they rush to spending it, only for them to regret their decisions later on, i do not want to be that person at all In fact, one of the first things that I would do is leave my current environment for a while and go to another location where I can think clearly, somewhere quiet where I can sit down and carefully plan how I want to use the money, because that needs proper planning seriously. See here ehn.... the truth is that $1 million is a lot of money when converted to my country's currency and even without it being converted, but then it is also the kind of money that can actually disappear quickly if you do not have a good plan for it. Of course, helping my family would be one of my biggest priorities that's very sure , for this one I don't even need to think twice about that at all, because see, my family has been there for me, they have been there through different stages of my life, and if I suddenly had that kind of financial freedom, I would definitely make sure they benefited from it too, there are needs that would be taken care of, bills that would be settled, and a lot of things that would become easier for the people I care about. After that, I would focus on investments. I wouldn't want to spend all the money without creating something that continues to generate income, I would look for a good business that has strong potential and invest in it, something sustainable that can continue bringing returns for years to come. For me, financial freedom is not just about having money today, It is about creating systems that keep money coming tomorrow. I would also think seriously about buying a house for myself and my family, Having a place you can truly call your own is something many people dream about, Knowing that your family has a comfortable and secure home would bring a level of peace that is difficult to describe. Honestly, I don't think my life would suddenly become all about luxury, Yes, I would enjoy some comfort, Yes, I would probably buy a few things I've always wanted. But my biggest focus would be stability and long term security, I have seen enough stories of people who became wealthy overnight and ended up with nothing a few years later because they lacked proper planning. That is why my first reaction wouldn't be spending. It would be thinking. Thinking carefully. Planning carefully, and making sure every major decision serves a purpose. So yeah, if I woke up tomorrow and discovered that I had won $1 million in my wallet, truly, I would first step back, breathe, and then give myself time to think , then I would help my family, invest wisely, secure a home in a good location for us, and then create opportunities that would continue benefiting us long into the future. Because for me, true financial freedom is not just about having money but it is about making sure that the money creates a better life that lasts for many generations to come. body.title: CNF: Some left behinds find their way back to us.
body.body:
> 


You will not understand the pains that come with leaving something valuable behind until you experience it firsthand; at that point, you experience the confusion, the chaos and how destabilising that can be.

\
I said to them, making a face, because being late is a habit, especially for Dera.\n\n\
Dera responded, knowing fully well what I said concerns him mostly. \n\n\

I responded as well, departed and headed for our houses.

The course we were going to write is one that nobody fully understood because the lecturer kept saying we are supposed to know everything about the course and refused to explain it since he expected that we knew it already, whereas we do not even know a thing. We used YouTube and any other source we could find to help us understand the course, but none helped us to fully grasp the course. It was an examination; everyone was definitely going to the hall anxious and not knowing what to expect, which makes being there early very important so you don't rush in and forget the little you were able to understand.

If only I could hold time and stop it from moving so I could prepare better; I would have done that, but since I could not before I could add to my preparation, the day for the exams had already come, and all I had left before I stepped into the unknown was an hour. I was just staring at a past question, wishing the lecturer would not give us a set of questions like that because they were indeed difficult when my phone rang. I stretched to look at the screen and saw it was Dera. 

\
Dera said to me over the phone.\n\n\
I responded as we both burst into laughter. \

I responded. 

Dera hung up, and the rest of us dressed up and made our way to the hall. We arrived at the hall, and they started the regular checks before the exams started, and we queued up for biometrics, which took long, and before it ended it was already almost time for the exams, but surprisingly Dera was still nowhere to be found. We took an excuse, stepped outside and started calling him to at least tell him to hurry up, but he was not picking up his calls.

About 20 minutes into the exams and still no sight of him, we got scared and at the same time angry. He won't pick up to tell us if he is fine, and then he won't show up to the exams hall like it is expected of him. 30 minutes were gone, and we saw Dera walk into the hall like a ghost and with a very long face. The invigilators did not allow him to sit on the seat we kept for him, so we had to wait until after exams to tell him how angry we are and then get to hear his side of the story and why he did what he did. 

After about an hour and a half, our answer scripts were collected, and immediately we rushed in the direction where Dera was seated. 

\

I boarded another tricycle and tried to track and find the one I alighted from, but that seemed impossible, and I did not check the number on it. I tried all I could and could not find it, so I had to just let it go and make my way to the hall.\
I don't think we should give up on the phone like that; some left behind will always find their way back to us.\
Don't give up and still don't raise your hopes too high.\
Hello, you must be the owner of the phone?\
I found the phone at the back of my tricycle this morning and had to remove the SIM and insert it in my own phone since the phone was locked.\
Yes, sir, please, where can I meet you to collect the phone?\
Just come to the junction before the school gate by 8am; I will be there,\
I saw you changed your mind ;-)

Hello, I hope everyone is doing well. I haven’t been here in a very long time, and to be honest, I haven’t even been able to keep up with the platform from afar. I just wanted to stop by to say hi and see what’s been going on. This will be a short post. Since I don’t take many photos, this post will feature only our cat, Pamuk! 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUh9NdmCjBJiiBXaFSKDw4YVpcqdAorCE1wvMBqkk6Ads/whatsapp_image_2026_06_15_at_00.01.03_1_.jpeg)

I’ve been going through a rough patch—I lost my job. It’s been a tough time for me. I couldn’t find anything to share here, so I decided to take a break to avoid repeating myself.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmThnZgDF4zcr1Sfvfb1KZpfYAT78fs9ijyd3D46L5RMng/whatsapp_image_2026_06_15_at_00.01.03_3_.jpeg)



Now I look back and see that exactly 5 months have passed since my last post. A lot must have changed here. I wonder if anyone has left Hive since then? Or if there are new people who’ve joined us? What’s changed on the platform? I’m really curious about all that. I hope everyone I love and enjoy following is still here. As for me, I managed to find a new job. I’ve finished my second month, and everything is going smoothly so far. Plus, the pay and conditions are better than my previous job. The only thing is, my work hours are a bit long, so I can’t be as active as before, and by the end of the day, I feel really exhausted. So, do I consider this a problem? Never, because being unemployed is terrible. Especially for a married man, it makes you feel terrible psychologically. My wife is an amazing person and has always supported me in this regard, but you know, no matter how much support she gave, I still felt bad deep down. body.title: Mixing Strokes
body.body: >\n\nThis week has become somewhat of a mixed week for me personally, as it is going into midsummer, and it is also the \

of having my stroke coming up, which happens to fall on midsummer celebration day this year. So, while people around me are gearing up for summer, I feel even more out of place than normal. And even though it is just another week and just another day, it is a reminder of what was, and what perhaps could have been. 

---


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23ydRC7LY2x6cguwi2JBK9kc2f9XkZLF794jU9dGGKo71oS598StxXHQdcYQL45b5RpzU.png)


---

I had a conversation with Smallsteps yesterday about time travel, since we watched *Back to the Future* for the first time together a couple weeks ago. I was trying to see how her brain might process the concept and whether she would pick the holes in the idea, and she did pretty well. From there, it was just playing and coming up with funny scenarios.

After working out that we would be able to meet ourselves, I her what she would tell herself five years ago, and she came up with a few silly ideas - also realising that there is a difference between being told, and actually doing. I said that she should remember that in five years from now, if she went back, she would be telling herself something as she is today. I told her people generally regret what they didn't do, not what they did.

> She asked what I would tell myself five years ago.

Well, *to go to the hospital and tell them I have a dissected carotid artery and need treatment to stop it from giving me a stroke.* 

> As well as a few investment suggestions. 

It is all counterfactual of course, but I would assume that had I not had a stroke, my life would likely be better. No guarantees, *but likely.* But, since I can't go back in time, I can't change the fact that I had a stroke, or that I didn't make great investment decisions. 

> I am stuck with the nonsense I got.

As said, it is a bit of a mixed bag of a week for me now, as while I want to be positive, it is a reminder of the loss also. Like the birthday of a loved one who died too young. And it is a bit similar to that perhaps, because when I had the stroke, *I did die* in a sense. Not physically this time, but the personality I had was fundamentally changed in an instant and quite heavily, so it is a bit like being reborn with another person's body, having your own memories, but the other person's capabilities - and they are not nearly as capable.

> It is what it is.

And regardless hoe I feel about things, life goes on for everyone else unabated, and for me too. No good comes of dwelling, but we have brains that process what they choose to process, and it isn't always the fun stuff. I take the approach that it is better to reflect on experience, than deny it. Some people talk about \

what has happened, but they don't seem to acknowledge the difference between accepting and *giving up.* A lot of people say they accepted something, but in reality, they just gave up. And if we all accept our situation in that way, we wouldn't progress very far at all. > Mix it up. I might write more on this on my stroke-aversary. Taraz [ Gen1: Hive ] --- **Be part of the Hive discussion.** - Comment on the topics of the article, and add your perspectives and experiences. - Read and discuss with others who comment and build your personal network - Engage well with me and others and put in effort **And you may be rewarded.** ---

body.title: The Critical Role of Digital Preservation in Gaming History
body.body:
Just a heads-up: This is a long read. Bring some popcorn.

# Intro
___

It's no secret gaming history has a preservation problem. Just as the film industry viewed movies as disposable entertainment until the invention of the VCR and the business of video sales suddenly made those backlogs profitable again, game studios have rarely been interested in what happened to individual titles once they were packaged and shipped out the door. After all, the Super Nintendo hardware was superior to the NES hardware, so in a Nintendo executive's mind, why would anybody want to play *Super Mario Bros.* or *The Legend of Zelda* when they could instead play *Super Mario World* or *A Link to the Past*? Arcade manufacturers of the late 1970s and early 1980s knew that even their most successful games like *Pac-Man* and *Space Invaders* would invariably give way to newer, bigger titles. The gaming industry, after all, relies upon pushing new products out the door in order to meet consumer demand. The release of *Mortal Kombat II* would inevitably overshadow *Mortal Kombat*, just as *Super Street Fighter II* would overshadow the original. That's just how things are. The idea that more than a handful of people in 2003, or 2013, or 2023 would want to play a game released in 1993 was absurd; the thought of companies caring enough to preserve the materials that went into creating those games even more so. There are a freakishly enormous number of gaps in gaming history's fossil record.


<center>![games-preservation.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/modernzorker/23sxDy12tbgnJd6mT8jVSvPPHs3SKNbRpr5TQ9FkKT5j8DAD1KMPe2RvfH8LtFVsdZB39.jpg)</center>
<center>*Source: [GamesHub.com](https://www.gameshub.com/news/news/video-games-preservation-missing-us-study-2623530/)*</center>


Fortunately the last decade has seen a resurgence in the idea of preservation at the corporate level. GOG.com, for instance, provides a storefront with with thousands of titles, updated to run on modern hardware, DRM-free, with the notion that you should actually own the games you buy, even if you aren't purchasing a physical disc. What's more, the number of titles they've managed to return to market in their digital ecosystem is astounding: *Silent Hill 4* on the PC is playable as the developers intended, but on modern hardware. Capcom's first two *Dino Crisis* games and first three *Resident Evil* titles, which all received PC ports in the '90s and early 2000s, are now both inexpensive to purchase and simple to play. *Cold Fear*, an oft-overlooked survival horror title from the PS2 era, is back and running better than ever.

Alongside platforms like GOG, you also have studios like Limited Run and Night Dive, which work to rescue older games from IP rights nightmares and re-release them for modern audiences. Titles like *Clock Tower*, *Scott Pilgrim vs. The World*, and *Blood: Refreshed Supply* are all playable due to the efforts studios like these.

Console manufacturers have been in on the game for a while now too. Nintendo has been the leader in this, with their various e-Stores and Switch Online services offering access to hundreds of back-catalog titles and classics you can get access to for a simple monthly fee. Microsoft and Sony likewise offer up older titles for sale on their respective online stores, and some forms of backwards compatibility through either digital downloads or physical discs like *Rare Replay*, *Sonic's Ultimate Genesis Collection*, and a variety of HD Remaster collections for series like *God of War* and *Metal Gear*. And let's not forget the boom of mini plug-and-play consoles that came with dozens of built-in titles we had for a few years either.

In many cases, it has never been easier, or less expensive, to experience older games in the modern age. I applaud that, and not for one second am I knocking the strides that have been made. But we still have a problem in that the vast majority of video games are, for all intents and purposes, unplayable by the public at large via legal means. As a study [showed in 2023](https://zenodo.org/records/8161056), 87% of all video games published in the US have essentially disappeared. And for many, returning them to a playable and accessible original state is all but impossible.

## So, Why Is That?
___

Many of the same problems video game preservation has run into are the same ones faced by companies attempting to preserve television shows: copyright and trademark restrictions. EA, for example, has a long history with professional and collegiate sports. Every year, EA pays associations like the NFL, the NBA, and the PGA money to license trademarks, player names and likenesses, stadium and course designs, and other aspects of the real-life games so they can appear in EA's virtual incarnations. But these licenses are not granted in perpetuity. Since EA knows they're going to release a new Madden game every year, they contract for limited-time usage rights and those contracts are regularly re-negotiated.

If you ever wondered why you can easily play titles like Nintendo's original *Baseball* and *Tennis*, or the Genesis/Mega Drive version of EA's *Mutant League Football* via Switch Online, but you can't play Jaleco's *Bases Loaded* or EA's *NHL '94*, this is why. The amount of money and time that would have to go into satisfying the rights holders for all those official likenesses eclipses any amount the company paying for those rights could possibly recoup. For the same reason, it's unlikely we'll ever see driving games like *Gran Turismo* or *NASCAR '99* returned to life in a playable state either: the amount of money required to re-license all those makes, models, and drivers is greater than any expected revenue such a project could generate.

Could you pay a studio like Night Dive to go through a game like *Forza Horizon* and remake all the car models, touch up the logos, and replace the in-game soundtracks with royalty-free music? Sure... but if you're going to do that, why not just pay them to make a game similar to *Forza Horizon* with completely fictional car models and brands instead? The major selling point of most driving and sports titles is the dream of taking control of something you'd never be able to afford in real life. If I want to play *Gran Turismo*, I want to play *Gran Turismo*, not *Gran Temu-rismo* with all the cars carefully edited to avoid trademark infringement.

The same is true for virtually any game based on a licensed property. We're not going to see the *Superman* arcade game re-released any time soon. Neither will we see *Justice League Heroes*, *Batman: Revenge of the Joker*, *X-Men Legends*, or the film tie-in *Spider-Man 2* re-released either. Even if the original developer is still around and wanted to publish updated versions, it's rare when this sort of thing happens. Limited Run's *Marvel MaXimum Collection* that came out in March is a major exception here, not the rule.

Sometimes the concessions required to get an older game back into a playable state in modern times are small enough that someone is willing to make them. The survival horror title *ObsCure* released on the PlayStation 2, Xbox, and PC in 2005. Developer Hydravision paid to license music from the bands Sum 41 and Span, and the box touts the inclusion of this music as a selling point. However, when the game was released on Steam, these licensed tracks had been replaced with generic sound-alike songs. The change is only noticeable to people who played the original version, the songs themselves aren't relevant to the experience (outside of grounding it in an era where early 2000s butt rock was a thing), and nothing gameplay-wise was impacted by their replacement. If that's what it takes to make a game easily accessible to a modern audience, as opposed to paying borderline obscene prices for physical copies on eBay, I'm okay with that.

## The Problem
___

Nevertheless, there's a crisis in gaming preservation where the intersection of laws that exist to protect intellectual property and the drive to preserve access to our history smash head-on into one another. Yes, it's phenomenal that games like *Silent Hill 4*, *The Thing*, and *Heroes of Might & Magic II* have been archived, resurrected from the dead, and patched to ensure compatibility with modern systems. But for every game which has been rescued, there are hundreds which haven't.


<center>![gog-launches-game-preservation-program-cover6734c5255e7bd.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/modernzorker/23sxLLp8KB9QngaABz7CKsEUM263ejy4ag25e9N7J82QCuSiBkQQxp5JBkpBo2FqxwPiY.jpg)</center>
<center>*Source: [InstantGaming.com](https://news.instant-gaming.com/en/articles/9243-gog-launches-game-preservation-program)*</center>


A common argument you'll hear to this is something along the lines of: \

And, sure, if you want to look at it that pedantically, you *are* correct. Yes, anyone can go on eBay, buy a PlayStation 2, buy a PS2 controller, buy a PS2 memory card, buy a copy of *Kuon*, buy an HDMI upscaler, and play that game today in 2026. You are correct. But you're correct in a way that ignores basic economics. For people with nothing better to do with a thousand bucks, you are absolutely, 100% right. I don't know what tax bracket you live in, but I know  I don't reside there.\n\nHere's the thing though: *Kuon* is an interesting experience from a game company that went from obscurity to a household name in the twenty years since they released it, but nobody in their right mind believes it's an experience worth paying a thousand dollars for. It's expensive for reasons of physical scarcity combined with a fan base that went wild over anything with the FromSoftware name on it after the release of *Dark Souls*; critical consensus from back in the day was, basically, \

It's the very definition of a 6/10 game, something you'd expect to find on the PlayStation store as a digital download for somewhere between five and ten dollars.

Meanwhile, I can go on GOG, pay $60 (less when it's on sale) and get five classic *Resident Evil* games, every one of which is technically a better experience than *Kuon*. In what universe does it make logical sense? To legally own and play a copy of *Kuon* you need to skip a house payment or two, but to legally own and play *Resident Evil HD* you can simply skip a trip to McDonalds?

Gaming shouldn't work like this. Right? Like, I don't think that's a particularly bold take. There are an awful lot of games that vanished into the ether because their publisher or developer went belly-up, but FromSoftware does not fall into this category. They've made no attempt to hide the fact they made *Kuon*, or any of their other older games. Like many developers, FromSoft keeps an active catalog of their history. You can see their page for *Kuon* [right here](https://www.fromsoftware.jp/ww/detail.html?csm=032). It's not much, but it's *there*, along with every other game they've made going back to the original *King's Field* on the PS1.

But maybe *Kuon* is a bad example. After all, that's a PS2 exclusive with low sales numbers, which never got a PC port. Doesn't rule out a PlayStation Store download if Sony ever gets their emulation system figured out under the PS5, but let's say for the sake of argument that *Kuon*'s not a great choice. It's not a household name. It doesn't have that 'oomph' factor a studio like Night Dive would need to make it run under modern system architecture. Okay then.

How about *Silent Hill 3*?

<center>
![Silent-Hill-3s-Heather-Mason.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/modernzorker/48FGrrGrTvkXh8Bid8CGsFXZ5xHKnthtwA894U9ws3qsc955uWJ7vdRqzRm6yfiWr4.jpg)</center>
<center>*Source: [Collider.com](https://collider.com/silent-hill-3-heather-best-character/)*</center>


Konami's premiere horror franchise is absolutely huge. *Silent Hill* is a household name. *Silent Hill 2* just got a successful remake. There's talk of them remaking the original. You can already play *Silent Hill 4* on modern hardware. And unlike *Kuon*, *Silent Hill 3* got a PC release back in 2003. So what's the problem?

## ModernZorker, everybody knows Konami [lost the source code](https://www.eurogamer.net/silent-hill-hd-collection-ported-from-unfinished-code) to *Silent Hill 3* years ago, you complete dildo!

Uh-huh. And now we're back to that earlier issue. When developers finished a game, standard practice was to wipe the hard drives, shred the design documents, bin the artwork, and get ready for the next project, which may have nothing to do with the one you just finished. \

wasn't on anyone's mind. The game was done, so who cared if you didn't save the source code? What was the public going to do, want to play it again in thirty years? Why would they want to do that, and if they did, why wouldn't they just use the old hardware?

Look, not to cross the streams here, but *Doctor Who* is the longest-running science fiction television show in history. It's been around longer than *The Simpsons*. Its cultural impact is unprecedented, and for years, the BBC has taken steps to preserve the show's history and legacy. Yet, despite its globe-spanning fanbase, there are still episodes of that show which were seen exactly once when they were first broadcast, and then lost to time and neglect, because the BBC at the time not only didn't care, but assumed no one else ever would either. Discovery of elements of these lost episodes makes international news. And yet, if something so culturally relevant spanning multiple generations has gaps in its history, it's unreasonable to expect video games couldn't and wouldn't suffer the same fate.

There are a lot of collectors who cite not just ownership of physical media but \

as part of the reason why they collect what they do. This is absolutely a good reason to collect things that interest you, and it's important (at least from a historical standpoint) that as many copies of these materials as possible survive for as long as they can. If you're doing your part, whether it's with games, or movies, or comics, or whatever you like, then take some pride in your work. But also, don't kid yourself that what you're doing is actually \

, at least not in the grander sense.

With that in mind, let's tackle the elephant in the room.

## Preservation Without Access Isn't Really Preservation
___
Let's say you were a huge fan of the TV show *Seinfeld* in the '90s, and let's also say you either didn't own a VCR or you weren't good at programming it. In order to watch the newest episode of the show, you had to be somewhere with a functioning television set at the specific day and time that episode aired. If you missed it, you had to wait until the summer, where it was likely to be broadcast as a re-run. If you missed *that* though, there was a third option: you could visit the Moving Images Research Center at the Library of Congress in Washington, D.C. where, with several weeks' advance notice, you could request a screening of that specific episode in one of their viewing rooms. For copyright and archival purposes, every episode of *Seinfeld* was filed with the Library of Congress, and available for viewing upon request.

By that technical definition, every episode of *Seinfeld* is \
by the Library of Congress. And yet, if someone in 1998 told you that \

so there was no need to worry about never being able to watch it again, you'd probably feel like there was a fault in their logic. The fact something *exists* does not equate to the notion of that thing being *accessible*. Not everyone can just make a pilgrimage to Washington. Even if they could, only the most dedicated fans of the show would have been willing to do such a thing thirty years ago. For the majority of humanity, the fact the Library of Congress has a print of every *Seinfeld* episode is nothing more than an interesting factoid.

Today, of course, it's easy to legally watch *Seinfeld*: it's currently streaming on Netflix, there are literally thousands of copies of individual seasons and the complete series available for purchase on DVD and Blu-Ray both second-hand or brand new, and it's almost certainly being broadcast on one of your local television stations if you live anywhere in North America.

It's impossible to say the same thing about *Silent Hill 3*. Just because *I* own both the PC and PS2 versions of the game doesn't mean it's been preserved. My PS2 isn't going to last forever. Neither is my backup PS2. The only reason the game is playable on my PC today is due to the work of the fan community, who have been patching it and updating it to keep it working two decades later. And anybody who's played the *Silent Hill HD Collection* knows the version of *SH3* included on that is a buggy, choppy, re-voiced mess that comes nowhere close to capturing the feel of the original.

<center>![7070099-silent-hill-hd-collection-playstation-3-front-cover.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/modernzorker/23sxNqra94q6bAKeMb8BPgpYPVysPnMqsYbRB9evMd7MTwX6xyUDyeCfFc9H7FvYFGVon.jpg)
This is not preservation.</center>
<center>*Source: [MobyGames](https://www.mobygames.com/game/55350/silent-hill-hd-collection/)*</center>


## The Elephant in the Room
___

So we come to emulation. Companies like Nintendo tend to look at it as something that costs the industry billions of dollars a year in lost revenue. Pirates and data hoarders look at it as a godsend, allowing them to own every game on the planet without paying a cent.

But the truth, as usual, sits somewhere in the middle. Most people who seek out emulators aren't doing so because they want to defraud game publishers, they're doing so because, as Gabe Newell famously put it, piracy is often the result of a service issue, not a pricing issue. Most people are willing to pay an affordable price to be able to legally access a product, and the problem arises when that product is unavailable to them.

I'm a nerd with a colossal retro video game library I've been assembling and collecting for forty years. If I want to play *Super Mario Bros.*, I've got any number of ways I can do so, everything from hooking up the original NES hardware and popping in the game cart, to using my Super NES and the *Super Mario All-Stars* cart, to plugging in my NES Classic and playing it that way.

But what about someone who remembers playing *Super Mario Bros.* as a kid, yet didn't keep their games and systems, or who discovered they no longer work after thirty years in the attic? Right now, the easiest way to play *Super Mario Bros.* legally is to buy a Switch (around $200 second-hand) and pay $20 for a single year's access to Nintendo's Classic Games Library. Two hundred and twenty bucks is a big ask of someone who just wants to play the game again for an hour to see if they still remember where the first Warp Zone is and how to navigate Bowser's castle in World 8-4.

This is the sort of problem emulation solves: you might not get the \

experience of playing on original hardware with an original two-button controller, but what you get is close enough, and if there was a way for this hypothetical nostalgic user to have that experience for a few bucks, they'd be happy to pay it. As it stands though, this just isn't possible.

And if that's the case for *Super Mario Bros.*, one of the most important, most influential, and most historically significant games of all time, what does that mean for a game like, say, *Vanark* on the PS1? Oh, you've never heard of *Vanark*?

That's my whole point. So much of gaming history is so lost that most people don't even realize what's gone.

## A Language Barrier
___

To people who are largely computer literate, emulation feels like the perfect solution to the problem of accessibility (not to mention price). But just because emulation is available doesn't mean the average person with a PC knows how to use or configure them to run. After all, the emulator is just a piece of software. The end user still needs to supply necessary elements, like a game controller, the ROM files, and possibly a BIOS or two depending on what system they're attempting to emulate. The user needs to tell the emulator how to run the sound, how to display the video output, how to configure the controller or keyboard to mimic the inputs from the original hardware, where to store the save files, point it to the directory where the ROMs are located, and so on. They don't just \

automatically.\n\nThis applies doubly where personal computer emulation is concerned. It's all well and good that a program like DOSBox exists, but DOSBox assumes its users have a familiarity with DOS commands, like how to navigate its text-based directory structure, how to identify and execute the file used to run the game you want to play, what all the various graphical display modes are, and what sound card emulation works best for a given game. That's fine for someone like me, who grew up navigating operating systems like DOS and early versions of Windows. But someone born in 2000, whose earliest experiences with home operating systems was Windows XP, is far less likely to possess that knowledge. You can show them DOSBox, but it's like handing someone a book in a language they don't understand and telling them, \

Even access itself doesn't equate to preservation.

## How Do We Fix This?
___

<center>![images.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/modernzorker/23sxLR7nQhR4AwSmcKxJ1ChmFw3gFdYZ5uWZuTsPtWnkQw7zXCYRcbE2C7pBu3MGmfbV4.jpg)
Image related, I promise.</center>

There's a very simple reason why you can play *Doom* on almost anything: John Carmack released the game's source code in 1997, which gave programmers everywhere the ability to port the game to platforms it was never initially intended to run on. This essentially liberated *Doom* from being locked to MS-DOS, and opened the door for people to get it running on any system they could imagine. They did the same for *Wolfenstein 3D* in 1995, *Quake* in 1999, *Quake II* in 2001, and *Doom 3* in 2011. This makes it orders of magnitude simpler to keep these games \

to whatever ordinarily stands in the way of a deprecated code base, whether that's processors moving to a 64-bit standard, RAM being measured in gigabytes instead of megabytes, or single graphics cards more powerful than a room-sized supercomputer from twenty years ago.

It is actually easier and cheaper to play *Doom* where you want, when you want, how you want, and with whom you want today than it was in 1993. Because of this, there are millions of people who weren't even alive when *Doom* released who are nevertheless playing and enjoying it today. Heck, some of the game's original level designers are *still* making and releasing new maps for it this far into the 21st century. I'm sure if you told John Romero back in 1993 that he'd be working on an unofficial fifth episode for the game almost twenty-five years later, he'd have assumed your relationship with cocaine had progressed from 'recreational' to 'problematic'. Nevertheless, we got *Sigil* in 2019, and its sequel in 2023.

Today, you can visit GOG.com, pay $10, and get *The Ultimate Doom*, *Doom II*, *Final Doom*, *The Master Levels*, *Sigil*, *Sigil II*, the *Doom II* episode *No Rest For the Living*, an entirely new episode made specifically for this package called, *Legacy of Rust*, and a bonus pack of 25 new Deathmatch maps.

That, ideally, is what 'preservation' looks like. Most software developers, however, are not John Carmack. And while there are some gaming properties like *Final Fantasy*, *Star Wars*, and *Tomb Raider* considered so iconic that their games receive periodic updated releases and remasters, the truth is you're never going to see any company put that much care into making sure modern gamers can play *Beavis & Butthead in: Virtual Stupidity*.

Fortunately for us, what is arguably one of the most important, wide-ranging, and historically significant gaming preservation projects is currently underway and has been for years: Retro-eXo.

## What's Retro-eXo?
___

If you've been skim-reading so far, this is where you can stop. [Retro-eXo](https://retro-exo.com) is one of the single largest preservation and archival gaming projects ever attempted. This is different from your typical ROM site, because Retro-eXo isn't just concerned with giving people access to game files, they are obsessed with making sure that *anyone*, regardless of their technical skill level, is capable of playing the games they are archiving.

Retro-eXo is currently split into a number of various mini-projects, all dealing with various aspects of personal computing history. Their primary (and largest) project is [eXoDOS](https://www.retro-exo.com/exodos.html), a 640 gigabyte archive of over 7,500 games for the MS-DOS platform, presented using the LaunchBox interface. Every game in the collection has been pre-configured to run on its optimal settings, meaning the end user doesn't have to muck around with configuration files, setup programs, memory management, sound card selection, virtual drive mounting, or any other roadblock. Just like on Steam or GOG, you can search for the game you want to play, double-click the box art, and the game launches. Users can check out screenshots, short videos, scans of the box and media artwork, and even read the instruction manuals.

An optional 220 gigabyte media pack is also available. It's not necessary to run any of the games, but it does include a bevy of magazines, books, soundtracks, interviews, strategy guides, and other goodies to maximize your enjoyment of all the software you've just found at your fingertips. eXoDOS preserves not just the games themselves, but also the history surrounding those games so anyone interested can explore the larger context surrounding these titles in a one-stop-shop style. And eXoDOS is just the tip of the iceberg.

There's [eXoAppleIIGS](https://www.retro-exo.com/appleIIGS.html), an 8 gigabyte archive of software for the Apple II line of personal computers.

Or how about [eXoWin3X](https://www.retro-exo.com/win3x.html), a 345 gigabyte archive of around 1,100 pieces of Windows software from the pre-Win95 era.

Maybe you don't give a fig for modern games and all their fancy graphics, and you'd like to go back to the text-based era, when Infocom was king, and all you needed to save the day was a brass lantern, an elvish sword, and a desire to match wits with a devious developer with a penchant for obtuse puzzles. Say hello to [eXoIF](https://www.retro-exo.com/if.html), a 30 gigabyte archive of over 2,000 text adventures for a whole slew of different home computers and mainframe types.

Or maybe you think text adventures suck, and the best gaming era came when LucasArts was doing their thing with games like *The Secret of Monkey Island* and *Full Throttle*. If so, you'll be happy to learn that [eXoDREAM ](https://www.retro-exo.com/dreamm.html) exists to let you relive all those classics.

Or maybe you're like me, and there are a number of games from your childhood you'd love to revisit, but they were released for the Windows 95/98/Me platform and don't play well with more modern, 64-bit operating systems. If that's the case, you're definitely going to want to keep an eye on the eXo team's latest release, [eXoWin9X](https://www.retro-exo.com/win9x.html), which first rolled out earlier this year and offers access to over 600 games from the first three years of this particular era in gaming, with more to come as the team gets them one-click ready. Incidentally, *Beavis & Butthead in: Virtual Stupidity* is included, in case you were wondering.

## Wait a minute: aren't you endorsing piracy and copyright infringement on a massive scale?
___

<center>![pirate-flag-9261083_1280.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/modernzorker/23sxUzZnqUpvL7uyEN7UiVFbLCUEHo3fcKPFaNFTGBZQ9FZyvsexrqspPYTnwAfXgWCDz.jpg)
*Who, me?* (Source: [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/illustrations/pirate-flag-jolly-roger-9261083/))</center>


Believe it or not, the honest answer is 'no'. I don't want to encourage illegal activities in the slightest. If there is some other, legal way that I, or anybody else, can play any of these games or systems, then I recommend doing exactly that. Pay the ten bucks to be able to play all those *Doom* games on GOG. Drop $15 to own the remasters of those first three *Tomb Raider* games. I encourage anyone and everyone to play original games on original hardware whenever and wherever such things are possible.

But that's also easy for me to say. I'm the nerd who owns several thousand retro games and a dozen classic systems, all in working order, to play them on. Most of the rest of the world is nowhere near as lucky as I am.

So I want to remind my readers that over 80% of our gaming history is, for all intents and purposes, lost. It's inaccessible due to scarcity or price, languishing in copyright hell because the company that owns the rights doesn't even know what they own, or simply aren't interested in investing the time and money to bring it back to life. And that's just talking about normal, single-player titles without an online component. Do you want to play something like *The Crew*, or *The Matrix Online*, or some other piece of 'games-as-live-service' content where the servers were shut down, and even if you still have the physical media you bought and paid for, you can't do anything with them?

Hey, just a thought, but how about we...

# <center>[Stop Killing Games!](https://www.stopkillinggames.com/en)</center>

...while we're at it?

Nope, say the majority of game publishers. Buy something new. Buy something different. Wait until we remake it. Give us more money for something you won't be able to use in the future, unless we think there's more money to be made in re-releasing it, and then you can buy it again. At least until we tell the storefronts to stop selling it. Because we can do that too, you know.

Want to take a few laps around the track in *Gran Turismo 3: A-Spec* with a friend to relive your college days? It shouldn't be that hard, right? *Gran Turismo 3* was the second-highest selling PS2 title of all time, barely edged out by the franchise behemoth that is *Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas*. It sold fifteen million copies, and routinely shows up on lists of the best games ever made. Surely, *surely* a game that huge, that popular, is easily and cheaply accessible on Sony's digital storefront, right?

You already know the answer to this. You didn't even have to load up the PlayStation store.

Buy yourself a working PS2, a controller, a memory card, a Composite-to-HDMI switch, and a copy of the game off the second-hand market. What, you don't *want* to spend a couple hundred bucks to play *Gran Turismo 3: A-Spec*? 'Sorry', shrugs Sony, 'our hands are tied. Copyright law. Trademark law. Intellectual property, licensing rights, you know the routine. Would if we could, and all that.'

These games all belong to a historical legacy. Even if they are terrible (maybe even *especially* if they are terrible), they are worthy of preservation, if for no other reason than so they can be used as an example to future game makers of what *not* to do. But unlike other forms of media, ours is not set up for preservation and access, but rather deprecation and depletion. Even the most well-cared-for PlayStation will eventually stop working. The connectors in even the most carefully-maintained *Super Mario Bros.* cartridge will eventually corrode. The people who worked so diligently to create the software and hardware that we hold sacred in our memories will not live forever. We do them no honor by allowing their works to degrade, to fall out of circulation, to become forgotten, to get locked behind an increasingly-expensive paywall called \

.

If the only way to be a part of the solution is to become a problem in the eyes of the people who will not or cannot do anything to mitigate the issue, then our cultural memories, our cultural history, have, in essence, become crimes waiting to happen. Emulators, ROM sites, and projects like Retro-eXo are both the past and the future of our hobby.

Whether the game publishers like it or not.

body.title: Starker Auftakt: Deutschland feiert einen deutlichen Sieg beim WM-Debüt 2026
body.body:
Die deutsche Nationalmannschaft hat ihr erstes Spiel bei der FIFA-Weltmeisterschaft 2026 mit einem überzeugenden Erfolg gestartet. Gegen den WM-Neuling Curaçao setzte sich das Team von Bundestrainer Julian Nagelsmann klar durch und schickte ein starkes Signal an die Konkurrenz in Gruppe E.

Die DFB-Elf dominierte das Spiel von Beginn an im Houston Stadium. Mit einer Mischung aus erfahrenen Routiniers wie Manuel Neuer im Tor und jungen Talenten wie Jamal Musiala, Florian Wirtz und Kai Havertz spielte Deutschland druckvoll und kombinationssicher. Bereits in der ersten Halbzeit fielen mehrere Treffer, darunter Tore von Felix Nmecha und Nico Schlotterbeck. Curaçao gelang zwar ein Ehrentreffer, doch die deutsche Mannschaft behielt die Kontrolle.

In der zweiten Halbzeit baute Deutschland den Vorsprung weiter aus. Kai Havertz verwandelte einen Elfmeter, und Musiala krönte eine starke Leistung mit einem weiteren Tor. Am Ende stand ein deutlicher Sieg auf dem Spielbericht – Berichte sprechen von einem 7:1 oder 4:1-Ergebnis, je nach Quelle, in jedem Fall eine klare Angelegenheit.

### Nagelsmanns Strategie geht auf
Bundestrainer Julian Nagelsmann setzte auf eine flexible 4-2-3-1-Formation, die sowohl defensive Stabilität als auch offensive Durchschlagskraft bot. Besonders auffällig waren die Debütanten und jungen Spieler wie Nathaniel Brown, die nahtlos ins Team passten. Neuer zeigte seine gewohnte Klasse und hielt den Kasten lange sauber. Der Sieg ist der erste WM-Auftaktsieg für Deutschland seit 2014 und weckt große Hoffnungen auf ein erfolgreiches Turnier.

Curaçao, das kleinste Land, das je an einer WM teilnimmt, zeigte Kampfgeist und feierte sein Debüt mit Stolz. Die Inselnation von rund 150.000 Einwohnern begeisterte mit leidenschaftlichem Spiel und erhielt viel Anerkennung, auch von den deutschen Fans.

### Ausblick auf die Gruppe E
Mit diesem Erfolg startet Deutschland optimal in die Gruppe E. Nächste Gegner sind die Elfenbeinküste (20. Juni in Toronto) und Ecuador (25. Juni in New York/New Jersey). Die Mannschaft hat gezeigt, dass sie bereit ist, um den fünften WM-Titel zu kämpfen.

Die Stimmung in der deutschen Mannschaft und bei den mitgereisten Fans ist euphorisch. Nach enttäuschenden Auftritten in früheren Turnieren könnte 2026 das Jahr der Rückkehr an die Weltspitze werden. „Wir haben heute ein starkes Zeichen gesetzt“, sagte Nagelsmann nach dem Spiel. „Aber es ist erst der Anfang.“

body.title: LLMs in medicine: from the USMLE benchmark to the real consulting room
body.body:
OpenAI's o3 scores 96% on MedQA — the American medical licensing exam (USMLE). GPT-5 scores 73% on HealthBench. In April 2026, a study by Harvard Medical School and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, published with repercussion on NPR, concluded that an OpenAI reasoning model equaled or surpassed physicians in diagnostic accuracy for real patient cases. These numbers are real. But there is a gap between benchmarks and clinical practice that the industry has not yet solved — and understanding this gap is more important than any individual score.

What medical benchmarks measure
-------------------------------

MedQA is a multiple-choice exam with 4 options per question, based on the USMLE question bank. Newly graduated physicians pass with 65%. Experienced physicians typically score 85-90%. o3 scores 96%.

The criticism of MedQA as a measure of real clinical competence is well founded: multiple-choice questions with 4 alternatives are the most favorable possible environment for language models. The model only needs to identify the most plausible answer among predefined options. In clinical practice, the options are not listed.

HealthBench, created by OpenAI with 262 physicians from 60 countries and 26 specialties, is an attempt to measure what really matters: quality of communication, handling of uncertainty, appropriateness of escalation (\

), safety in emergency triage, and precise clinical guidance across multiple conversation turns. GPT-5 scores 73% — impressive, but 23 points below the score on MedQA. This 23-point difference is the distance between knowing medicine and practicing it in a real context.

The knowledge-practice gap
--------------------------

A systematic review published in JMIR in 2025, covering 39 clinical LLM benchmarks, quantified the problem precisely. Diagnostic accuracy falls from 82% in traditional clinical vignettes to 62.7% in multi-turn dialogues with patients — a drop of 19.3 percentage points. Only 5% of studies evaluated LLM performance on real patient data. Only 4 peer-reviewed studies documented real clinical implementation worldwide up to 2025.

The gap exists because clinical practice involves: incomplete information provided by the patient, symptoms that change over the course of the consultation, multiple simultaneous conditions, socioeconomic context that affects management, and the need to decide when to say \

and refer. None of these elements is present in multiple-choice questions.

The most deployed product: documentation, not diagnosis
-------------------------------------------------------

The medical AI product with the greatest penetration in 2026 is not a diagnostic assistant. It is Microsoft DAX Copilot (Nuance), a system that captures the conversation between physician and patient and automatically generates a draft clinical note.

The reason DAX Copilot reached more than 10 million clinical encounters when other medical AI products remain in pilot is simple: it does not make diagnoses. It captures what the physician said and did, and structures it into a clinical format. The physician reviews and signs. The error is not critical — it is just a poorly written note. The regulation is manageable. The value is immediate: 7 minutes saved per consultation, 50% less time on documentation after the consultation.

Hippocratic AI, specialized in agents for non-diagnostic tasks (discharge education, caregiver preparation, post-hospitalization follow-up), used the same logic: scaling off the radar of medical device regulation by not making diagnoses. The result is 1.8 million completed calls with 8.95/10 patient satisfaction.

The Harvard/Beth Israel case: what the study really says
--------------------------------------------------------

The study published in April 2026, which concluded that OpenAI's reasoning model \

deserves careful reading. It evaluated clinical cases presented as structured text to the model and to physicians under test conditions — without direct contact with the patient, without physical examination, without the ability to order additional tests. Under the conditions of the experiment, the model was more accurate.\n\nUnder the conditions of the experiment — not in real practice. The distinction matters. Physicians have access to information that text does not capture: the general appearance of the patient (the \

), the way they breathe, the result of the physical examination, the intuition accumulated over years of seeing how diseases present in atypical ways. None of these inputs were available to the physician or to the model in the study.\n\nThe result is valid and relevant. But it does not mean that LLMs should replace physicians. It means that, as a decision-support tool in specific contexts, the potential is real — and that the next 2 to 3 years will define what those contexts are.

body.title: Neutro
body.body:
This weekend, which is almost over, has been quite busy. But busy in terms of physical effort, not because I attended multiple events out and about.

I’ve spent three consecutive days waking up early to go to the only ATM that almost always has electricity. There are others near my house, but they never have power, so walking it is. Transportation doesn’t help, especially on weekends.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVAHWNgTiPjLSe9KP8WbazsfTzyodHKSRYMDxAMR1wR1T/img_20260613_wa0037.jpg)

---
The most pleasant day for me was Saturday. I went to visit my longtime friend without warning. It seems my instinct was right because she was preparing one of those feasts she knows how to make. Before arriving at her house, I decided to walk toward a small hill covered with pines nearby. I had always wanted to climb it but had never made up my mind.

With so much free time, I decided it was finally time to go up there, and it was definitely worth it. The view from there was extraordinary. The phone’s lens couldn’t capture at all what my eyes were seeing. The whole city could be seen from there. I felt like having a bit of wine and drinking it while enjoying that view.

---
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdn5JSs2j7qcyLhVYEF987ZSbgi9M7sE5P1X1B9bwMU5B/img_20260613_083633.jpg)

---
Once again my friend cooked chickpeas, but this time with many more ingredients than the last time. She was cooking with charcoal, but luckily, as I walked through the door, electricity appeared. The rest of the dishes were cooked in record time. After all that sun and walking, the food was enough fuel to finish the day.

---
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbxrsm6bySXbjDLhw4CDpETwvaXAdf2mvFpYgYoC3nFCt/img_20260613_100609.jpg)

---

Today, Sunday, I went back to the ATM. I handled a transfer for my uncle, who doesn’t know much about these “modern things.” Now I’m at home, watching how the sun stays hidden behind thin clouds, creating the same unbearable steam I mentioned several days ago. A neutral weekend for me. It wasn’t the best, but certainly not the worst either.

---

body.title: Relaxing On The River
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcZ85HZu2cF5S5y8oqT2imV7LhT5pjH7zu4QbW4AyakYr/hive_.jpg)
*This post is for #SublimeSunday is inspired by @c0ff33a and #BeautifulSunday is initiated by @ace108*
2 weeks ago, I spent my weekend away from home for 1200 km with my son and his family. Today, my wife, granddaughter, and I visited her hometown, about 500 km from our house. We went to visit my wife's mom. At first, I planned to go alone, but just before the trip, my wife decided to join me and we also decided to take our granddaughter with us.
[![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdVW7DsZuiDJ6iGdhPKfqcCAjxnYvdLqxxowsJpJaKyRF/20260613_043035489_ios.jpg)](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdVW7DsZuiDJ6iGdhPKfqcCAjxnYvdLqxxowsJpJaKyRF/20260613_043035489_ios.jpg) We arrived late on Friday evening, and we spent Saturday doing various things at Mom's place. She's 85 years old, but she's trying to show us that she can handle everything on her own, but it's really hard for her. Today at 5 a.m. I went to the Neya River to go fishing. I had about 2 hours to go fishing. I have not been to this place for 2 years and the goal of my fishing was the chub. I completed this minimum program, I found this guy exactly in the place where I planned. Of course, I didn't take him with me, I let him go back into the river. I always release chubs for a number of reasons: they don't taste good, they have a lot of bones, they grow slowly. This fish is interesting to catch, it resists it very much. During the trip to my son, we also went fishing with him and he caught a chub. I convinced him that he needed to be released back.
[![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQsCzX51GuPNDdVgn2ax8JqBcdY9GvRcmM9crDqCESdZX/20260611_1.jpg)](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQsCzX51GuPNDdVgn2ax8JqBcdY9GvRcmM9crDqCESdZX/20260611_1.jpg) I returned from fishing, the girls were still asleep, so I went for a walk towards the crossing of the Unzha River. I was in this place at the end of April, but then the water level was high and now I wanted to look at the river.
[![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcMtxbizyN64z1EroMBgpVZ5KCPwAeHVCNv2jakHES4RM/20260611_2.jpg)](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcMtxbizyN64z1EroMBgpVZ5KCPwAeHVCNv2jakHES4RM/20260611_2.jpg)
[![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTWArm7ZexzYNECBtAuaMxYcKhYRRDhnyfCmko2EMSHDj/20260611_18.jpg)](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTWArm7ZexzYNECBtAuaMxYcKhYRRDhnyfCmko2EMSHDj/20260611_18.jpg)
[![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPBLzwuCye2uxcaXaUMcdjxstbx72t8hNG4CzpQXhGVk4/20260611_17.jpg)](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPBLzwuCye2uxcaXaUMcdjxstbx72t8hNG4CzpQXhGVk4/20260611_17.jpg) It's 8 a.m., there's silence on the river, a great place to bring your wife and granddaughter here so they can walk on the water. Just to walk around, because they don't have swimsuits, and we didn't plan on swimming. The temperature here has been around +30 degrees for more than a week and there is no rain. At home, it rained periodically all week and the temperature was about +23.
[![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdxznRKvmb5ySxWVMXhxeULHyAFXK2xam3P7seqBzkb2W/20260611_12.jpg)](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdxznRKvmb5ySxWVMXhxeULHyAFXK2xam3P7seqBzkb2W/20260611_12.jpg) After lunch, at about 3 p.m., we arrived at this beach again. Oh, there are already vacationers here. It turned out that my wife had never been to this place. When she was young, she and her friends went swimming in another place. Actually, we realized that she had already forgotten the surroundings of the city. By the way, did I say it was Makariev? I've already told you about this city. I love this ancient city. It stands apart from the railway and therefore there is no heavy industry in it, only enterprises of the timber industry. It is pleasant to relax in this city: fishing, hiking, forest, mushrooms, berry.
[![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRgVdfwxgKUydGmbpeTXheRaeqy3zorPuaTUEvcuAxP3J/20260611_9.jpg)](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRgVdfwxgKUydGmbpeTXheRaeqy3zorPuaTUEvcuAxP3J/20260611_9.jpg)
[![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYsPAhC1MGSRzp2vrYrNEmp1amYgjsRvQcE1GAoRXizPd/20260611_10.jpg)](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYsPAhC1MGSRzp2vrYrNEmp1amYgjsRvQcE1GAoRXizPd/20260611_10.jpg) Who is more happy about the river - a grandmother or a granddaughter? In a couple of weeks, the water in the river will decrease even more and the beach will become bigger, the river will become narrower. Then you can even try to leave the spinning under the bushes on the opposite shore. Although, there is a lot of pressure on the fish in this place. I saw fishermen in this place, closer to the ferry.
[![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTUJZh89enu6yKGYLfqQubAnEDM2E3N5sE5wQWA7SGQiJ/20260611_11.jpg)](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTUJZh89enu6yKGYLfqQubAnEDM2E3N5sE5wQWA7SGQiJ/20260611_11.jpg)
[![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRGLTacfdgWXoHNoTqEundua3iiefkpcwLGmvEsk3Qg14/20260611_16.jpg)](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRGLTacfdgWXoHNoTqEundua3iiefkpcwLGmvEsk3Qg14/20260611_16.jpg) It's an old ferry. I realized that it's not working at the moment.
[![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcg5FnHoGaXExTyxN2WaNmCRMg2nHiwyAsFs6yypVGMR6/20260611_15.jpg)](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcg5FnHoGaXExTyxN2WaNmCRMg2nHiwyAsFs6yypVGMR6/20260611_15.jpg) People stayed swimming on the river, and we had to get ready to go home. That's why we left the river. By the way, today, when we were driving home, we met a mother moose on the side of the road, and the moose was standing at the edge of the forest and waiting for my mother. The sun was shining in my face, the glass wasn't very clean, so the DVR video turned out to be bad, I can't show it. Moose in the rays of the setting sun from afar at first seemed to me like plywood, but then they came to life and quietly went into the forest. I had previously slowed down the speed.
![imagehive1.png](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYbD5H7vX4jU6TiFbUKDRt1VvurE3tmJNBgpmF4jxEYkW/imagehive1.png)
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdnr6CyN4mtmwyYLY8pARGkVVgkXFcvLZv62JTVLhKesF/image.png)
***Don’t Worry, Be Happy*** (C) Bobby McFerrin
Text & Photography by @apnigrich
With love @apnigrich
Good luck and have fun

body.title: Sad tale  : My Actifit Report Card: June 14 2026
body.body:
![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/6795bc5f-e4b4-4abd-85c0-1be70cc76b62.jpg) Nature can seem cruel sometimes 😔. We learned today from local environmental staff that one of our swans at Ifield Mill Pond has passed. It is not known how this happened, but tests are being done on the bird by environmental authorities. There are still two cygnets surviving as you can see in my pictures, amongst other wild fowl. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/fa99c5be-5c69-40d3-a520-2b0c8de49b11.jpg) There are so many geese here now. Mostly canada geese, but a few other types, such as Egyptian geese. This lake is so nice to walk around. Especially with the suspended platform across the middle. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/e6b5fc03-1489-4764-84a6-8008945d0627.jpg) ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/61b5cffb-140b-4bec-a9d6-9b367af7b357.jpg) Even with such sad news, we know that nature has resilience to recover from setbacks like this and future years will show this.

body.title: Seasonal fruits and cereals caught my fancy
body.body:
‎Towards afternoon today, I had a walk along the streets of our town. On my way,  I saw and captured this trending pleasant cereal that everyone is enjoying. 
‎

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaz9BicnDtcuSFehkwHwZqRe1hxFrVpKnUgPPUpxzRizU/1781469476613.jpg)

‎The ears of grain up there is known as maize or corn 🌽. This is it's season and people are already making huge amount of moneys with it. For example, the one you're seeing above is for sale. 
‎..........................................................................
‎On the same place, I saw and captured this seasonal fruit.
‎
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbj5AnbNt9Mdvw3tut1HkiGYgibv3pP6sgsxd3DohdXQ5/1781469501217.jpg)

‎Locally, it is popularly known as Ugiri or Ujiri. One famous thing about this particular seasonal fruit is that it possess multiple advantages. You can leak and enjoy it's outer layers. Then, crack the kernel, and you will see ogbono. Ogbono is used in preparing draw soup. Also, the kernel chaff can as well serve as firewood.
‎...........................................................................
‎Next was avocado pear. 
‎
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXo1BBoGZWayYALKxZCtZzGEhidKEZhk8sgPdN1DK1U4y/1781469518659.jpg)

‎It is another seasonal fruit that I can't joke with. Because of my love and passion for avocado, (Ube bekee), I bought one heap from the seller.
‎......................................................................................................................................................
‎
‎You may be wondering where I was heading to when I captured all the above pictures. I was on my way to a mechanic vulcanizer to repair my mom's business vehicle. 
‎
‎So, it was the avocado pear (Ube) that caught my fancy and attracted me into buying some.
‎
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWhf5v2vwfJPDRJggctjoWSscv8v7SuWPAqtcffSCAGWQ/1781469558333.jpg)

‎I spent hours at the mechanic. He arranged the vehicle and I left with happiness although I spent hours there waiting for my turn.
‎
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU5hwGDXodhrR1g5D9s575Ent98vfRhLWK1AAN6ck5WSA/1781469573768.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmP3zVytFggpSezK6QG7QL1bMnHvzhhRX5oNFqdEm12x88/1781469573959.jpg)

‎Thanks for going through my today's blog.
