links.title: SIWES (STUDENTS INDUSTRIAL WORK EXPERIENCE SCHEME) FEELS LIKE JOB HUNTING
links.body: alt=\

/> Hello freewriters ! 👋 My first semester exams are finally over, and honestly, I feel relieved. After weeks of reading and studying, assignments, tests, practicals, and trying to survive the pressure that comes with being a student, it feels good to have crossed that stage. Finally 😁 Now, my attention has shifted to something completely different. SIWES (STUDENTS INDUSTRIAL WORK EXPERIENCE SCHEME) mandatory for Science students in my school. For those who have gone through it before, you probably understand what I'm talking about. At least you might have had an experience. For those who haven't, SIWES is supposed to be a period where students gain practical experience in their field of study. Sounds simple, right? Hmmm Well, finding a place to do it is a different story. At this point, searching for a SIWES placement feels a lot like searching for a job opportunity.😂 You prepare your documents, print your Siwes introductory letter, update your CV, and start moving from one organization to another hoping for a positive response. Some places tell you they are no longer accepting students. Probably because their slots are filled up. Others ask you to come back later. Some collect your documents and leave you waiting for a response that may or may not come. Over the past few weeks, I've been making inquiries, sending applications from one organisation to the other, and reaching out to people who might be able to help. The process has taught me something important: opportunities rarely come to those who sit and wait. It comes to those who act. I've realized that sometimes you have to keep showing up even when the outcome is uncertain. You just have to show up regardless of the circumstances. There were moments when I thought I had found a place, only for things not to work out as expected. There were also moments when I felt discouraged seeing how competitive the process can be. But instead of giving up, I decided to keep trying.
alt=\

/>

One thing this experience has shown me is the value of networking. It can never be overemphasised. A simple conversation can open a door that months of searching cannot. Sometimes the person who eventually helps you is someone you never expected.

As a Science Laboratory Technology student specializing in Biochemistry, I hope to secure a placement where I can learn practical laboratory skills and gain experience that will be useful for my future career. Beyond completing a school requirement, I want this period to be an opportunity for growth and learning.

For now, the search continues.

I'm choosing to stay optimistic and keep pushing forward. After all, every student looking for SIWES is hoping for the same thing, a chance to learn, grow, and gain real world experience.

If you've ever searched for a SIWES placement, internship, or even a job, then you probably understand the feeling. The waiting, the uncertainty, the follow ups, and the hope that the next application might be the one that works out.

Thankfully, first semester exams are behind me, and now it's time to focus on what comes next. It's time to build.

Hopefully, before long, I'll be sharing good news about finally securing a placement. Until then, I'll keep submitting applications, making calls, following up, and doing my best not to get discouraged.

And honestly, if SIWES is this stressful, I can only imagine what actual job hunting feels like. 😂 We hope for the best always.

Have you ever struggled to find a SIWES placement, internship, or job opportunity? How did you eventually get through it? I'd love to hear your experience in the comments.

> This question , if I do like to celebrate my birthdays, of course, I do really like celebrating my birthday. Birthdays are special because they give us a chance to stop and think about life, every birthday reminds me that I am still here , I am still alive and still looking forward to days. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcjSQeVBtJoe3cHX9Q1dXTfN39svzq25voeiH4VgG9VXm/1781443675642.png) I also like celebrating the birthdays of people around me, It is nice to make someone feel loved on their special day I do not need to do something expensive, sometimes a simple message or a phone call can make their day special. When it comes to my own birthday, yes I like to do something nice for myself, i do not need a party with plenty people, sometimes I just want some time to myself to relax and think about the year. This year birthday was not how I planned to spend it but still it was my birthday whichever way it went, so I stayed home because I did not have money to go out to celebrate my birthday the way I wanted, hmm, yes I was a little disappointed. There were a few things I wanted to do, nothing too extravagant, just something small that would allow me enjoy the day and create good memories for myself, but life happens, and sometimes priorities come first. At first, I felt a little bad about it, you know how birthdays come with expectations sometimes, you imagine how the day will go, what you would like to do, where you would like to go, and then reality decides to take a different route. But after thinking about it, I realized something, the most important thing is that I was alive to see another birthday, not everyone gets that opportunity, the fact that I was healthy enough to celebrate another year of life is already something worth being grateful for. Besides Birthdays are not going anywhere, there are more birthdays to come, life has its ups and downs, some years are better than others, some birthdays are celebrated big and others are quiet, that does not make them any less special. For my birthday I would like to have some time to myself , I would like to go to somewhere nice and enjoy good food, I just want to relax and appreciate myself for that day, and dust reflect, I want to do things that makes me happy. I do not need anything complicated, I just want to be happy and grateful, see, birthdays are not about parties or spending plenty money, they are about celebrating life, so even though this year's birthday was not what I wanted I am still thankful for it. I am thankful for life, i am thankful for growth, I am thankful for another chance to keep moving, I am thankful because I know there are more birthdays ahead of me to celebrate. *** --- ***Image Is Modified With Chatpt*** ![1000573341.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/treasuree/23s9c1MqSx1HhT1yGGJrzoEBDBcyBewncBKsKPuN1kVPXLcoQ7uNM77SbgWqKK6ErUSTg.png)

links.title: [테이스팀#660] 히로시마현대미술관에서 만난 작은 쉼표, Cafe KAZE
links.body:
![IMG_1541.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeDu68ewtEDxE3ZEGfBKU4H9ppcCEYo8oxK8AVMLCYSnw/IMG_1541.jpeg)


히로시마현대미술관(Hiroshima MOCA)을 둘러본 뒤 1층에 있는 Cafe KAZE에 들렀다.

이름처럼 ’KAZE(바람)’를 테마로 한 공간인데, 미술관에서는 이 카페를 “일상 속에 스며드는 기분 좋은 바람 같은 존재”로 소개한다. 전시를 감상한 뒤 잠시 쉬어가는 공간이자, 접시 위의 음식 또한 하나의 작은 예술 작품처럼 경험하길 바라는 의도가 담겨 있다고 한다. 

통유리 너머로 히지야마 공원의 초록이 보이고, 전시의 여운을 이어가기 좋은 차분한 분위기였다. 미술관 입장권이 없어도 이용할 수 있다는 점도 매력적이다.

주문한 메뉴는 기간 한정 메뉴인 북유럽식 오픈 샌드위치와 레모네이드.

훈제연어와 마스카르포네 치즈를 듬뿍 올린 오픈 샌드위치 위에는 오렌지와 링곤베리, 그리고 딜이 아낌없이 올라간다.

부드럽고 바삭한 빵에 훈제연어의 감칠맛, 마스카르포네의 부드러움, 오렌지의 산뜻함이 더해져 생각보다 훨씬 깔끔한 맛을 낸다. 특히 연어 위를 가득 덮은 딜 향이 인상적이었다. 흔히 접하는 샌드위치보다 훨씬 향긋하고 산뜻한 느낌.

곁들여 나온 당근라페도 좋았다. 레몬 껍질이 들어가 있어 상큼함이 한층 살아난다.

무엇보다 기억에 남은 건 계절 샐러드.

한국에서는 쉽게 보기 힘든 허브와 잎채소가 섞여 있었는데, 씹을 때마다 풀향과 허브향이 은은하게 퍼진다. 단순히 곁들임 채소가 아니라 접시 전체의 향과 분위기를 완성하는 역할을 하는 느낌이었다.

미술관에 있는 카페여선지 음식도 하나의 작품처럼 보였다. 화려하지는 않지만 재료 각각의 향과 맛을 살린 구성.

미술관 카페라고 해서 단순한 휴게 공간 정도를 예상했는데, 오히려 히지야마 공원의 초록과 현대미술관의 분위기를 가장 편안하게 즐길 수 있는 장소였다.

히지야마 언덕에 오른 뒤 잠시 쉬어가고 싶다면, Cafe KAZE는 꽤 좋은 선택인 듯 하다. (단 하나의 선택이기도..)

links.body: 1/5 🧵 Alex Freeman announced himself on the biggest stage like he’d been there for years. In a 4-1 USMNT win over Paraguay, the 21-year-old wasn’t just solid — he was the calm, two-way engine that quietly held the whole right side together. Unsung hero is exactly right.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The headline result was historic: the U.S. scored 4 goals in a World Cup match for the first time, and Folarin Balogun bagged the first American World Cup brace since 1930. Paraguay’s own manager admitted the U.S. beat them tactically, technically, and physically. That’s not a lucky win. That’s a statement.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 Freeman’s impact was in the details that win games. He won 9 of 14 duels, helped start the sequence for the opener with a smart pass into Weston McKennie, and added an assist on Gio Reyna’s goal. In Pochettino’s setup, he’s doing a brutal hybrid job — part right center back, part right back, expected to defend hard and still join the attack. For a player this young, that level of composure is rare.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 The other big takeaway: the US back line looked far steadier than many expected. Chris Richards reportedly completed 83 of 83 passes — absurdly clean for a World Cup match — while Tim Ream hit 93% of his passes and helped progression from the back. Yes, both had a hand in the one Paraguay goal, so it wasn’t flawless, but overall the defensive unit looked much less shaky than the pre-match anxiety suggested.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 5/5 🧵 A few lingering notes: McKennie influenced the game more than the box score shows, repeatedly finding space and linking well with Pulisic and Tillman. The win also shouldn’t be shrugged off just because it came against Paraguay — this is a side that beat Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay in qualifying. The one real concern is Tyler Adams’ yellow card, because another in the group stage would trigger a knockout-round suspension. Big win, but not quite stress-free. 📎 [Source](https://nypost.com/2026/06/13/sports/alex-freeman-was-usmnts-unflappable-unsung-hero-in-world-cup-debut/)\n\n#threadstorm
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 1/4 🧵 Aldon Smith’s story ended the way sports fans hate most: way too early, with a reminder that elite talent and a stable life are not the same thing. The headline is simple and brutal — the former 49ers All-Pro linebacker has died at 36.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 大伟哥你家两少爷还在执行阅读奖励吗？ 嘿嘿\n主角电视好像挺火的，我还没看过，看大伟哥分析的文字感觉挺有意思
links.author: neithya

links.body: 2/4 🧵 The core news: the 49ers announced Smith’s death on Saturday. No cause was provided in the article. San Francisco’s statement leaned on two things people remembered immediately — how dominant he was from day one, and how big his personality was off the field, especially that “infectious smile” the team highlighted.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/4 🧵 As a player, Smith was a monster early. Drafted No. 7 overall out of Missouri, he finished second in Defensive Rookie of the Year voting in 2011, became an All-Pro in 2012, and piled up 33.5 sacks plus 103 tackles in his first two seasons. That’s not just “promising” — that’s franchise-wrecking edge rusher stuff. He became one of the NFL’s most feared defenders and helped power the 49ers to the Super Bowl in the 2012 season.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/4 🧵 The harder part of the story is that his career also became a case study in how off-field issues can derail even rare talent. The article notes multiple suspensions and arrests, including a 2014 suspension for violating the NFL substance abuse policy and later DUI arrests that led to his release from San Francisco. Smith himself later admitted the gap: he said he was good at playing football, but “wasn’t a good football player,” meaning he lacked the discipline, direction, and stability the job demanded. He later had stints with the Raiders, a 2020 return with the Cowboys, and a Seahawks signing that ended after another arrest. In the end, this is a piece about brilliance, lost momentum, and a life cut short. 📎 [Source](https://nypost.com/2026/06/13/sports/aldon-smith-all-pro-49ers-linebacker-dead-at-36/)\n\n#threadstorm
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 1/5 🧵 The Knicks finally did it. **First title in 53 years**, and they closed it out the hard way: coming back again, on the road, with Jalen Brunson delivering a flat-out legendary performance. New York beat San Antonio **94-90** in Game 5, and this one instantly goes into franchise mythology.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 Brunson was the whole storm. He dropped **45 points** in the title clincher and took over in waves: 8 straight in the second quarter to cut a 16-point hole, 14 in the third as the Knicks kept clawing back, then **13 straight in the fourth** to flip another double-digit deficit into a championship. That’s not “good game” stuff. That’s career-defining, statue-energy stuff.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 What makes it wilder is how this series looked on paper. The Knicks trailed by **10+ points in every game** of the Finals and led for just **23.6% of the series**, which is an absurdly low number for a champion. But that was the identity: survive the punches, own crunch time, and let the Spurs make the mistake first. San Antonio often controlled stretches; New York controlled the moments that actually mattered.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 The supporting cast wasn’t exploding offensively in the clincher either. Karl-Anthony Towns fought foul trouble and scored just **2 points**. Bridges had **14**, Hart **13**, Anunoby **11**, and the bench gave only **9**. So while this postseason was framed as a full team effort, the closeout became Brunson’s personal masterpiece. By the final buzzer, any Finals MVP debate was dead and buried.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 5/5 🧵 The bigger point: this wasn’t just a championship, it was an exorcism. The old banners from **1969-70** and **1972-73** finally have company. For generations of Knicks fans, a title was basically inherited trauma wrapped in nostalgia. Now it’s real, permanent, and attached to a new face of the franchise in Brunson. New York isn’t chasing history anymore — it just made some. 📎 [Source](https://nypost.com/2026/06/13/sports/knicks-win-first-nba-championship-in-53-years/)\n\n#threadstorm

links.title: Item left behind.
links.body:
<Sub>[source](https://pixabay.com/photos/road-stop-overgrown-abandoned-2609200/)<sub>











![1000230925.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oyebolu/23t7FH5utEkyquTihfUcjAN9uuMtRfzCp8cJLxPZKjpjZTSpQRPctBaMGXt5Da5LAmMWp.jpg)








What is the secret about the name that the man walking by just called you?

Mr Foley asked as he selected the fried pork meat, which exuded fat and looked sumptuous, that he was purchasing.

“TIIJAYY,” I answered, and smirked, knowing that that name held a heavy significance then.

“ That was my nickname as a wild teen and the embodiment of that name is an item I left behind” I concluded.

The butcher wrapped the products we bought and gave them to us but as we were about to move towards our actual position which was just a few steps away.

“ TIIJAYY!” We heard again from a distance, a moving car as it passed, and to our surprise, the cat stopped,  reversed, and wound down.

“ Is it really you?”
The voice from the car pulled me back and I took an excuse from Mr Foley that I would meet him at the spot then I moved closer to the car.

I looked slowly, “ Yes, I think so, this is Samson” I ruminated.

Samson sat there, staring at me like he had seen a ghost from a life he no longer believed existed but still lived in it.

“ It’s been …. what? Ten years?” He said opening his bulging eyes which never changed to look at me from head to toe.

“ Something like that,” I replied looking back to confirm that Mr Foley was not out of reach as he concentrated on unwrapping what was on his table carefully.

Samson laughed awkwardly, “You sound like you have forgotten the number in counting” he uttered.

“ I have,” I replied simply.

A silence stretched between us and as I wanted to turn back, he said, “ I didn't think I would ever see you again”

“ I didn't think about it either” I replied and I noticed that wasn't what he was expecting and it made him pause.

 He muttered, “Wow you really moved on” 

I nodded and replied, “ a long time ago”

He looked at me carefully like he was searching for something familiar but couldn't see it. “ Do you ever think about knowing the truth of what had happened then,

Do you ever think about Jane and her decisions back then?” he uttered.

I shook my head, “knowing won't change anything and the truth is not mine anymore, it belongs to the past,

And for Jane, I still remember her but it no longer stays with me in the same way you mean. I said firmly.

“ You really don't feel anything deeply like before” he asked almost in disbelief.

I thought for a moment and answered,“ You are right but I am still a feeler, 

It is just that that was a long time ago and the wind moved between us and so many things had happened” I uttered.

Samson nodded slowly like he was finally understanding something he didn't want to accept.

“ So what now?” He asked.

I smiled lightly, “Wish you the best, friend” I replied leaving him and my past that he was still trying to carry.

Getting to the spot, Mr Foley said as his eyes were stuck on the television he was watching, “You are pretty famous around, 
Some people here knew you as a teen” he concluded in amazement.

I smiled and muttered, “That is a reality check for them because if growing is important ;

Then what used to matter won't anymore,
As people change likewise I have” I took a bite from the fried pork meat and continued,

“For instance, Samson, the man who called me from the car earlier was a friend who wanted to tell me a past truth but who cares“ I concluded.

“ Are you sure you don't want to know deep down” Mr Foley said after a sip from a cup he held.

I answered, “Living better is now, and the best is just a step ahead,

My past was no longer mine to carry as I had outgrown what once was,

So I placed it down gently, thanking it for what it once meant,

Though, I left it there not because I forgot but because I accepted it had ended,

And what I carried forward matters more than what I left behind” I concluded.

“ Well said” Mr Foley replied with a smile and “ don't let us forget why we are here” he concluded and we laughed at the dribbling skill that was displayed in the football match we were watching on the television screen which later resulted in a goal and \
We shouted.

links.body: 1/5 🧵 India just made the crypto tax game a lot less fuzzy. The big number is **$104M in undeclared crypto income uncovered** after officials sent **44,000+ notices**. The real story isn’t the tax rate — it’s that India now has the machinery to match what people traded against what they reported. That changes behavior fast.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The enforcement engine is pretty simple and pretty brutal: exchanges, custodians, and wallet providers send **user-level transaction data** straight to the tax department. That data gets cross-checked against **Schedule VDA**, the section where Indians must report virtual digital asset gains. If your filing and your trade history don’t line up, the notice lands. No mystery, no shrugging, no “they’ll never know.”
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 India’s crypto tax structure is already heavy: **30% tax on VDA gains** plus **1% TDS** on eligible transfers. But the article’s key point is that high rates were only half the story. In earlier cycles, enforcement was patchy because reporting was fragmented. Now the feeds are live and automated, which means compliance just went from theoretical to operational. That’s the real escalation.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 The market effect is where it gets messy. Retail users and active traders now face a bookkeeping nightmare, especially if they moved assets across wallets, swaps, and multiple venues. The article argues this could push more activity away from centralized exchanges and toward **DEXs, peer-to-peer rails, and non-custodial setups**. That’s the absurd tension here: tighter surveillance on CeFi may improve collections, but it can also shove activity into places that are harder to police.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 5/5 🧵 The broader takeaway: India hasn’t “banned crypto by tax,” but it has built a real enforcement perimeter around centralized activity. That means local volumes may keep migrating even if the developer base stays strong. The next fight is obvious: whether the tax dragnet expands into DeFi and self-custody, or stays partial and leaves gaps. Either way, unreported crypto income in India is no longer hiding in the fog. 📎 [Source](https://blockchainreporter.net/indias-tax-net-pulls-in-104-million-in-undisclosed-crypto-gains-as-automated-oversight-takes-hold/)\n\n#threadstorm

links.body: 1/5 🧵 Bitget getting registered in Argentina isn’t just a box-checking exercise. It’s the bigger crypto trend in plain sight: exchanges can’t just parachute into hot markets anymore, grab users, and sort out compliance later. In Latin America, regulation is becoming the entry ticket.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The headline move: Bitget secured PSAV registration in Argentina under the CNV framework. That puts the exchange inside the country’s formal rules for virtual asset service providers. In simple terms, Bitget now has a recognized legal/compliance footing in one of the region’s busiest crypto markets.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 What does PSAV status actually mean? Mostly obligations, not a gold star. Bitget now falls under AML and counter-terror financing rules, with duties around customer ID, risk monitoring, suspicious activity reporting, and record-keeping. Important distinction: registration does **not** mean Argentina’s regulator is vouching for Bitget’s products, safety, or returns.

links.body: 1/5 🧵 Bitcoin’s sellers are getting tired — but that alone doesn’t restart the bull. The core point here is simple: **selling pressure has cooled off, yet real buying demand still hasn’t stepped up hard enough to confirm recovery**. BTC looks less like it’s bleeding out and more like it’s stuck in a waiting room.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The article leans heavily on the **Sell-side Risk Ratio**, which has dropped toward the lower realization band near **0.1%** after the brutal correction from roughly **$126k to $60k**. In plain English: investors are no longer locking in huge profits or panic losses at the same pace. That usually means the market has moved out of the most violent distribution phase. But it also signals **reduced economic activity**, not necessarily fresh bullish conviction.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 There’s a historical angle too. Big spikes in realized selling activity — above **1%** — lined up with major cycle tops like **2017** and **2021**. Now that metric has compressed, and current price behavior is starting to resemble the stabilization phases seen after the **2014, 2018, and 2022** bear markets. That’s cautiously constructive, but not exactly champagne-popping territory. It suggests BTC may be building a base, not launching yet.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 Under the surface, the stronger signal is **long-term holder behavior**. Long-Term Holder supply climbed to **16.46M BTC**, while stablecoin liquidity sits around **$315B**. That combination matters: patient holders are still accumulating, and there’s plenty of sidelined capital in the system. On top of that, **Open Interest near $47B** shows leverage is rebuilding — but carefully, not in full degenerate mode. So the structure says conviction is there, but the trigger is missing.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 5/5 🧵 That missing piece is **spot demand**. The article points to weakening bearish momentum in **Spot Taker CVD**, modest **ETF inflows of $85M**, and a **neutral Coinbase Premium Index**. Translation: sellers have backed off, but buyers haven’t grabbed the wheel. Even valuation metrics like **MVRV Z-Score around 0.37** and **STH-MVRV at 0.84** say BTC is stabilizing while short-term holders are still under pressure. Bottom line: **the worst selling may be over, but recovery needs stronger buyer participation to become real**. 📎 [Source](https://ambcrypto.com/bitcoin-selling-pressure-fades-but-btc-recovery-still-needs-this/)\n\n#threadstorm

links.title: Perfect Brawl in Fray 12, But ClaNFT Had to Settle for Fourth Place
links.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc6gdt9GDdhGURPp1qqCQgfDg5zDsdKATXNmGvMxsLGHv/thumbnail_brawl.png)


Greetings, Splinterlands warriors!

In this post, I’d like to share the story of my latest Brawl results that I just went through with the ClaNFT guild. Recently, Splinterlands has been quite busy introducing various new features and exciting announcements. Some of them I’ve even discussed in previous posts. It feels like the developers are really trying to keep the game fresh amid the increasingly crowded blockchain gaming scene.

And somehow, that positive energy seemed to carry over into my gameplay this week.

If in Modern mode some time ago I finally managed to break into the Gold League after being stuck in Silver for quite a while, then this Brawl result brought a similar sense of satisfaction. Not because our guild became champions, but because for the first time in a long while, I managed to complete my matches in Fray 12 without a single loss.

As usual, my teammates in ClaNFT once again entrusted me with Fray 12. It almost feels like a permanent address at this point. If there’s a letter from Brawl, it’s definitely sent to Fray 12 under my name.

In this Brawl, there were actually seven matches that I had to go through. Initially, I received one automatic win because one of the opposing guilds didn’t fill their slot. During the Brawl, it turned out there were two more opponents who didn’t submit their teams, so those matches ended with a fled status.

The rest, I had to fight for myself.

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTyzEw9kdEiLqpDTDF4wDisWctTKbfBR4Z3i8w9X4921B/my_battles.jpg)</center>


And this is the part that made me quite happy.

The four matches that were actually played, I managed to win through strategies and team selections that, in my opinion, went exactly as planned. No bad surprises, no misplacement of monsters that I usually only realize after the match ends. Everything felt smooth.

The final result was **8 wins and 0 losses**.

Honestly, seeing that number made me smile quite wide.

Unfortunately, Brawl is a team game. And like football, sometimes a striker can score a hat-trick, but the team still fails to become champions.

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUgkZSgga6JRTy4pjk6G8K7QbwSxyNrR3BmfoP7h2WnUp/all.png)</center>


Even though I swept all my matches, it was only enough to bring ClaNFT to fourth place. Overall, our guild collected **222 points** with **74 wins**.

The rewards we received were:

* 2,450 Merits for each member who fully participated
* 20,413 SPS in the form of staked SPS for players who own a Spellbook

Not a bad result at all. Still, after seeing my perfect personal record, I did hope the guild could place a bit higher.

But that’s Brawl. Sometimes you play very well, but your opponents play even better.

---

## A Battle That Taught Patience

Out of all the matches I played, there was one duel that I think is worth discussing.

This battle featured two teams that both relied on magic attacks. My opponent used the Earth element with Archon **Immortalis**, a figure well known for being troublesome for magic users because he grants Void to his team.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYpXGMrK2uAJWQraFnWW4gsWwdzRP69Ed7NZTxvgoNUKH/round_1.png)


As if that wasn’t enough, the opponent also brought **Goblin Psychic** as their main healer.

Seeing that situation, I chose a rather extreme defensive strategy.

I placed **Iziar** on the front line as a Taunt monster that also has Void. The goal was simple: draw all enemy attacks while reducing incoming magic damage.

But I knew one healer wouldn’t be enough.

So I prepared three sources of healing at once. One healer focused on keeping the front line alive, while the other two were tasked with sustaining the backline.

The result felt like a battle of endurance.

Each round moved slowly. Monsters fell one by one. Heal was answered with heal. Void met Void. It felt like two stubborn boxers refusing to go down.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQADapBnzvRJxzn2nLHqwoMgjcNHvvx7GJKcg8zG1wt7R/round_7.png)


The battle lasted until round seven before I finally secured the victory.

If you want to watch the full duel, you can check it here:
<center> 👉  [**LINK BATTLE**](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sm_9OZxihcPYNWG13ENYkOo?ref=rqr4)  👈</center>

For me, the biggest lesson was that not every match needs to be won with overwhelming offense. Sometimes patience, sustain, and defensive strength are the true keys to victory.

---

## Time to Open 10 Gladius Cases

There’s one piece of news that excites me even more than this Brawl result.

After saving for so long, my Merits have finally surpassed **20,000**. That means the long-awaited goal has finally been achieved. I now have enough Merits to open **10 Gladius Cases** at once.

Honestly, I can’t wait to see what cards I’ll get. Will there be a legendary? Will there be duplicates I can immediately level up?

One thing’s for sure, I’ll share the pack opening results in my next post. So stay tuned.

See you in the next arena, and may victory always be on your side.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXuXxp6GBhwB1HpXvoabLn8Dt8QaRKSe1WNYDzqX1v6Vk/chaos_logo.png)

Talk about Splinterlands,
If you haven't tried out this fantastic game called Splinterlands yet, I invite you to [**Join**](https://splinterlands.com?ref=rqr4).
It's free, but you'll need to invest in a beginning deck or buy gaming cards to gain real assets like cards and tokens. 

___


If you already joined the splinterlands, and are looking for a place to grow. We need **YOU**. We are a chill, social guild looking for a few more active members! If you think you might be a fit, join us in our [**Discord**](https://discord.gg/5u638vHPVh)

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZAXaBtYPQQcQ4fDb2DMaFETkzmZ5DNhevYHW4pANVaM2/banner.png)</center>

The flower in the picture is like a beautiful glimpse of that familiar form. Kalmi is basically a creeping plant. This plant grows without any care in water bodies, ponds, banks, or roadsides of Bangladesh. And its chest blooms with magical flowers with a light purple and white hue. The contrast between the deep purple center of the flower and the light color of the petals is truly eye-catching. Just as the Kalmi plant provides us with nutrition, its flowers also satisfy our eyes and minds. In today's busy lives, we often overlook these simple beauties. Amidst the crowd of expensive exotic flowers, the softness of these native wildflowers reminds us that True beauty is not always in grandeur; it is in simplicity. # Learn Ethical Hacking (#57) - IoT and Embedded Security - Hacking the Physical World

![leh-banner.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc2LpoeHUPesc4Dy8haRKLJgfuDY6UBKdc3sED8Dz3JH9/leh-banner.jpg)

### What will I learn

- **The IoT attack surface** -- why billions of connected devices are the largest unpatched vulnerability on earth;
- **Firmware analysis** -- extracting, unpacking, and reverse engineering device firmware to find hardcoded credentials and backdoors;
- **Hardware hacking basics** -- UART, JTAG, SPI interfaces and what they expose when you open the case;
- **Default credentials and hardcoded secrets** -- the vulnerability that refuses to die in embedded devices;
- **Network-based IoT attacks** -- UPnP exploitation, MQTT interception, Zigbee/Z-Wave attacks, and CoAP enumeration;
- **Shodan and Censys** -- search engines for finding exposed IoT devices at scale;
- **Industrial Control Systems (ICS/SCADA)** -- the terrifying intersection of IoT and critical infrastructure;
- Defense: network isolation, firmware updates, secure boot, and why most consumer IoT will never be secure.

### Requirements

- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- binwalk and Ghidra installed for firmware analysis;
- Optional: a cheap IoT device for hands-on testing (smart plug, IP camera);
- The ambition to learn ethical hacking and security research.

### Difficulty

- Intermediate/Advanced

### Curriculum (of the `Learn Ethical Hacking Series`):

### The IoT Security Problem -- Why It's Different

The technical vulnerabilities are the same ones we've seen throughout this series -- command injection, default credentials, missing encryption, unpatched software. ### Firmware Analysis -- Extracting the Device's Brain

Every IoT device runs firmware -- the software baked into the device's flash memory. Extracting and analyzing firmware is the single most effective IoT security assessment technique. You do not need physical access to the device if the manufacturer publishes firmware updates on their support page (and most of them do):

```bash
# Step 1: Obtain the firmware
# Option A: Download from manufacturer's website (firmware update section)
# Option B: Extract from the device via UART/JTAG/SPI (hardware access)
# Option C: Intercept an OTA update (network capture during update check)
# Many manufacturers host firmware as .bin, .img, or .zip on their CDN

# Step 2: Analyze the firmware image with binwalk
binwalk firmware.bin
# DECIMAL       HEXADECIMAL     DESCRIPTION
# 0             0x0             uImage header, size: 1048576
# 64            0x40            LZMA compressed data
# 1048576       0x100000        Squashfs filesystem, little endian, v4.0
# 2097152       0x200000        JFFS2 filesystem, little endian

# Step 3: Extract the filesystem
binwalk -e firmware.bin
cd _firmware.bin.extracted/squashfs-root/

# Step 4: Hunt for secrets
# Password files
cat etc/shadow         # password hashes -- often MD5 or even plaintext!
cat etc/passwd

# Configuration files with credentials
grep -r \
etc/\ngrep -r \
etc/\ngrep -r \
etc/\ngrep -r \
etc/ --include=\

# Find ALL configuration files and search them
find . -name \
-exec grep -l \
\nstrings usr/bin/management_daemon | grep -i \

# Look for private keys and certificates
find . -name \
-o -name \
-o -name \

# If you find TLS private keys: they are the SAME key on every device
# of this model. One key compromise = MITM every device worldwide.

# Step 5: Check for debug/backdoor services
grep -r \

etc/init.d/
# Many devices start telnet or SSH at boot with default credentials
```

### Hardware Hacking -- Opening the Case

Sometimes firmware is not available for download and you need to extract it from the device itself. This is where hardware hacking comes in. Opening the case and connecting to debug interfaces on the PCB (printed circuit board) gives you access that the manufacturer never intended:

```text
=== UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) ===

UART is a serial debug interface found on most IoT device PCBs.
It often provides a root shell with ZERO authentication.

How to find it:
  1. Open the device (remove screws, pry clips on case seam)
  2. Locate the PCB (printed circuit board)
  3. Look for 4 pins in a row, often labeled: GND, TX, RX, VCC
     Sometimes unlabeled -- use a multimeter to identify:
       GND = 0V (continuity with ground plane)
       VCC = 3.3V or 5V (steady voltage)
       TX  = fluctuating voltage (data being transmitted)
       RX  = steady high (waiting for input)
  4. Connect a USB-to-UART adapter (FTDI FT232, CP2102 -- $5-10)
     IMPORTANT: match voltage levels (3.3V vs 5V) or you fry the board
  5. Set baud rate (try: 115200, 9600, 57600, 38400)
  6. Open terminal: screen /dev/ttyUSB0 115200

What you typically get:
  - Full boot log (kernel version, loaded modules, mount points)
  - Login prompt -- try: root/root, admin/admin, or empty password
  - Often: direct root shell with NO password prompt at all
  - If login required: boot log may reveal credentials in cleartext
```

```text
=== JTAG (Joint Test Action Group) ===

JTAG provides deeper access than UART -- full hardware-level control:
  - Read/write flash memory (extract firmware directly from chip)
  - Debug running code (set breakpoints, examine registers, step through)
  - Bypass secure boot (on some implementations -- dump keys from memory)
  - Brick recovery (re-flash a device you accidentally corrupted)

Tools:
  - JTAGulator ($170) -- automatically identifies JTAG pins
  - OpenOCD -- open-source debug interface software
  - Bus Pirate ($30) -- multi-protocol hardware hacking tool

JTAG is the \

interface. If JTAG pads are accessible and
not disabled in production, you have complete control of the device at
the hardware level. Some manufacturers remove JTAG pads, cut traces,
or blow eFuses to disable it -- but many simply leave it open.

=== SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) ===

SPI is used to communicate with flash memory chips. With a SOIC clip
($5-10) you can connect directly to the flash chip WITHOUT desoldering:
  - Read the entire flash contents (firmware dump)
  - Write modified firmware back to the chip
  - Tools: flashrom, CH341A programmer ($3 on AliExpress)

Total hardware hacking kit cost: under $50
Access level: root on most consumer IoT devices
```

I want to be clear about something: the fact that a $50 hardware hacking kit gives you root access on most consumer IoT devices is NOT a sign that the security community has failed. It's a sign that the IoT industry has not yet reached the maturity level where security is a design requirement rather than an afterthought. The smartphone industry went through this same phase -- remember when Android devices shipped with unlocked bootloaders and root was a `su` command away? The phone industry fixed it (mostly). The IoT industry has not, and the economic incentives suggest it may never fix it for cheap consumer devices.

### Network-Based IoT Attacks

You don't always need physical access. Many IoT devices expose services and protocols on the network that are trivially exploitable:

```bash
# Shodan: the search engine for internet-connected devices
# Indexes banners from every device responding on the internet
shodan search \
country:NL\nshodan search \
port:23\nshodan search \

has_screenshot:true
# GoAhead is a web server used by hundreds of IP camera models

# Censys: similar to Shodan, focuses on certificate and service data
# Both are LEGAL -- they only scan publicly accessible services

# Find IoT devices on your local network
nmap -sV -p 80,443,23,22,8080,8443,554,1883,5683 192.168.1.0/24
# Port 554:  RTSP (cameras -- often unauthenticated video streams)
# Port 1883: MQTT (IoT messaging -- often no authentication)
# Port 5683: CoAP (constrained IoT protocol -- often open)

# MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport)
# Lightweight pub/sub messaging protocol -- the backbone of smart homes
# Wildcard subscribe: see EVERY message on the broker
mosquitto_sub -h TARGET_IP -t '#' -v
# You might see: temperature readings, door open/close events,
# light on/off commands, motion sensor triggers, GPS coordinates
# All in cleartext. No authentication. No encryption.
# An attacker on the same network sees everything your smart home does.

# Publish a command to an MQTT topic (if no authentication)
mosquitto_pub -h TARGET_IP -t 'home/door/lock' -m 'UNLOCK'
# If the smart lock subscribes to this topic without auth... yep.

# UPnP (Universal Plug and Play)
# Automatically opens firewall ports WITHOUT the user's knowledge
upnpc -l    # list UPnP port mappings on the router
# Many IoT devices use UPnP to punch holes in the firewall
# so they can be accessed from the internet. The user never consented.
# Result: IP camera's web interface is world-accessible with admin:admin

# CoAP (Constrained Application Protocol)
# UDP-based IoT protocol for resource-constrained devices
coap-client -m get coap://TARGET_IP/.well-known/core
# Enumerate all resources -- sensor readings, config endpoints, etc.
```

The MQTT situation is particularly alarming. A protocol designed for machine-to-machine communication in constrained environments got adopted by the consumer smart home industry, and most implementations ship with authentication disabled by default. The result: tens of thousands of MQTT brokers on the internet broadcasting everything from room temperatures to GPS coordinates to door lock states. Anyone can subscribe. Anyone can publish. That smart home automation you set up so your lights turn off when you leave? An attacker subscribing to your MQTT broker now knows your occupancy patterns.

### The AI Slop Connection

AI is making IoT security worse in two distinct ways, and both connect directly to what we covered in episode 6.

First, AI-generated firmware code reproduces the same vulnerabilities found in decades of insecure embedded C: buffer overflows, command injection in CGI handlers, hardcoded credentials baked into binaries. The AI learned from millions of lines of bad embedded code on GitHub and generates more of it. A developer asks the AI to generate a \

and gets back a CGI handler that pipes user input directly to `system()`. The AI does not know (and does not care) that the code runs as root on a device controlling a door lock.

Second, AI is being embedded INTO IoT devices -- smart cameras with face recognition, voice assistants with NLP, smart home hubs with decision-making capabilities. These AI-enhanced devices have the original IoT vulnerabilities (default creds, no updates, no encryption) PLUS new AI-specific attack surfaces: adversarial inputs that confuse the model, model poisoning via manipulated training data, and privacy violations from on-device data processing that sends everything back to the manufacturer's cloud.

```text
AI-Generated IoT Code Problems:

1. Web interface CGI handlers
   AI generates: system(\

+ user_input) -- direct command injection
   Should be: input validation + exec with argument array (no shell)

2. Authentication
   AI generates: if (strcmp(password, \

)) -- hardcoded credential
   Should be: configurable credential stored in protected flash partition

3. Memory management
   AI generates: char buffer[64]; strcpy(buffer, request) -- overflow
   Should be: strncpy with bounds checking, or better: use safe string lib

4. Update mechanism
   AI generates: download firmware via HTTP, flash immediately
   Should be: HTTPS + signature verification + rollback capability

5. Data transmission
   AI generates: send sensor_data over plaintext TCP socket
   Should be: TLS with certificate pinning to manufacturer endpoint

Same pattern as every other domain: AI optimizes for \
\nnot \

But on an IoT device running as root with
no firewall, the consequences of bad code are immediate and physical.
```

### What Comes Next

IoT security brings everything in this series from the virtual world into the physical one. The attacks are familiar -- default credentials, command injection, missing encryption, supply chain compromise -- but the consequences extend beyond data theft into physical safety. When a vulnerability can unlock a door, disable a medical device, or shut down a power grid, the stakes of security shift from financial to existential. We've covered the full spectrum of attacks (episodes 1-50), the defensive disciplines (architecture, IR, threat intel, compliance, privacy), and the specialized domains (crypto, IoT). The next phase of this series moves to the tooling side: how do you build your own security tools, automate the techniques we've practiced by hand, and develop the programming skills that separate script users from security engineers?

### Exercises

**Exercise 1:** Download a firmware image for a popular IoT device (many manufacturers publish updates on their support pages -- try TP-Link, D-Link, or Netgear routers). Use **binwalk** to extract the filesystem. Document: (a) what filesystem type was used (squashfs, JFFS2, cramfs), (b) any hardcoded credentials found in `/etc/shadow` or configuration files, (c) what services start at boot (`/etc/init.d/` scripts -- look for telnetd, httpd, sshd), (d) any private keys or certificates found, (e) strings output from the main web server binary (look for hardcoded passwords or API keys). Save your findings to `~/lab-notes/firmware-analysis.md`.

**Exercise 2:** Use **Shodan** (free tier, no account needed for basic searches) to search for exposed IoT devices in your country. Try queries: `\
`, `webcamXP`, `\

port:1883` (MQTT brokers). Document: (a) how many results each query returns, (b) what device types are most commonly exposed, (c) what the most common open ports are across results, (d) any patterns in manufacturer or firmware version. Do NOT interact with any device -- observation only. Save to `~/lab-notes/shodan-iot-recon.md`.

**Exercise 3:** Research the **Stuxnet** worm in depth. Document: (a) the delivery mechanism (USB drive propagation to air-gapped network), (b) the full exploitation chain (four zero-days in Windows: print spooler, .lnk shortcut, Windows Server Service, Task Scheduler), (c) the payload (Siemens Step 7 PLC code modification -- what specific PLC instructions were changed and why), (d) stealth mechanisms (rootkit on both Windows AND the PLC that hid modified ladder logic from the SCADA display), (e) the physical damage caused (centrifuge speed manipulation: normal 1,064 Hz pushed to 1,410 Hz), (f) attribution evidence (joint US-Israel operation, codenamed Olympic Games). Save to `~/lab-notes/stuxnet-analysis.md`.

最近不知道是不是到了鸟儿繁殖的季节，总感觉街边多了很多不一样的小生机。以前走路路过一排排电动车店、自行车店、小吃店和服装店，从来不会特意抬头留意上方的景象，日复一日都是平平无奇的街景。
 
结果今天送孩子去上数学课的路上，孩子眼尖，突然发现临街一家门面的正上方，竟然搭了一个小小的鸟窝。刚好有大鸟叼着小虫飞回窝里，细细喂养窝里的小鸟。我顺着孩子指的方向抬头一看，果然如此，看着外形很像是燕子，瞬间觉得特别治愈，心里还默默猜想，店家有燕子筑巢，一定是喜事连连、福气满满。
 
本以为这只是偶然的小幸运，没想到没走两步，隔了一家店铺，头顶又发现了一个新鸟窝。我瞬间有些好奇，不确定这些筑巢的到底是燕子，还是其他种类的小鸟，新鲜感一下子拉满。
 
于是我和孩子一路仰着头，认真观察街边每家店铺的房顶。路过的店主看着我们母子俩频频抬头，觉得十分奇怪，也顺着我们的目光抬头观望。大家顺势聊了起来，店主们都说，这些鸟窝都是近半个月、一个月左右，小鸟陆续搭建起来的。
 
我们就这么边走边看，细细数了整条街道，居然足足发现了六家店铺都有小鸟筑巢。其中四个鸟窝都格外热闹，时不时有大鸟、小鸟探出头张望，灵动又可爱。原本几分钟的路程，我们硬生生看了十几二十分钟，全程觉得新奇又有趣。
 
不得不感叹大自然真的太奇妙了，生活里这些不经意被发现的细碎美好，总能带来满满的惊喜和温柔。更有意思的是我家孩子，全程脑洞大开，不停跟我科普提问，好奇燕窝为什么值钱、普通燕子窝和食用燕窝是不是一样、燕窝如何形成、怎么加工，还追问最贵的燕窝、血燕是什么样子。小孩子天马行空的想法，真的特别可爱。

That’s the headline, but the bigger point is this: one scrappy, deflected John McGinn goal may have cracked open Scotland’s best-ever path to the knockout stage. For a country that’s never made it past the group stage, that’s massive.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: True talk
links.author: favour20045

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The match was decided in the 28th minute when John McGinn’s shot took a deflection off a Haitian defender and looped in. Not a goal for the museum, but Scotland won’t care in the slightest. After decades of near-misses and absences, ugly goals count exactly the same as beautiful ones.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 The historical weight here is the real story. Scotland hadn’t won a World Cup match since beating Sweden in 1990, and they hadn’t even appeared at the tournament since 1998. That means an entire generation of fans had literally never seen Scotland win on this stage. That’s a brutal drought to finally snap.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 The group situation makes this even more interesting. Scotland now lead Group C with 3 points, while Brazil and Morocco drew 1-1. That’s close to the ideal opening scenario: Scotland gets the win, and the two strongest-looking rivals split points. Translation: Scotland fully controls its own fate from here.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: I thought that I saw the word `teater`, but then I noticed the edit on your comment !INDEED! 🤔🤯😅
links.author: savvytester

links.body: 5/5 🧵 The expanded 48-team format matters too. With four-team groups and the top two advancing, Scotland has a more realistic route to the knockout rounds than in past eras. So this wasn’t just a nostalgic win — it may be the result that changes the ceiling of their entire tournament. 📎 [Source](https://cryptobriefing.com/scotland-world-cup-win-haiti/)\n\n#threadstorm
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 1/5 🧵 The wild part isn’t “UFC + crypto.” It’s **UFC fighters getting White House event bonuses in a stablecoin tied to Trump’s family business**. That takes crypto sponsorship and jams it directly into presidential optics, government property, and family financial interests. Clean headline. Messy as hell substance.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The core fact: some fighters at Sunday’s White House UFC event are set to receive bonuses in **USD1**, a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by **World Liberty Financial**. That company is tied to the Trump family and the Witkoff family. The event is on the south White House lawn, scheduled for **14 June**, which also happens to be Trump’s birthday.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 Why this matters: paying in a stablecoin instead of just wiring dollars is functionally marketing. The article quotes a crypto policy expert saying it has the same economic effect as cutting a check, except now the payment itself advertises the token. In plain English: this isn’t just compensation — it’s product placement wearing boxing gloves.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 The conflict-of-interest fight is the real story underneath the spectacle. The White House line is that there’s **no conflict** because Trump’s assets are in a trust run by his children. Critics won’t buy that easily, because the article points out Trump previously appeared publicly tied to World Liberty, and financial disclosures list his holdings as **over $50m**. So even if the legal structure is neat on paper, the optics are brutal.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 5/5 🧵 There’s more baggage here too: World Liberty has already faced controversy around its governance token, litigation involving **Justin Sun**, and broader scrutiny as one of the biggest wealth engines linked to the Trump family. So this isn’t a random sponsorship — it looks like a high-visibility push to normalize **USD1** through sport, politics, and spectacle all at once. 📎 [Source](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jun/14/white-house-ufc-fighters-crypto)\n\n#threadstorm

links.title: My detailed experience with the cards obtained by opening the Glide Pack
links.body:
Today I had the opportunity open Glide Pack in the game. One of the most enjoyable things in game is opening a new pack discovering what kind cards inside. Every time I open a pack I feel kind excitement. Because you never know when a valuable rare card will be found. This time was no exception. After opening the Glide Pack, I got several interesting cards which have enriched my collection and provided me with opportunity create more powerful decks in the future.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRBELHPzSo5TWEuRDUbBPnfXKhC7L4hbZezNHuVtpsX4M/1781442990811.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVVhT648XwLGgLeB72c4rLpyHYEATS8G7yJ9RKzecNLS1/1781442828334.jpg)

After opening the first pack, I got Goblin, Whistling Damon, Helmet Kharafax, Witch of Warwick and the Rare card Sarius. Each card has different characteristics and can be used in different types of strategic matches. When I turned over the first card and saw the Goblin, I immediately realized that it is a fast unit. Since it is a low-manner card, it is easy use at the beginning  match and sometimes such a card plays a very effective role in keeping opponent under pressure. Although it is a small card, its value is much higher if used at the right time.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNgsYLrHf8iNCJobhqm88B6ZGcmLyiV9semF1fsrYjLH3/1781442827838.jpg)

 Then I got the Whistling Damon card. I really liked artwork and design  this card. Often, there are characters in game that are not only beautiful look at, but also contribute significantly to the battle. Whistling Damon seemed like just that to me. Considering its stats and power, it is suitable for moderate strategy use.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPT4j4KuEwAdbsYrVzZ5RRKuU6aY7LziGbpy2AzcuUerw/1781442827973.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRpLZ1kTmXvuhq3Ut7cKs72B4aw7TSj8nWpS8fvtLNjkN/1781442990926.jpg)

After getting the Helmet Kharafax card, I have another good addition to my collection. The defensive properties of this card attracted me. In the game, it is not enough to have only offensive cards, but also strong defense is needed. Sometimes a good defensive card can change the outcome of the entire match. I think Helmet Kharafax is one of those potential cards.

Then comes Witch of Warwick. The look and design of this card are really amazing. You can tell just by looking at this card that the game developers have put a lot of effort into creating the artwork of the card. It is not only beautiful to look at, but the functionality of the card is also important. I believe that Witch of Warwick can play an important role in creating different types of decks in the future.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbxuBS7yUWGVSAns6U9kXxjGRbY3yVtyvRXNVQDGv63k7/1781442828420.jpg)

 But the most enjoyable moment of the first pack was getting the Rare card Sarius. The feeling of getting a Rare card is always different. When I saw the word Rare, I really liked it. Because Rare cards not only enhance the beauty of the collection, but also increase the player's strategic potential. Sometimes, new types of decks can be created with Rare cards, which are not possible with ordinary cards. After getting Sarius, I thought this pack was already successful.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVVhT648XwLGgLeB72c4rLpyHYEATS8G7yJ9RKzecNLS1/1781442902312.jpg)

Then I opened the second Glide Pack. The second pack also had the opportunity to get several good cards. There I got Hugo Strongsword, Orella Abadon, Krash Wanderford and again Whistling Damon. The excitement was not less when opening the second pack. Because my hopes were even higher after getting the Rare card in the first pack.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPQ4WwgUyj7cSurMuVpnJwKLLnuizGYfn7dxFaWm5m8nY/1781442902540.jpg)

The Hugo Strongsword card seemed quite strong to me. Both its attack and defense are balanced. The game always needs cards that can hit on one side, and hold their position on the other. Hugo Strongsword is exactly that kind of card. I plan to use it in different combinations in the future.

 Then came Orella Abadon. This was the second Rare card and the biggest surprise for me. It was really a blessing to get two Rare cards in one pack opening session. I really liked the design, character, and potential uses of Orella Abadon. All players love to collect Rare cards, as they increase the value of the collection and can provide an extra advantage in competitive matches.

The Krash Wanderford card is also an important addition to my collection. Just by looking its appearance it is clear that it aggressive character. Sometimes such a card is very effective for quickly attacking and pressuring the opponent. I think that Krash Wanderford can perform exceptionally well when used with the right deck.

Getting Whistling Damon a second time was also a positive for me. Because having multiple copies of the same card opens up the opportunity to upgrade or level up in the future. Many players try to collect multiple copies of a particular card so that they can make that card stronger. So I see getting Whistling Damon a second time as an added benefit.

The experience of opening these two Glide Packs has inspired me anew. The joy, excitement, and anticipation that comes with opening a pack every time in the game is truly amazing. Sometimes the desired card is not available, and sometimes, if luck helps, valuable Rare cards are added to the collection. This time, luck was quite good in my case. Getting two Rare cards and being able to collect several useful cards is undoubtedly a successful pack opening experience.

One of the fun things about playing the game is gradually enriching your collection. Each new card brings new possibilities. New cards mean new strategies, new decks, and new experiences. After opening this Glide Pack, I feel even more excited. Because my collection has added some cards that can help me in various battles in the future. 

Overall, today's Glide Pack opening was a very enjoyable and memorable experience for me. Goblin, Helmet Kharafax, Witch of Warwick, Hugo Strongsword, Krash Wanderford, Whistling Damon, Sarius and Orella Abadon—all of the cards have enriched my collection. I was especially happy to receive the Rare cards Sarius and Orella Abadon. As a gamer such moments motivate me even more and encourage me  play game with new enthusiasm every day. I hope  open more Glide Packs in the future and collect new powerful and Rare cards. At the same time, I will be able improve my deck and achieve good results in competitive matches. This pack opening experience today will undoubtedly be a joyful chapter in my gaming journey.

links.body: 1/5 🧵 BTC is trying to do the most important thing in a downtrend: **stop going down first**. The article’s core point is simple — the higher timeframes still look bearish, but the 1-hour and 4-hour charts are finally showing signs of life. In plain English: this looks more like a **relief bounce attempt** than a confirmed trend reversal.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The headline number is **$64,549** at 8 a.m. Eastern on June 14. That matters because BTC is sitting above a key support area after falling hard from roughly **$82,969** earlier in the year. The article frames the **200-week SMA** as the big battlefield — historically a level where sellers often start losing their edge. If that floor holds, bulls at least have a case.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 Shorter timeframes are where the optimism comes from. On the **4-hour chart**, BTC is making **higher lows**, which usually means panic selling is cooling off. On the **1-hour chart**, momentum and **MACD** have both turned positive, suggesting traders are trying tactical longs on dips. The article highlights **$62,700 to $63,000** as the reactive support zone and **$64,500 to $65,500** as the first upside target area.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 The bigger picture is still ugly, though. **11 of 14 moving averages are bearish**, and from the 20-period MA onward, basically everything is still flashing downside pressure. That’s why the article doesn’t call a bottom — it says the daily chart remains corrective. Translation: one decent bounce does not magically erase a broader bearish structure. Bitcoin needs a convincing move through roughly **$65,000 to $67,000** before this starts looking like more than a temporary recovery.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body:
5/5 🧵 The real risk line is clear: if BTC loses **$62K**, pressure can build back toward **$59K-$61K**. If it closes below **$59K**, the article says the **$50K zone** comes back into play. So the setup is basically this: **short-term momentum improved, long-term trend still suspect**. Bulls finally have something to work with, but they have not won the fight yet.  
📎 [Source](https://news.bitcoin.com/btc-momentum-turns-positive-as-bitcoin-fights-to-hold-the-64000-zone/)

links.title: My first time attending a book fair /Ma première participation à un salon du livre EN /FR
links.body:
Hello book lovers, /Bonjour chers lecteurs,

As you already know, I published my first novel at the end of January 2026 and it has been available on Kindle since the end of February 2026.

It is still only available in French and is not yet on Kobo. 

I haven’t had the chance to get started on the English translation yet, but it won’t be long now.
As for Kobo, we’re gathering information, because we’re a bit worried that it might be too easy to download or hack the system. If any of you have any information on this, we’d love to hear it 😇.

> Vous savez déjà que j'ai publié mon premier roman fin janvier 2026 et qu'il est disponible sur Kindle depuis fin février 2026.
> 
> Il n'est toujours disponible qu'en français et n'est pas encore sur Kobo. 
> 
> Je n'ai pas encore eu l'occasion de m'atteler à la traduction en anglais, mais cela ne saurait tarder.
Pour Kobo, nous prenons nos informations, parce que nous craignons un peu qu'il ne soit trop facile de le télécharger ou de pirater le système. Si certains d'entre vous ont des infos à ce sujet, nous sommes preneurs 😇.

I took part in two book-signing sessions, which helped me improve the way I presented my book both verbally and physically, and prepared me for this first book fair. 

This was the first ‘Belgian Literature Fair’, held on the weekend of 6 and 7 June 2026 at the Palais des Congrès in Mons. There were well over a hundred exhibitors in attendance, including publishing houses.

> J'ai fait 2 séances de dédicace qui ont permis d'améliorer ma présentation verbale et physique de mon livre, ce qui m'a préparée à ce premier salon du livre. 
> 
> Il s'agissait du premier \

, organisé le weekend des 6 et 7 juin 2026, au Palais des Congrès de Mons. Il y avait une bonne centaine d'exposants présents, dont des maisons d'édition.

![salon litt belge 7juin26.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/faustine.books/EoptuFGjkSybxVfvEZfxGV5TQTD8uciWe6PK29Lufuffug9icBvMnfyc6LX1KJyZeGk.jpg)
*Me at my stand /Moi à mon stand*

It was a wonderful, enriching experience, where we met some interesting people. 
There are still things we need to improve, of course; we’re still learning. 

On the other side of the pillar was a publishing house, with whom we had a chance to chat and whom we’ll be contacting again very soon.

At these events, there are also short talks and book-signing sessions with better-known authors. I wasn’t able to attend these talks myself as I was at my stand, but Ithara was able to attend an interview with Thomas Gunzig and chat with him. 
Thomas Gunzig is a Belgian author (black humour, social satire, absurdity, irony, offbeat imagination), who is very approachable and friendly.

> C'était une belle expérience, enrichissante, où nous avons fait des rencontres intéressantes. 
Nous avons encore des choses à améliorer, bien sûr, nous sommes toujours en phase d'apprentissage. 
> 
> De l'autre côté du pilier se trouvait une maison d'édition, avec laquelle nous avons pu échanger et que nous recontacterons très prochainement.
> 
> Lors de ces événements, il y a aussi des petites conférences et des séances de dédicace d'auteurs plus connus. Je n'ai pas pu assister moi-même à ces conférences puisque j'étais à mon stand, mais Ithara a pu assister à une interview de Thomas Gunzig et a pu interagir avec celui-ci. 
Thomas Gunzig est un auteur belge (humour noir, satire sociale, absurdité, ironie, imaginaire décalé), très accessible et sympathique.


![6juin26 thomas gunzig et moi litt belge 3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/faustine.books/EpA4PWWyuD8hmsu7Fyihkq2uSMzffHN4YRNCPqHF7GkcT1PnZ6GH5JxNrA5cDJX7gyP.jpg)
*Myself and Thomas Gunzig /Moi-même et Thomas Gunzig*

For the time being, the next book fair I’ll be attending is the “Salon du livre de Wallonie”, which will take place at Lotto Mons Expo on the weekend of 26 and 27 September 2026. 

In the meantime, we’ll be making a few more improvements to our stand, such as adding a tablecloth and tweaking the promotional poster slightly. We’ll also sort out the administrative side of things to make sure everything is done properly. 

I’ll also be holding a few book-signing sessions to meet potential readers.

And then, of course, I’m continuing to write my second novel (and I’m already thinking about my third, but shhh). 

> Pour le moment, le prochain salon du livre auquel je participerai sera le \

, qui aura lieu au Lotto Mons Expo, le weekend des 26 et 27 septembre 2026. 
> 
> D'ici là, nous allons améliorer encore un peu notre présentation, en prévoyant une nappe et en modifiant un rien l'affiche descriptive. Nous allons aussi nous renseigner du côté administratif pour que tout soit fait comme il faut. 
> 
> Je ferai également l'une ou l'autre séance de dédicace pour aller à la rencontre de lecteurs potentiels.
> 
> Et puis, évidemment, je continue à écrire mon deuxième roman (et je réfléchis déjà à mon troisième, mais chuuuut). 

Events like this disrupt our daily routine, but I really enjoyed it. It wasn’t a particularly noisy atmosphere, unlike other kinds of fairs, and that suited me fine as I don’t like noise. 

We were still pretty exhausted after that literary weekend, though, and it took us a few days to recover.

I’m glad I was able to attend a reasonably sized fair before the one in September, which will be four times bigger. 

Entry is free for visitors; they’re just asked to register online in advance.

I hope to be able to tell you soon about the latest developments, book signings, translations, and so on.

Happy reading, and see you soon!

> Ce genre d'événement perturbe notre quotidien, mais cela m'a beaucoup plu. Ce n'était pas une atmosphère très bruyante, comme le sont d'autres genres de salons, et cela me convenait puisque je n'aime pas le bruit. 
> 
> Nous étions tout de même bien épuisés après ce weekend littéraire dont nous nous sommes remis en quelques jours.
> 
> Je suis contente d'avoir pu participer à un salon de taille raisonnable avant de participer à celui de septembre qui sera 4 fois plus grand. 
> 
> L'entrée est gratuite pour les visiteurs, il leur est juste demandé de s'inscrire en ligne, au préalable.
> 
> J'espère pouvoir vous raconter rapidement les prochaines avancées, séances de dédicace, traductions, etc.
> 
> Bonnes lectures et à bientôt !

Faustine

links.body:
![gg.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/EoyQ3GhMBK4jdZgwEx5KieCVfSZTg9DvWi2DDKZPL3z3Xst2sEMdfKYWQ7nUQ2kY2p8.png)



Colleagues, as usual, I'm back bright and early to show you my new drawing, inspired by one of the beautiful cards in the game. Today I chose a guitar, the R361 Ugos Flying V. This guitar is one of the most striking out there, and that's partly thanks to something obvious: its design. It has a V shape and is part of the Flying V guitar family. The guitar itself, in terms of sound, can do the same as any other guitar, but its best feature is undoubtedly its design.

Music, like any instrument, depends on who plays it; that's undeniable. Since I'm not a guitar expert, I wouldn't be able to distinguish its sound from other electric guitars. But I bet some of you who see my drawing know a lot about guitars and might be able to tell which sound is which. In fact, if you have any tips for differentiating electric guitars, feel free to share them in the comments so I can learn, and so can others who read this. I'm going to leave you with an example video anyway; in this video, a musician plays this type of guitar.

https://youtu.be/D0EBXzYO7EQ?si=PQYGP1kE0bMg7Wda

What did you think? I personally like their music. I should mention that this V-shaped guitar design was actually created by Gibson, the very famous instrument manufacturer. That was back in the '60s. It was supposedly designed to be futuristic for its time. And rock and metal bands quickly adopted it to give the impression that their music was innovative. Very clever technique. Okay, let's move on to the drawing, which is probably what you're all eager to see today. First, I drew the card's frame.

<div class=\

> ![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/Eo2BM1YUX8CywTFdEGxyfNt9JLyRtV2rMvfnamCX4LyrgxZ9DMkKxftrGjT6jo9Qw5A.jpg) After finishing the frame, I drew what would be the guitar's neck; as you can see, it's rectangular. Next, I drew the V-shaped body. It turned out like this. ![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/Eo2BM1YUX8DHkUJTD4FGFNBf5hcPv8DtD5kqgdM8WwRgY2DdNqyMgZCh2F8nbtNH5z7.jpg) ![3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/Eo4JhGpWi9G1Qom3scQwwfMSYstwAANs1vffUMPbxxRhEUVEXXDEWPv6AnHgBq1KkLG.jpg) Then I drew the headstock area at the top of the neck next to the six tuning pegs, each of which tunes one of the strings. In total, this guitar has six. The pegs turn to loosen or tighten the strings, creating various different notes. ![4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/Eo4JhGpWi9G1QoiHGhHt6GtCmybMSWieG2xgVWNo4489RMjtouYKf2R9bEBSxhVLSkm.jpg) Now comes the painting. As you'll see in the following screenshots, I started by painting the frame and then the two backgrounds, both the exterior and the interior. For the exterior, I used one of the predominant colors from the example chart. On the guitar, which was the last thing I painted, I first applied a base coat with the main colors, and then on top of that layer, I painted the details like the knobs and strings, as well as the string supports. ![5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/EoAg4ghD376zPo8E5p1xPE9DJyvpZ4pmorH6mjzkjfvNr29UNd3Z76o793xzEqdu4Hz.jpg) ![6.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/Eq5DxAfFtBps1nJHAzpzTDTWCUPNkDmfm366wguQQgimM94DLwV7gDZvnhi2DPVMZCS.jpg) ![7.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/Eq9UrLN68dwwAGFnnsoDiA87C6LHeK6dCN32pUJ2x9QsdPXqsG6omqcRx63MZYvN9r1.jpg) ![8.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/EqDjbz2TCyQDKnxLLPJ2oRUMS89nG6K7KPG9BojegVf1ngG3Vrwtd4BGbsMknpSQRxQ.jpg) ![9.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/EqDjddF1xkKD18Lu3f5kbB3rnxN8YA8QT3XScuZz2oyPsZGdujJHSxqoaauxHy4YbDn.jpg) And to say goodbye for today, here's the finished drawing. See you in the next one; it was definitely fun painting this guitar. ![10.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/23ydGHEqhMKEvDMSNmvVSRHWBkLc12xQjkYATLmXqRaLAbW3T78QoPXaBqYWymW2syEbT.jpg)

links.body: 1/5 🧵 One airstrike in Beirut may have just complicated a US-Iran deal that was already shaky. The real story here isn’t just the blast — it’s the accusation that regional escalation could deliberately sabotage diplomacy and pull Washington back toward war.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The article says a diplomat tied to the negotiations believes the Beirut strike created fresh obstacles to finalizing the agreement. That source goes further, framing it as an attempt to derail President Trump’s deal and reignite US military entanglement. That’s a heavy claim, and it shows how fragile these talks are when events on the ground can instantly reshape the political math.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 Israel’s side pushes back hard. A senior Israeli official rejected the idea that Israel caused the clashes and argued that Hezbollah has spent the last three days targeting Israeli civilians. That matters because the narrative battle is almost as important as the military one: each side is trying to define whether this is sabotage, retaliation, or self-defense.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 On the Iranian side, the article highlights a more nuanced response than the usual doom-posting. Iranian parliamentary economic committee member Zohoryan says the draft memorandum does contain flaws and ambiguities, so criticism isn’t baseless. But he also argues that calling it “Iran’s surrender” or “worse than the nuclear deal” is exaggerated and misses the actual substance of the text.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 5/5 🧵 Bottom line: the piece paints a deal caught between diplomacy and regional chaos. The memorandum may be imperfect, but the bigger risk is that outside violence hardens positions before negotiators can finish the job. In plain English: bad timing, bad optics, and a very real chance that geopolitics steamrolls policy. 📎 [Source](https://www.panewslab.com/en/articles/019ec621-9b44-72d2-96e7-2db1cb0fc91a)\n\n#threadstorm

links.body: 1/5 🧵 India isn’t changing crypto taxes much — it’s changing enforcement. That’s the real story. Authorities say they found **$104M in undisclosed crypto income** and have already sent **44,000+ notices**. The era of vague “I made some gains” reporting looks dead.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The tax rates themselves are the same blunt instrument: **30% tax on crypto profits** and **1% TDS** on eligible transfers. What got sharper is the reporting. Under the new **Income Tax Act, 2025**, now in force from **April 1, 2026**, investors are expected to disclose **transaction-level data**, not just a final profit/loss number.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 That means India wants the full paper trail: **trades, token swaps, transfers, and disposal events**. And not just on centralized exchanges. The scope reaches into **DeFi activity and multi-wallet usage** too. In plain English: if you moved assets around five wallets and three platforms, tax authorities want that map, not your vibes.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 The other big shift is data matching. **Exchanges, custodians, and wallet service providers** are being pushed to submit **per-user transaction details** directly to tax authorities. That data can then be reconciled against **individual tax returns and blockchain records**. If your records are sloppy, incomplete, or contradictory, that’s exactly where the trapdoor opens.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 5/5 🧵 Bottom line: this is less a “new tax” story and more a **surveillance + compliance upgrade** for crypto in India. Active traders, DeFi users, and anyone spread across multiple wallets are now far more exposed to recordkeeping mistakes — or deliberate non-disclosure. Clean bookkeeping just went from “smart” to “non-optional.” 📎 [Source](https://coingape.com/india-cracks-down-on-104m-undisclosed-crypto-income-amid-tax-season/)\n\n#threadstorm

links.body: 1/5 🧵 Volkswagen isn’t just trimming fat — it’s cutting **19,000 jobs in Germany by the end of 2026**, and that’s only the near-term slice of a much bigger restructuring. The real story: Europe’s biggest carmaker is being squeezed by weak EV demand, high costs, and brutal competition from Chinese manufacturers.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The cuts are being done through **attrition, early retirement, and voluntary departures**, not forced layoffs — at least for now. That matters. Volkswagen is trying to shrink without detonating a war with German unions. It’s basically restructuring with a velvet glove on, because the steel glove would cause political and labor chaos.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 This isn’t a one-off move. The 19,000 cuts sit inside a **binding 2024 labor agreement** to eliminate **more than 28,000 jobs by 2030** at the core VW brand. And the broader warning sign is even uglier: earlier disclosures suggested **as many as 50,000 group-wide job cuts in Germany** could happen by decade’s end.

The market will care less about the headline layoffs and more about the details: plant impact, cost savings, and whether factory closures are lurking behind the polite language. links.body: 1/5 🧵 The big takeaway: this isn’t “crypto maybe finding product-market fit.” It’s crypto getting shoved in front of the biggest sports audience on Earth. The 2026 World Cup group stage is giving **Kraken, Chainlink, Chiliz, and Avalanche** exactly what brands crave: billions of eyeballs and actual user touchpoints, not just logo wallpaper.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The scale matters. This World Cup is bigger than any before it: **48 teams, 104 matches**, spread across **the US, Mexico, and Canada**. More matches = more broadcasts, more fans, more digital engagement, and more chances for FIFA’s crypto partners to be seen in live products tied to the tournament. That’s the real story here: distribution at absurd scale.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 Each partner has a distinct role. **Kraken** is the official crypto exchange supporter. **Chainlink** provides oracle infrastructure for prediction markets, meaning it helps connect real match results to on-chain betting systems. **Chiliz** is pushing fan token integrations across **Solana and Base**. **Avalanche** powers **FIFA Collect**, which has already generated **85,000+ blockchain addresses** and includes a **Right-to-Tickets** feature for fan access.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 One useful clarification in the piece: the officiating appointments and the crypto deals are completely separate. FIFA named **170 match officials** total — **52 referees, 88 assistant referees, 30 video match officials** — and they were selected through FIFA’s standard process after a **10-day seminar in Miami**. No token voting, no blockchain referee nonsense. Good. Football has enough chaos already.

links.body: 1/5 🧵 The SEC just greenlit something bigger than another plain vanilla Bitcoin fund: **T. Rowe Price can launch an actively managed crypto ETF that may hold 5–15 assets, including BTC, ETH, XRP, SOL, DOGE, and even SHIB.** That matters because Wall Street is moving from “Bitcoin only” toward curated multi-asset crypto exposure in one wrapper.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The core shift is structure. This isn’t a simple index clone. The fund will use the **FTSE Crypto US Listed Index** as a benchmark, but the manager is allowed to actively rotate holdings and try to **outperform** it. In normal conditions, it’s expected to hold **between 5 and 15 eligible assets**, though it can dip below or go above that range when needed. That flexibility is the whole pitch: one listed product, multiple coins, active management instead of autopilot.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 The approved eligible universe is broad by ETF standards: **Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, Cardano, Avalanche, Litecoin, Polkadot, Dogecoin, Chainlink, Stellar, Hedera, Bitcoin Cash, Shiba Inu, and Sui**, plus cash, cash equivalents, and some stablecoins for operations. The eyebrow-raiser is the inclusion of **DOGE and SHIB**. That’s not just “serious crypto beta” — it’s an admission that market demand now includes meme-coin exposure inside regulated products.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 There’s an important caveat: **approval of the exchange listing rule is not the same as the full commercial launch being live today.** The SEC approved NYSE Arca’s proposal under **Rule 8.201-E** on June 12, which clears the path for listing and trading shares, but the issuer still controls the rollout process. Because it’s actively managed, the order also leans hard on safeguards: firewall rules around sponsor staff and affiliated broker-dealers, plus the ability to halt trading if holdings disclosure isn’t shared fairly.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 5/5 🧵 Bigger picture: this lands in a market where ETF demand is still messy, not one-way euphoria. The article notes **XRP ETPs pulled in about $10.68 million in the week ended June 12**, while some **Bitcoin and Ethereum products saw outflows**, and U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had already logged a **13-day outflow streak from May 15 to June 3**. So this approval is less “everyone is piling in” and more “the menu is expanding fast, even while investor appetite stays selective.” 📎 [Source](https://crypto.news/sec-approves-t-rowe-price-crypto-etf-with-btc-eth-and-xrp-exposure/)\n\n#threadstorm
