body.title: The Tanagra craze
body.body: > 🇳🇱 [nl]| |-|-|-|-| ![banner-tanagra-2026-en.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bartman67/Eo6JR6Ay5vTkNadurCh3VwwTwkT5B3bFDnBTkPCBPYZdu5NrW6QJdg1B1V7eJz75CLm.jpg) When I innocently started researching who or what a \

was, I expected - as so often happens - to end up in some obscure corner of history and an even more obscure part of the internet. Nothing could be further from the truth; it turned out to be a craze comparable to Flippos and Tamagotchis...

But let's start at the beginning, about 150 years ago, at the end of the 19th century.

Shortly after 1870, terracotta figurines dating from antiquity suddenly appear out of nowhere on the European art market. They are new, they are beautiful, they turn out to come from [Tanagra (Greece)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanagra), and they cause a true sensation.

They are soon called \

, and every self-respecting museum starts a collection, while wealthy art collectors proudly display them in their homes. And as often happens when art becomes commerce, forgeries quickly appear. Not only clever merchants, but also 'clever' contemporary artists are inspired by them, resulting in more and more derivative works, and the craze only grows larger.

I must honestly admit that until recently, I had never heard of Tanagras (and let's be honest, I'm not the only one...). And now, more than a hundred years later, the memory of these once so popular Tanagras seems to have almost completely faded.

And that's precisely what makes me curious. **Et voilà**, the account of my quest and what I discovered.

---
### History of Tanagra
---
Tanagra, or \

as the ancient Greeks wrote it, is a place now about an hour's drive north of Athens ([map](https://www.openstreetmap.org/?mlat=38.327&mlon=23.535#map=8/38.327/23.535)). The city already existed in ancient Greece, and from the 4th century BCE, it became known for its large-scale production of terracotta figurines.
These mold-cast figurines, mainly depicting women and girls, were used in homes, temples, and as grave gifts.

The figurines were covered with a white slip, on which realistic colors were applied with water-based paint after firing. The figurines were often only 10-25 cm tall and were distributed throughout ancient Greece and far beyond.

Although it is now known that they were also made in other cities, the name Tanagra is still used for all comparable figurines, even if they were made elsewhere. This is mainly thanks to a (re)discovery at the end of the 19th century.

---
### Discovery... and Looting
---

In the early 1870s, the Necropolis - the cemetery - of Tanagra is discovered. At that time, archaeology is still mostly a hobby for adventurers and profit-driven traders. They see fame and dollar signs before their eyes, and in 1871, about ten thousand tombs are looted. The terracotta figurines, which were first found there, find a ready market in Western Europe and from then on bear the name of their find site: Tanagras. Antiquity is in fashion at the time, and every self-respecting museum, followed by many wealthy individuals, is eager to acquire these figurines.

The Greek government and population react with indignation to the looting and smuggling of heritage abroad. Between 1873 and 1875, the excavations are under government supervision led by [Panagiotis Stamatakis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panagiotis_Stamatakis).

---
### A True Craze
---
<div class='pull-left'>

As a result of exhibitions at the **British Museum** (London), the **Hermitage** (St. Petersburg), the **Metropolitan** (New York), but especially the **Louvre** in Paris, the figurines gain in popularity.

The most famous Tanagra is probably the \

purchased by the Louvre in 1876 (see adjacent image). On this figurine, the original watercolor paints are still clearly visible. The figurines can still be found in [the collections of various French museums](https://pop.culture.gouv.fr/lien-partage/69f8bdbb525591bd03488a15?type=advanced) up to the [Kröller Müller Museum in the Netherlands](https://krollermuller.nl/en/griekenland-tanagra-figurine). A few years after the first purchases, the figurines also appear at the **1878 World's Fair in Paris** with over 16 million visitors, introducing the general public to them. A demand for the figurines arises, naturally in limited supply. In addition to forgeries, contemporary artists are also inspired and/or smell money (in this or reverse order...). A real stream of works based on Tanagras emerges.
![Lady in Blue - source: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Lady_in_blue_Louvre_MNB907.jpg/500px-Lady_in_blue_Louvre_MNB907.jpg)
--- ### Derivative Works --- A small selection from the enormous amount of artworks that have appeared since the end of the 19th century. --- #### Sculptures and Paintings by Gérôme ---
![Τάναγρα - Gérôme - source: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f9/G%C3%A9rome_Tanagra_1890.jpg?uselang=fr) ![Hoop Dancer - source: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/95/Jean-L%C3%A9on_G%C3%A9r%C3%B4me--Hoop_Dancer--before_1895--Haggin_Museum--Stockton-CA.jpg)
One of the earliest (dated...) derivative works I could find is by [Jean-Léon Gérôme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-L%C3%A9on_G%C3%A9r%C3%B4me). In 1890, this French sculptor/painter created a [life-size Tanagra in marble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanagra_(G%C3%A9r%C3%B4me_sculpture)) (also holding a Tanagra figurine in her hand), which became very famous. The statue was presented at the 1890 Salon, after which he produced various bronze editions of it. The small figurine in the hand of the Tanagra (itself inspired by a Tanagra) was also released separately under the title \

). He also made two paintings of imaginary studios where Tanagras are being painted (and where, among others, his own Tanagra can be seen). Additionally, he made - twice even - a self-portrait in which he is working on his own marble Tanagra. I think we can safely say that Gérôme had a slight obsession! This same Gérôme also painted Pygmalion (and Galatea), which I already wrote about in [this blog](https://peakd.com/galatea/@bartman67/wie-was-galatea). ![Self-portrait - source: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/38/Gerome--Haggin--The-Artist-and-His-Model.jpg) --- For those who understand French, here is an interesting video about Gérôme and his Tanagra sculpture: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uZbcP9uIcS0 --- #### Fashion ---

> ![ball gown - source: Les modes: Revue mensuelle illustrée des arts décoratifs appliqués à la femme.](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bartman67/23wqnntCCT62XXYxi4ojCncroa6rbEPfBQRsT2ZfjF3BxnYxhMJPUFMcP5J6jwAKR2Bfv.png) More than 20 years later, the influence was still there. In 1923 - we're now in the 'roaring twenties' - the red dress shown here on the right appears, made of velveteen by designer Bernard, in the typical style of the time. (source: *Art, goût, beauté: feuillets de l'élégance féminine*, January 1, 1923; see [Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k10391998/f18.image))

>
The ancient Tanagras are often depicted wearing beautifully pleated robes, and their popularity had a lasting influence on fashion.

For example, the design in the adjacent photo is a dress called \

from 1902. (source: *Les Modes: revue mensuelle illustrée des arts décoratifs appliqués à la femme*, April 1, 1902 - see [Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k5725776b/f13.image)). --- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bartman67/23y96BxKDdnWukAhhCFgDUq9ayrdvzJgV3UwGHkaFvZpeWnGufMUZCDPqLTUyjwnVpNef.jpg) --- #### Pablo Picasso --- ![Terracotta draped woman (3rd century BC). Tanagra with drapery (1951), Pablo Picasso.](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bartman67/2423qcm7NuwW3Zk2isqgTebws4o78V1y4S6PssUNfkSSM654YrxS9bwFbrbU7Aq1zRCpr.png) The fact that this was not just a passing fad is evidenced by none other than Pablo Picasso still drawing inspiration from Tanagras more than half a century later, as shown in the image above. He created his own \

(see image below, from [this website](https://picasso-ceramics.org/the-feminine-muse/))

![Blue Tanagra - Picasso (1947-48) - Photo by Eric Baudouin](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bartman67/23y94FBwRXPyUebWgrDRAZ1kBBQBqjLt2xUB7ZSiHk5kh3znX4CK6AoHyxE8hKch6nStz.png)

And it doesn't stop with Picasso: in 2022, his modern sculptures inspired the [model collection of Maison Alaïa](https://amagazinecuratedby.com/news/tanagras-from-picasso-to-alaia/). More than a century after the examples described above, Tanagras continue to inspire fashion.

---
#### Children's Story
---
<div class='pull-left'>

The fact that the craze wasn't limited to the 'serious' art world is evidenced by the appearance of children's stories about Tanagras. In 1898, the French [youth weekly \
](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k9114620d/f2.item) published a story about a dollmaker named Hermogène, titled \

.
![Illustration of Hermogène, the dollmaker - source: Gallica](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bartman67/EoySwzVqSGuRoksdS7NtyH1qQQBXPbZ8pK9C59kL9eMc97bXibdfPM1Z713YitPsK5e.png)
--- #### Tanagra by Villanis ---
![Tanagra - Emanuel Villanis - around 1900](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bartman67/EqhUbSdZ9mPg9Q37PY9pFTABuXVywbihynj3yyjrryk75qe6k4obXEwG7HavbyNKyrU.jpeg)
For me personally, it was this figurine by the French sculptor [Emmanuel Villanis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Villanis) (1858-1912) that led to my discovery of Tanagra. I came across it at an auction in 2024; I had never heard of Tanagra before, but I was far from the only interested party. It's not known exactly when he made it - probably between 1890-1900. It's one of the most successful and popular works in his oeuvre. Compared to his other work in the pronounced Art Nouveau style, it's less flamboyant and more restrained, almost serene. And notably: Villanis was clearly not inspired by the pleated dresses - which are completely absent - but rather by the tranquil beauty and mysterious gaze of the figurines.
--- ### In Conclusion --- It's remarkable how our culture recycles. More than two thousand years later, we still recognize the beauty of the Tanagras. We not only collect and admire them, but we create new sculptures, new paintings, clothing, and stories. Personally, two things have stayed with me from this quest: 1. You can, 150 years later, still follow almost step by step the development from a discovery to a trend to a craze. It does require some research, but we are talking about the time of our (great-)grandfathers! 2. How slow developments were back then compared to now! From 1870 well into the 20th century, whereas now we tend to speak of trends lasting 1 or a few years... --- ### Further Reading --- For those who can't get enough of Tanagras, a quick internet search reveals a wealth of information: * [Timeless Beauty in Tanagra Sculptures - Ruurd Halbertsma (pdf)](https://www.collectaaa.be/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/tanagranl.pdf) - Publication in Dutch by the National Museum of Antiquities in Leiden * [Short play (sketch) from 1939 about Tanagra](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bd6t51283961k/f6.image) * [Recent educational material about Tanagra](https://www.pedagogie.ac-nice.fr/dsden06/eac/wp-content/uploads/sites/5/2018/04/Tanagra.pdf) (pdf - in French) * [The diminutive dancing girl who made a big impression - By Susan Moore, 16 May 2018, Apollo Magazine](https://apollo-magazine.com/the-diminutive-dancing-girl-who-made-a-big-impression/) (online publication in English) |

‎Hello friends of Hive 👋, you are welcome to #Hive Learners Creative Sunday. I am @emmanuel50, and today I'm here with the Hausa cover song titled \

\n‎\n‎Takama is a Hausa song. This song is one of my favorite songs that I love to sing. I really enjoy this song because it has a powerful and incredible message that always touches my heart. Anytime I listen to this song, I always learn a lot from it. Takama in Hausa means \

and the song is all about people becoming proud and underrating their fellow human beings because of the things of this world. This song carries a really powerful message, and it illustrates to us that we don't have to be proud of the things we have. This song is passing a message, and it is telling us that we, as the children of God, should always appreciate and thank God for the things He has done in our lives, but not mock the people whom God has not blessed yet. Because if we become proud and underrate those whom God has not blessed, God will never be happy with us.
‎
‎I really love this song from the deepest part of my heart. This song has blessed me in diverse ways. Takama teaches me to love one another and to help those who are in need. It has taught me never to be proud of the things of this world because everything in this world is vanity upon vanity. Sincerely speaking, I have truly learned a lot from this beautiful and amazing song. The lyrics of this song carry such a powerful and heart-touching message. In fact, to me, this song is a life changer.

body.body: >\nGreetings everyone and all hivers around the world, its been few days since I did not create any post here in the community because of the past busy day i experienced. Yesterday was the last day of coconut harvesting activity and I am very excited to know the exact number of coconuts we harvested for the past previous days. Even if our town was celebrating fiesta, still we did our harvesting and gladly our workers are doing their best to finished their works before paying them for labor. We gathered the coconuts in one place so we can easily hauled it using wooden cart pulled with Carabao. \n</div class=\

>

![IMG20260612094805_01.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/EoAbfh2qVwPf2tb1BCN2Npuvv6RCbQxDD1hSuWU6SjPpD2tkkKZRKD1XKPrfdg6nDuA.jpg)
</center>
Early in the morning when our hauler was started to hauled some coconuts left here at the farm. Using this unique Wooden cart pulled with a Carabao, He carefully placed the coconuts inside the cart and it takes almost three hours of hauling activities. Carabao is very important here at the farm so we can carry lots of goods to be transfered from one place to another. I also kept myself busy checking the areas to see if all coconuts are hauled and no coconuts left or unnoticed. 

![IMG20260612081222_01.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/EoiW9Sfu5ZQFFpPVH6VaA3X3F9KS2MXXFNrYikmVYRijDS2XTi1GQuWDczSZALtrtcX.jpg)
</center>
While resting, I decided to eat my simple breakfast this Bihon combined with softdrinks is perfect to eat for breakfast. This bihon was given from our Neighbor who celebrated Her Birthday last day and lucky the food was not spoiled because we put it in the refrigerator. I was having an enjoyable and delicious breakfast since Bihon Dish is one of my favorite food to eat. 

![IMG20260612103103_01.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/EpCAQkvssLavpeUL8xSrL5wGbrz51gZSeWBNcQxwFWDUKePqvh7ffmbfwiyJc4FwBnm.jpg)
</center>
She also gave this pair of slippers and a pieces of biscuits. I was very thankful for her generosity and have a delicious snacks for snack time. This kind of biscuits is slightly expensive and I also gave her ripe Bananas as for exchange for her kindness and generosity. 


![IMG20260612135646_01.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/EpEJpHYxLnaLc4QodKY6N17ethZHHFbMg1YSmU7LZ63f9SiHM8qg4am74fZeemAfJAv.jpg)
</center>

![IMG20260612135636.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/EpA1bZLqWJFuJoiP1ZnsFMuP4BfxGbXtXMiSfVKs1VQhuoEumgmH22D12X3WEu1rWrc.jpg)
</center>

body.title: AI News Daily - June 14, 2026
body.body:
# AI News Daily - June 14, 2026

Today’s AI news is mostly about the operating layer: coding agents getting deeper browser/debugging powers, agent platforms getting plugin marketplaces, enterprise software exposing MCP tools, and frontier-model access becoming a policy and governance risk. I checked the last three AI News Daily posts before writing this. June 11 covered DiffusionGemma, visible Anthropic safeguards, OpenAI on Oracle, TCS/Anthropic, Anthropic policy, Gemini outage, the Meta support breach, and OpenClaw. June 12 covered OpenAI buying Ona, Codex rate-limit reset banking, Oracle procurement, Anthropic Fable transparency, DeepMind’s multi-agent safety fund, Gemini for Business Profiles, and Meta/Manus. June 13 covered Anthropic’s Fable/Mythos shutdown, Kimi K2.7 Code, AA-AgentPerf, Meta workforce changes, xAI turbine expansion, Gemini TV controls, and Claude Corps. I avoided repeating those unless there is a material new development.

## 1. xAI launched a Grok Build Plugin Marketplace for terminal agents

xAI announced the Grok Build Plugin Marketplace on June 11. This is a catch-up item from the last 2-3 days, and it was not covered in the last three AI News Daily posts. The marketplace lets Grok Build users browse, install, and update plugins from inside the terminal, with launch plugins from MongoDB, Vercel, Sentry, Chrome DevTools, Cloudflare, and Superpowers. xAI says plugins can bundle skills, slash commands, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and language servers into a single installable package.

That is the important part. Coding agents are becoming operating environments, not just chatbots that edit files. A plugin marketplace gives an agent a repeatable way to acquire domain-specific powers: inspect production errors, deploy to Vercel, query MongoDB, operate Cloudflare Workers, or attach to Chrome DevTools. xAI says remote plugins are pinned to commit SHAs and verified at install time, which is useful, but the broader trust problem remains: once agent plugins can perform real actions, marketplace review, permissions, provenance, and sandboxing become product-defining features.

My take: the coding-agent race is moving from model quality to ecosystem quality. The best terminal agent will not only be the one with the strongest model; it will be the one with safe, discoverable, maintained integrations that developers can actually trust.

Sources: https://x.ai/news/grok-plugin-marketplace · https://github.com/xai-org/plugin-marketplace · https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/06/11/xai-ships-grok-build-plugin-marketplace-with-mongodb-vercel-sentry-chrome-devtools-cloudflare-and-superpowers-plugins-at-launch/

## 2. OpenAI’s Codex added Developer Mode for browser debugging

OpenAI’s June 11 Codex changelog included a developer-impacting feature that deserves its own attention: Developer Mode for Browser use in Chrome and the Codex in-app browser. This is another catch-up item from June 11 that was not yet covered as its own story; June 12 covered Codex reset banking, but not this debugging change. Developer Mode gives Codex controlled Chrome DevTools Protocol access so it can profile performance, inspect network traffic, read console output, analyze runtime errors, and review page state.

That matters because frontend debugging is one of the places coding agents usually fall down. A text-only agent can guess at bugs from code, but real web issues often live in rendered DOM state, browser timing, hydration, missing assets, runtime errors, and layout behavior. Codex also added the `/init` command in the app composer for creating project instructions, plus performance improvements that OpenAI says make Browser use up to 2x faster through CDP and DOM snapshot optimizations.

My take: this is a practical step toward agents that verify their own work instead of stopping at “tests pass.” For web apps, browser instrumentation is not a luxury. It is the difference between a code-writing assistant and a debugging teammate that can inspect the actual running product.

Sources: https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog · https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes · https://developers.openai.com/codex/

## 3. Salesforce’s Summer ’26 release turns MCP into enterprise plumbing

Salesforce published its developer guide for the Summer ’26 release, with production rollouts landing June 12 and June 13 depending on the instance. This is one of the more important enterprise developer stories because Salesforce is turning major platform capabilities into APIs, CLI commands, and Model Context Protocol tools under the “Headless 360” umbrella. Standard hosted MCP servers are now generally available for SObject access, Data 360, and Tableau, while custom hosted MCP servers can expose Apex actions, Flows, Apex REST endpoints, AuraEnabled methods, Prompt Builder prompts, Agentforce agents, and API Catalog mappings.

Salesforce also added developer and designer MCP tools for coding agents. The DX MCP server includes SLDS guidance and ApexGuru-driven code review from org runtime metrics. The Metadata API Context MCP server now exposes more granular tools for generating metadata files with less token waste. Data 360, OmniStudio, Commerce Cloud, and Marketing Cloud Engagement all get agent-facing paths too. Salesforce is also open-sourcing a library of Agent Skills that work with Agentforce Vibes and can be installed into other coding agents.

My take: this is what enterprise AI adoption looks like when it gets serious. Instead of asking agents to scrape screens or memorize platform quirks, Salesforce is exposing governed tool surfaces. That is the right direction: agents need authenticated, auditable, permission-aware tools if they are going to touch real business systems.

Sources: https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2026/06/the-salesforce-developers-guide-to-the-summer-26-release · https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/mcp/overview · https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills

## 4. OpenAI reportedly faces a 42-state consumer-safety investigation

Business Insider reported today that OpenAI is facing an investigation from attorneys general across 42 U.S. states focused on ChatGPT’s effects on minors and vulnerable users, data handling, engagement practices, and safety controls. This is not a model launch, but it is strategically important enough to include because consumer-protection law may become one of the main ways AI products are governed before AI-specific law fully catches up.

The developer angle is straightforward: safety, age controls, memory, data use, and engagement loops are no longer only trust-and-safety policy decisions. They are product requirements with legal exposure. For AI app builders, the questions regulators are circling around are the same ones users will ask: What does the system remember? How does it respond to vulnerable users? Can minors use it safely? Are there dark patterns that encourage dependency? Can a user understand and control what the product does with their data?

My take: this is a warning shot for every consumer AI product, not just OpenAI. If your product offers companionship, advice, personalization, memory, or always-on engagement, you need safety design and clear data controls early. Retrofits are expensive, and investigations are even more expensive.

Sources: https://www.businessinsider.com/openai-states-investigation-chatgpt-impact-children-vulnerable-adults-2026-6 · https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/06/53183214/openai-reportedly-faces-legal-and-regulatory-storm-as-states-probe-ai-safety-and-consumer-protection · https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq

## 5. New reporting adds Amazon and White House details to Anthropic’s model shutdown

Yesterday’s June 13 post covered Anthropic disabling Fable 5 and Mythos 5 after a U.S. directive. The material new development today is reporting from Axios about how the shutdown happened. Axios says Amazon researchers found jailbreak paths and elevated concerns to U.S. officials, which helped trigger a rapid White House response. The report also says Anthropic had previously notified the government about the June 9 Fable release and that the government did not object at the time.

The underlying dispute is not only whether a jailbreak existed. It is whether the reported capability was unique enough to justify emergency export-style controls against one company’s top models. Anthropic’s position, as reported, is that the technique did not demonstrate a special flaw in Fable 5’s safety systems and that comparable assistance may be available from other models. Government officials, according to Axios, viewed Mythos-level capability as requiring a harder national-security process before public or foreign-national access.

My take: this is the clearest example yet that frontier model release is becoming a regulated operational event. Labs may need release playbooks that look more like aerospace or cybersecurity disclosure processes: prebriefings, red-team evidence, escalation paths, customer contingency plans, and a rollback strategy if government pressure lands after launch.

Sources: https://www.axios.com/2026/06/13/anthropic-amazon-white-house · https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/jun/13/anthropic-disable-advanced-ai-models-us-government-order · https://x.com/AnthropicAI/status/2065597531644743999

## 6. Meta starts putting controls around internal AI token spending

New reporting says Meta is tightening internal AI usage after employee token consumption approached huge cost levels. The company is reportedly moving away from “token-maxxing” culture toward centralized spend monitoring, AI Gateway controls, and budget discipline. This is a practical story, not a flashy one, but it belongs in today’s roundup because it is the enterprise AI adoption hangover in miniature.

The first wave of AI rollout is usually “give everyone access.” The second wave is “why is the bill so high?” The third wave has to be governance: which workflows are worth premium models, which can use cheaper models, where caching helps, when agents should stop, and how teams connect AI usage to actual business outcomes. Meta is not a normal enterprise buyer, but the lesson generalizes. If even Meta needs stronger token controls, ordinary companies definitely do.

My take: AI cost management is becoming an engineering discipline. Teams should expect model routing, quota policy, prompt optimization, eval-driven downgrade paths, caching, and usage analytics to become normal parts of production AI systems. The free-for-all era is ending.

Sources: https://mlq.ai/news/meta-caps-internal-ai-token-spending-after-costs-approach-billions-in-2026/ · https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/news/story/after-microsoft-and-uber-meta-is-also-dealing-with-soaring-ai-bills-caps-tokenmaxxing-2926101-2026-06-13 · https://www.wired.com/story/mark-zuckerberg-meta-employee-meeting-interrupt-ai/

## 7. AI adoption keeps getting more operational in commerce and healthcare

Two smaller stories today point in the same direction. Magicpin says its Vera AI assistant is scaling toward one million merchants by year-end, while King Faisal Specialist Hospital is using HLTH Europe to highlight human-centered AI systems aimed at reducing administrative burden and supporting clinicians. These are not frontier-model stories, and I would normally rank them below model and developer-tool news. I am including them because they show where AI is turning into operational infrastructure.

The common pattern is workflow integration. Merchants need help with listings, customer interaction, local discovery, and daily operations. Hospitals need documentation support, routing, triage, summarization, and administrative relief without compromising clinical judgment. In both cases, the value is not “AI can chat.” The value is AI embedded into repetitive, domain-specific processes where humans still own the outcome.

My take: the near-term winners in applied AI will be boring in a good way. They will not be blank chat boxes. They will be assistants wired into messy workflows, with enough context and guardrails to save time without pretending to replace the people accountable for the work.

Sources: https://m.economictimes.com/tech/technology/magicpin-scales-ai-assistant-vera-targets-over-10-lakh-merchants-by-2026-ceo/amp_articleshow/131716258.cms · https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/06/14/3311433/0/en/kfsh-highlights-human-centered-ai-as-a-path-to-better-care-at-hlth-europe-2026.html · https://www.hlth.com/events/europe

## Bottom line

The strongest signal today is that AI products are becoming systems of tools, policies, budgets, and operational dependencies. xAI and OpenAI are making coding agents more extensible and more capable of real debugging. Salesforce is exposing enterprise systems through MCP. Regulators are circling consumer AI safety. Anthropic’s shutdown shows frontier releases can collide with national-security process after launch. Meta’s token controls show that AI usage must be managed like infrastructure.

The practical takeaway: the model still matters, but the surrounding system now matters just as much. The durable advantage is in integrations, permissions, observability, lifecycle management, cost controls, and clear safety behavior.

---

AI News Daily is researched and written with AI assistance, then reviewed and edited for clarity, usefulness, and source quality.

body.body:
https://youtu.be/czrkocLZzR0
There is a temptation, especially now, to wonder whether tutorials are even necessary anymore. We live at the dawn of a new kind of assistance: an AI that can answer almost any specific question the moment it comes up. So why sit through a forty minute tutorial when you could just ask, the instant you get stuck?

Both approaches have a place, and they are not really in competition.

Tutorials do something an AI answer cannot: they map out a territory before you have a reason to go there. They give you vocabulary, the names for things like feedback loops, displacement, level remapping, so that later, when you hit a wall, you actually know what to search for or ask about. Without that vocabulary, even a good AI assistant becomes harder to use, because you do not yet know the shape of the question you are trying to ask.

Asking AI in the moment is best suited to concrete, verifiable problems. Getting stuck on XYZ coordinate mapping and asking for a fix is a perfect example: the question is specific, the answer can be plugged in immediately, and you can see right away whether it worked. That is a genuinely good use of the tool, and there is nothing lesser about reaching for it.

Although I made it through, what I wanted to create turned out different because I didn't follow any tutorial, much like the tutorial above, which you can find on my Patreon.

body.title: 🐜 Camponotus nicobarensis – Week 9 | More Brood and a New Arena
body.body:
# 🐜 Camponotus nicobarensis – Week 9 | More Brood and a New Arena

<center>
![20260614_090847.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ant.runner/EpLgzngS8uEz1coYu7PDzFzVcYmkdV4oTBLGgo2eEwWLeTcoSmC94f4Z1YuXtffE6Ww.jpg)
</center>

### 📈 Current Status

* Queen: 1
* Workers: approximately 16
* Brood: significantly increased

The colony continues to develop very well.

With around 16 workers now, counting every individual is becoming increasingly difficult. Thanks to the many hiding places available, the ants spend much more time outside the test tube, so future worker counts will likely be estimates rather than exact numbers.

The most encouraging development is the brood. After several workers emerged over the past weeks, the brood pile has grown noticeably again and now contains a healthy number of larvae and pupae.

---

## 🥚 The Brood Is Growing Again

<center>
![20260614_090821.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ant.runner/EoyQ1bvymG16rLjgNUmZ6WYpyzCtqGsAS7RK2evafW31mJ1tYij8tVgLbYxNAcAA8Rs.jpg)
</center>

Just a few weeks ago, the brood appeared smaller because several pupae had emerged as new workers.

Now the situation has changed completely.

The queen continues to produce new offspring, and the workers are actively caring for the developing brood. The test tube once again contains a substantial amount of larvae and pupae.

It seems the colony has successfully moved beyond its first small growth phase.

---

## 🏗️ Expanding the Setup

<center>
![20260614_090746.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ant.runner/EowG79uSrzzmR49fnBNMnmGNHwegpy1Mw2z1UQosbN9nkrHddBFc9EHwewYVAzhyWcJ.jpg)
</center>

This week also brought the first major expansion to the setup.

I connected a new arena measuring **10 × 10 × 20 cm**.

Instead of adding a deep substrate layer, I only used a thin layer of ground cover and filled the arena mainly with small branches.

This creates plenty of climbing opportunities and hiding spots, which Camponotus nicobarensis seem to appreciate.

The setup also looks much more natural compared to a completely open arena.

---

## 🕷️ An Unexpected Visitor

<center>
![20260614_090730.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ant.runner/Ep5o9hVnwYA8KkzZiRjsMmniR7pRC1cCDNxdijmBNFyY2B1qE28UV6CZ9yV49Ui2z6h.jpg)
</center>

While setting up the new arena, I noticed a small surprise.

A tiny spider apparently made its way into the setup together with the branches.

For now, I have decided not to remove it. Instead, I'm curious to see how long it can survive in the arena and how the ants will react to their unexpected new neighbor.

My guess is that a growing Camponotus colony will eventually have the upper hand, but as a small accidental experiment, it will be interesting to watch.

That said, I still hope that no actual pests found their way into the setup along with the natural materials.

---

## 🔌 Preparing for Future Expansions

Since Camponotus nicobarensis are known for their rapid growth, I have already connected additional tubing for future expansions.

At the moment these connections do not lead anywhere, but they will make future upgrades much easier to implement.

The colony does not need the extra space yet, but I prefer preparing early rather than having to redesign everything later under time pressure.

---

## 🐜 Activity Continues to Increase

With every new worker, the arenas become more active.

It is now common to see multiple ants exploring outside the test tube at the same time, moving through both the original and the newly connected arena.

The branches seem to be especially popular, with workers frequently climbing and investigating the new structures.

The colony is clearly entering a new stage of development.

---

## 🧠 Personal Thoughts

Watching this Camponotus nicobarensis colony develop remains incredibly enjoyable.

The combination of increasing activity, growing brood numbers, and the first setup expansions means that something new seems to happen almost every week.

The colony is still small, but it already feels much more alive than it did only a few weeks ago.

---

## 🔎 Looking Ahead

Over the next few weeks, I'm especially looking forward to:

* more workers emerging
* continued brood development
* seeing how the colony uses the new arena
* and finding out when they begin fully utilizing all connected areas of the setup

---

👉 How early do you expand your Camponotus colonies? Do you wait until space becomes limited, or do you prefer to prepare ahead of time?

body.title: Animal Connection
body.body: Capturing these moments was all about patience and waiting for that split second when the animal feels completely at ease with you It is amazing how much personality shows up in a frame once the barrier between human and wildlife just disappears If you love seeing these raw and funny connections as much as I do please share the love Cheers 🥰 Morteza Yousefi

/> Photographing animals especially primates requires a totally different mindset than shooting landscapes or architecture because you are dealing with living beings that have their own moods and agendas When you work with monkeys you quickly realize that they are incredibly curious and social creatures which makes them fascinating but also very unpredictable subjects The secret to getting a great shot is often just sitting back and letting them get used to your presence until you are no longer a stranger to them but just another part of their environment You have to be ready to capture the small things a look of surprise a gentle touch or a funny expression because those are the details that tell a real story and make people feel a connection to the animal It is also important to remember that when we take these photos we are guests in their world so respect and safety always have to come first From a technical side you need a fast shutter speed to keep up with their quick movements but the real magic is in the timing and finding that perfect composition where the focus is sharp right on their expressive eyes Beyond the technical gear it is a meditative process that teaches you to slow down observe patterns and appreciate the intelligence behind those watchful gazes Whether you are in a dense forest or a sanctuary the goal is the same which is to showcase their unique spirit and remind us of the shared connection we have with the natural world Sharing these moments is my way of bringing a little piece of that wild unpredictable beauty into your day and I hope it reminds you that sometimes the best photos are the ones that capture a feeling instead of just a pose
/>\n\nThis is my entry for the #monomad challenge

body.title: Jak psychologia i nowoczesna technologia kształtują współczesny iGaming?
body.body:
Współczesna branża rozrywki online to jeden z najbardziej fascynujących poligonów doświadczalnych dla innowacji technologicznych. To, co zaczęło się dekady temu jako proste przeniesienie gier mechanicznych do świata bitów i bajtów, dziś stanowi potężny ekosystem, w którym zaawansowana matematyka spotyka się z psychologią behawioralną. iGaming w 2026 roku to nie tylko „gry losowe” – to precyzyjnie zaprojektowane interaktywne doświadczenia, które wykorzystują najnowsze osiągnięcia w dziedzinie User Experience (UX), aby dostarczyć użytkownikom bezpiecznej i angażującej rozrywki na najwyższym poziomie.

Dla świadomego użytkownika internetu w Polsce, kluczowym wyzwaniem staje się zrozumienie mechanizmów, które sprawiają, że dana platforma jest godna zaufania. W zalewie ofert marketingowych, rzetelna informacja i twarde dane techniczne stały się najsilniejszą kartą w ręku gracza. Aby mądrze nawigować po tym dynamicznym rynku i odróżnić merytoryczne recenzje od pustych haseł reklamowych, warto korzystać z profesjonalnych baz wiedzy. Pod adresem <https://top-casino-online.pl> można znaleźć szczegółowe audyty techniczne i zestawienia, które pozwalają na chłodno ocenić parametry takie jak uczciwość algorytmów RNG czy realną wypłacalność operatorów. Taka edukacja rynkowa jest dziś fundamentem bezpiecznej zabawy w cyfrowym świecie.

### Psychologia „bliskiej wygranej” i pętla dopaminowa

Jednym z najbardziej intrygujących zjawisk w projektowaniu nowoczesnych gier jest mechanizm znany jako „Near Miss” (bliska wygrana). Z matematycznego punktu widzenia, gdy na bębnach automatu brakuje jednego symbolu do ułożenia najwyższej kombinacji, jest to przegrana jak każda inna. Jednak badania neurologiczne wykazują, że ludzki mózg interpretuje taką sytuację jako sygnał: „byłeś blisko, następnym razem się uda”.

Nowoczesne platformy wykorzystują tę wiedzę nie po to, by manipulować, ale by budować dreszczyk emocji, który jest esencją tej formy rozrywki. Kluczem do zachowania zdrowego dystansu jest świadomość, że każdy spin jest niezależnym zdarzeniem statystycznym generowanym przez certyfikowany algorytm, a wizualna oprawa to jedynie estetyczny dodatek do czystej matematyki.

### Matematyka jako gwarancja uczciwości

W 2026 roku zaufanie buduje się na parametrach technicznych, z których najważniejszym jest **RTP (Return to Player)**. Jest to wskaźnik, który informuje gracza, jaki procent postawionych środków statystycznie wraca do społeczności w długim terminie. Standardem dla platform premium są dziś tytuły oferujące RTP na poziomie 96-98%.

Równie istotna jest **zmienność (volatility)**. Określa ona profil ryzyka danej gry:

*   **Niska zmienność:** Częste, ale mniejsze wygrane, idealne dla graczy szukających relaksu i dłuższej sesji.

*   **Wysoka zmienność:** Rzadsze, ale potencjalnie spektakularne wypłaty, dedykowane osobom o większym budżecie i cierpliwości.

Zrozumienie tych zależności pozwala na lepsze zarządzanie kapitałem i dostosowanie tempa gry do własnych preferencji, co jest kluczowe dla polityki odpowiedzialnej gry.

### Sztuczna Inteligencja: Cichy strażnik bezpieczeństwa

Największym przełomem technologicznym ostatnich lat jest wdrożenie Sztucznej Inteligencji (AI) w systemy ochrony gracza. Algorytmy machine learning monitorują wzorce zachowań w czasie rzeczywistym. Ich zadaniem jest wczesne wykrywanie anomalii, które mogą świadczyć o utracie kontroli nad grą lub o próbach oszustw. Nowoczesne systemy potrafią proaktywnie zasugerować użytkownikowi przerwę lub automatycznie nałożyć limity depozytów, zanim problem stanie się realny. To etyczne podejście do biznesu, wspierane przez technologię, buduje trwałą lojalność i odróżnia liderów branży od podmiotów nastawionych na krótkoterminowy zysk.

### Świadomy wybór to podstawa

iGaming w 2026 roku to triumf technologii, designu i przejrzystości. Wybierając sprawdzone, licencjonowane i rzetelnie przetestowane platformy, gracze zyskują dostęp do rozrywki na światowym poziomie. Pamiętajmy jednak, że informacja jest najpotężniejszym narzędziem w cyfrowym świecie. Zawsze weryfikujmy parametry techniczne platform przed podjęciem jakichkolwiek decyzji finansowych i stawiajmy na źródła, które opierają swoje opinie na faktach, a nie na marketingu. iGaming jutra to przestrzeń bezpieczna i transparentna – o ile korzystamy z niej z głową.

body.title: [ENG-SPN] The Day They Mistook a King for a Pirate / El Día que Confundieron a un Rey con un Pirata
body.body:
![DSCN0464.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/Eos1n4DJiew3hxDH26s7LtGF55HuEShMRxmWU1EunyYz6tK2Ec9FxEEx7Jum4nssUfm.JPG)

Now it's another one of those idyllic fishing villages whose population swells every summer thanks to tourists captivated by its unique charm: Tazones. But there was a time when this picturesque place, located at the head of the Villaviciosa Estuary, was a simple fishing village that almost changed the destiny of Spain.

![DSCN0476.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/EptcrFbuTuFXXhj1sEe96CiY56NtQfVpA3zAGXQ7VjQGWFhUXzCqJEyHXgZExL9hBz6.JPG)

It happened around the 15th century, when the young Charles V of Germany was sailing towards Spain to take the throne as Charles I. The port he was scheduled to visit was Laredo, in neighboring Cantabria. But fate, always at the mercy of the whims of the Wheel of Fortune, had other plans and, unleashing a terrible storm, drove him dozens of kilometers away from the Cantabrian coast.

![DSCN0463.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/EqSW1ZvKHuanQiG7GbxYkAgRZuDC17C6APYUiMhm2aw9hn7rmCqbsr6SESxECEWqAZ3.JPG)

These were times when piracy was still rampant, and the Asturian coast, despite the protection of its steep cliffs and the rough waters of its seas, was not immune to unwanted visitors. When the entourage of the phlegmatic future emperor disembarked, setting foot on these waters for the first time, much like the daring astronaut Neil Armstrong on the dusty surface of the moon, they were mistaken for pirates and nearly hanged—an event that would have completely altered the course of Spain, under whose reign it was always said that the sun never set.

![DSCN0467.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/EqDk4dmSNEME9mfhfv1WBSxWHohRfhZqXCMQqkvqzNhzsuXrqBQ4TC17pHrweT9HdHA.JPG)

Ahora es otro de esos idílicos pueblecitos de pescadores que todos los veranos ve multiplicada su población por un turismo enamorado de su peculiar encanto: Tazones. Pero hubo un tiempo, en el que este pintoresco lugar, situado a la vanguardia de la Ría de Villaviciosa, era una sencilla aldea de marineros, que a punto estuvo de cambiar el destino de España.

![DSCN0462.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/EoEp9iM7Ug8SqNkGo2exF5ri37jj1x7a7mtDFAEpjeJvB45TrYSXQZdpunbDu6jYUSg.JPG)

Ocurrió, aproximadamente, en el siglo XV, cuando el joven Carlos V de Alemania navegaba hacia España para hacerse cargo del trono, con el nombre de Carlos I. El puerto que tenía previsto acogerlo, era el de Laredo, situado en la vecina Cantabria. Pero el destino, siempre servil a merced de los caprichos de la Rueda de la Fortuna, tenía otros planes y desencadenando una terrible tormenta, lo alejó decenas de kilómetros de las costas cántabras.

![DSCN0478.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/EoiUnGf69AcGWVSpeoqa1Pi7VdSee91qjLUaDFP7SCjoeZtePpXAA2akzWiSWku1Fwa.JPG)

Eran tiempos en los que la piratería todavía estaba en pleno auge y las costas asturianas, a pesar de la salvaguarda de sus abruptos acantilados y la bravura de sus aguas, no eran inmunes a visitas no deseadas. Cuando el séquito del flemático y futuro emperador desembarcó, poniendo por primera vez el pie en estas aguas, como hiciera el atrevido astronauta Neil Amrstrong sobre la polvorienta superficie de la luna, fueron confundidos con piratas y poco faltó para que fueran ahorcados, hecho que hubiera dado un giro total a una España, bajo cuyo reinado, siempre se dijo aquello de que no se ponía el sol.

![DSCN0480.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/Eq36YQw9E21pvHo53QQubcLZKXEfwoLZ3z4wUmDrrjNf9VWxb9uWJp1xL9veA3e2zWe.JPG)

body.body: Have you ever been to a mineral water pool?\n\nOr do you think that the Romans did not \

with their famous Roman baths scattered everywhere? 😉 (of course where there are mineral water springs) I have been to such pools several times in my life, but now for the first time I had the physical need to visit one of them. Due to health/physical trauma reasons. But I never imagined that along with physical healing, this mineral water pool would have a beneficial effect on many other levels and on my psyche. That is why today I invite you to come with me on a visit to this place, where I hope you will feel the same as I did then.

/> This mineral water swimming complex in the village called Mineralni Bani/Mineral Water Baths (and how else 😄), bears the pompous name Daisy Palace. There is a hotel and a pool complex here, but in fact, I'm not sure the hotel works. Anyway, not the hotel, but the pools are the topic and reason of this post.
/> At the entrance of the pool you will be greeted politely and you will pay BGN 11 (for children the ticket is cheaper) And so - for about 5.50 euros you will have a deck chair and umbrella:
/> a small pool full of mineral water:
/> large pool with diluted mineral water to be able to swim in it:
/> trampoline.... And one more thing. Many more things.

>

Soul's Detour is a project started by me years ago when I had a blog about historical and not so popular tourist destinations in Eastern Belgium, West Germany and Luxembourg. Nowadays, this blog no longer exists, but I'm still here - passionate about architecture, art and mysteries and eager to share my discoveries and point of view with you.

body.title: 🌱 Onion Transplant Day – A Big Step Toward a Successful Harvest
body.body:
Today was an important day on our homestead as we officially transplanted our onion seedlings into the field. After weeks of carefully nurturing them in the nursery, the seedlings were finally strong enough to move to their permanent growing beds. This is one of those farming days that requires patience, teamwork, and attention to detail, but it is also one of the most rewarding stages of crop production.
The morning started with preparing the seedlings for transplanting. We carefully uprooted the young onions, making sure to preserve as much of the root system as possible. Healthy roots are essential because they help the seedlings establish quickly after being moved. Looking at the bunches of fresh green seedlings in our hands was a reminder of how much growth can happen from a tiny seed with proper care.
Once the seedlings were ready, we moved them to the prepared beds. The soil had already been worked and drip irrigation lines were installed to ensure efficient water delivery throughout the growing season. Having a drip system in place is a great advantage because it helps conserve water while providing consistent moisture directly to the root zone.
Transplanting onions requires proper spacing to allow enough room for bulb development. We carefully placed each seedling into the soil, row after row, making sure they were positioned correctly. It was a labor-intensive process, but teamwork made the task much easier and more enjoyable. Every planted row represented progress and brought us one step closer to harvest.
After transplanting, the field received a thorough irrigation. Water is critical immediately after transplanting because it helps eliminate air pockets around the roots and reduces transplant shock. By the end of the day, the beds were well-watered and the seedlings had already begun settling into their new environment.
Farming always teaches patience. Although the field may not look impressive to some people today, we know that every mature onion bulb begins with a small seedling like these. Over the coming weeks, we will focus on irrigation management, weed control, and proper nutrition to encourage healthy growth.
Days like this remind us that successful farming is built on consistent effort rather than instant results. We are excited to watch these onions grow and look forward to sharing updates as the season progresses.

>

Hello, coffee lovers! Welcome back to my blog. Today, I’d love to share with you how I celebrated the grand opening of a new coffee shop in my city with a delicious, frothy latte. Join me, and I’ll tell you all about it.


<center>
![1000485394.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/chacald.dcymt/EoyRUAJ4QppkzxaKLSVEKhvNfGj83ooWwQgpc41aLJgMbTyYATZjaEqVr5WEZvRditc.jpg) </center>


<div class = \

>

I was running some errands and taking care of paperwork when a man opened a glass door and invited me in. The aroma of coffee literally drew me to the table. They told me it was opening day and that they had a wide variety of coffee to offer, and that the barista was eager to show off his latte art.

Without thinking twice, I ordered a vanilla latte because that sweet aroma tempted me. While they were bringing my coffee, I took in the small space—everything was laid out beautifully with that sophisticated touch of a city café. I loved every detail.

<center>
![1000485400.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/chacald.dcymt/Eoc8yHYBqVmpe2yRTsvvWy6mFA2eniu8AdVooEqnj7jVoz47mWb8CowLGAVQua7nnQe.jpg)</center>

<div class = \

>

They had some balloons out to celebrate. Even though they were still setting things up and hadn’t launched their social media yet, they were doing everything they could to provide the best café service.

Several weeks ago, I’d seen them building this place, but it wasn’t until they put up the coffee bean decorations that I realized it would become one of my favorite spots in town.

<center>
![1000485390.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/chacald.dcymt/23wgHhNnQrqkMJviCsVpskbP27WPY1hNqcYoKwQ2MMtJzot7iRoJQnfGTPTzskerpwWdy.jpg)</center>


<div class = \

> My town is small and doesn’t have many coffee shops to visit. But here, I hope every visit is a unique experience. They offer specialty beans, beans sourced from different parts of the world, but my favorite will always be the local bean that comes from our own land. They even offered me an iced coffee served with one of their traditional desserts. I loved this place and hope to visit again very soon. Thanks for joining me in discovering this new coffee shop—see you next time. Bye!
![1000485392.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/chacald.dcymt/23vhwrqZ4ubKrzpeCyPN66xQkTB8xduyPmxX2i9aYvWMT82vbSMhQmmCqFBwmK3CLMrNE.jpg)

>

¡Saludos amantes del café! Sean bienvenidos una vez más a mi blog, en esta oportunidad me encantaría compartir con ustedes como fue que estrené una cafetería en mi ciudad con un delicioso y espumoso Latte. Acompáñenme y les cuento.

<center>

body.title: 🌌 “No era un sueño… era el momento exacto en que el día dejó de ser normal”
body.body:
Desperté con una sensación difícil de explicar.
No era miedo.
No era cansancio.
Era esa intuición incómoda de que algo ya había ocurrido… sin mí.
Salí a la calle.
Todo parecía normal.
Demasiado normal.
Las personas caminaban, hablaban, reían… pero había algo extraño en sus movimientos, como si siguieran un guion que yo no había leído.
En la esquina, el semáforo cambió de color… pero nadie reaccionó al cambio.
Como si el tiempo no fuera igual para todos.
Entré a un café buscando algo familiar.
El barista me miró solo un segundo de más.
Lo suficiente para hacerme dudar.
El café llegó perfecto.
Demasiado perfecto.
Como si no hubiera sido hecho… sino recreado.
Saqué el teléfono.
La pantalla tardó en encender.
Y cuando lo hizo, no vi la hora.
Vi un mensaje que no debería estar ahí:
“Hoy ya ocurrió. Estás en la repetición.”
Sentí un vacío extraño en el estómago. Miré a mi alrededor.
Nadie parecía haberlo leído.
O peor…
Tal vez yo era el único que aún no debía saberlo.
Antes de poder reaccionar, el mensaje cambió:
“¿Quieres recordar lo que pasó antes de despertar?”
Y ahí me quedé.
Mirando la pantalla.
Sin saber si lo peor era la pregunta…
o que una parte de mí quería decir que sí.Ahora dime algo tú:
Si descubrieras que estás repitiendo el mismo día sin saberlo…
¿querrías seguir igual o recordar lo que pasó antes?

body.body:
# <center> World Cup </center>
#

I love football, as you know.

So inevitably I love the world cup, when the best players in the world come together to try to win this famous trophy.


![FIFA-World-Cup-trophy.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUDe7aSB5TGYcf5Ln6ztaf7mtJxPq8GFNkXyeBu2tfwzn/FIFA-World-Cup-trophy.jpg)

It's more than a little heart breaking that Ireland didn't manage to make it to World Cup 26. After a terrible start to their small group of four teams, they completed a famous double of wins against Portugal (2-0) and Hungary (3-2) to book their place in a play off.

That play off started perfectly with Ireland going 2-0 up in the first half, but they let it slip and Czechia took full advantage drawing level and beating us on penalty kicks, a sickening way to go out of any tournament, just ask our closest neighbours England...

Anyway that's a story for a different day, alas Ireland are not there this time and the wait goes on for our fourth appearance - 1990, 1994 and 2002 being our other times.

Lots of the matches here are on at stupid o clock, so I've only seen around three full matches so far, with Canada vs Bosnia and the first half of Brazil vs Morocco the pick of them.

![download.webp](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTuM4kQjRtvYaiZZpgjxoxwxaaQHDQpSimMUKStpnKrTV/download.webp)

So I had a choice to make last night before watching the Qataris take on the Swiss.

What would be the tipple of choice?

Some decent normal and non alcoholic choices peered out from the fridge.

![20260614_095328.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaKxW7avPYgQJ4K5JKRdvGFQKKrw8b5TaCP1ahkquWrNe/20260614_095328.jpg)

![20260614_095320.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmciWRS4m8XjkHbjSuzYB6sn7f3EbYjwe5eVxkw5wGdq15/20260614_095320.jpg)
 
In the end I went with Vino Tinto!

My brother in law won this bottle in a raffle and because he lives in Dublin, he told me to just have it.


![IMG-20260613-WA0010.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXmELwMe37Pe71qif8SG6jVjnkH6ujyWYZm83RY6eoC8h/IMG-20260613-WA0010.jpg)

So have it I did, with some nice Lindt dark chocolate 🍫 👌

![IMG-20260613-WA0011.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXSz2u9UbQHM6482Zino4jApuzTgnLikrevj818RxHGPA/IMG-20260613-WA0011.jpeg)


Well, that's it.

Until next time Beer Saturdayorians...

Oh by the way...

How was your Beer Saturday?

Where were you?

What was the drink of choice?

Who was with you?

Are those your feet?

How's your auld one?

Any other craic?

body.title: Writing Prompt: “not gonna fail this time”, entry posted by thepavsalford
body.body:
A big hug to all members of the Freewriters community!

May writing inspiration always be with you.

This is my entry to the Writing Prompt by @mariannewest for [13 June 2026, Freewriters Community Daily Writing Prompt Day 3133: not gonna fail this time](https://ecency.com/@daily.prompt/13-june-2026-freewriters-community-daily-writing-prompt-day-3133-not-gonna-fail-this-time).

How long will it take me to become a successful writer?

Will my articles and books manage to attract readers right from the beginning or will I have to hone my writing skills and rise to the ranks of successful authors slowly and steadily with time?

I don’t know how much I would be willing to pay, if a person could safely answer these questions, but I don’t think there is anyone who could give a definite answer, because nobody really knows, and neither do I.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6qxPce1M9lc

One thing is for sure though.

I’m not gonna fail this time.

I’ve written for various online writing platforms since the dawn of the era of user-generated content and online writing, and I’ve witnessed the eventual decline and demise of them, leaving writers like myself out in the cold and looking for greener pastures.

The thing is that after you get your feet wet as a writer, you are bitten by the bug of having your thoughts and ideas published and read by people, and there is no way back, even you don’t realize it yourself.

Because, at the end of the day, writing is a lifelong habit that you can’t break.

It’s a one-way street.

The only solution is to accept yourself as a writer first, before others are ready to accept you as such.

So yes, I have to keep a positive mind at all times, and reject failure as an option.

吃不完吃不完 根本吃不完哈哈哈😃今天早上本来是打算走小菜园拔点小葱后 在去菜场的，到了小菜园后就走不动了哈～好多天没过来了想看看我的紫苏、鸡毛菜、小米椒和南瓜🎃的长势。还没到，经过闺蜜妈妈的小菜园 她就告诉我，说我家菜园的菜长的很好！

两个人跟我说南瓜不结果，那我肯定要来确定一下有没有挂果，刚开始南瓜藤上开的都是公花 这是正常的。第一个抢镜的当然是小番茄啦🍅有些已经成熟了，红红的看着就喜人😊这番茄真的能长，枝条都压弯了呦！一通摘摘摘……还摘了一个小号的普罗旺斯，挂太多果了，长得就小，把番茄顶全部打了，疯长得枝条也打了一些，让养分全部去到番茄。

掐了一些紫苏叶，够我用来做一次紫苏饼了，叶子有点被虫子吃了，它们是饿晕了吗？啥时候 紫苏的味道也可以接受了。鸡毛菜也拔了一些，太密了！大的拔了小的才有机会长嘛！

辣椒长得也挺好，花挺多 辣椒也挂了一些，只是我买了3种辣椒，螺丝椒和薄皮椒，还有一个玉脂小米辣，螺丝椒好像没看到呢，玉脂长势差点，感觉缺水缺肥。

瓜类也不错，黄瓜今天摘了6根，我的贝贝南瓜也开始挂果了，不过长势一副缺肥的样子，西瓜也一样，挂果缺肥状态！豆角长势也不错，小豆角已经长到差不多筷子长度了。茄子秧长得特别壮大！今天又收获一个大茄子。

满载而归！都不用去菜场了呢～就是我的衣服从白色已经变成花绿白了😂鞋上也是粘满了泥巴，在每样菜间摘果还是有点累的，主要脚下不太好走，但是很开心～



---

## Speaker verification vs speaker identification

Before we write any code, let me clarify the two main tasks in speaker recognition. They sound similar but they're fundamentally different problems.

**Speaker verification** (SV) answers a yes/no question: _\

_ You have a stored voiceprint (an embedding vector from enrollment) and a new audio sample. Compute the similarity. If it's above a threshold -- accept. Below -- reject. This is a **binary classification** problem (same speaker or different speaker), and it's what banks use for phone authentication, what smart speakers use for personalization, and what forensic analysts use for voice matching.\n\n**Speaker identification** (SI) answers a who question: _\

_ You have a database of enrolled speakers with their voiceprints. Given a new audio clip, find the closest match. This is an **N-way classification** problem, and it's what meeting transcription systems and surveillance systems use.

Both tasks rely on the same foundation: **speaker embeddings** -- fixed-dimensional vectors that capture the essential characteristics of a voice while being invariant to what's being said, background noise, and recording conditions. The quality of your embeddings determines the quality of everything downstream:

## Speaker embeddings: d-vectors and x-vectors

A speaker embedding model takes a variable-length audio segment and produces a fixed-size vector that captures vocal identity. Two segments from the same speaker should produce similar vectors; segments from different speakers should produce distant vectors. This is conceptually identical to how FaceNet (episode #88) maps face images to embedding vectors -- same problem, different modality.

**D-vectors** (Variani et al., 2014; Wan et al., 2018) use the simplest possible approach: process Mel spectrogram frames through an LSTM (episode #49), then average the frame-level hidden states to get a single utterance-level vector:

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
import numpy as np


class DVectorModel(nn.Module):
    \

def __init__(self, n_mels=40,
                 hidden=256,
                 embed_dim=256,
                 n_layers=3):
        super().__init__()
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(
            n_mels, hidden, n_layers,
            batch_first=True)
        self.proj = nn.Linear(
            hidden, embed_dim)

    def forward(self, mel_frames):
        \

output, _ = self.lstm(mel_frames)
        # Average pooling over time
        embedding = output.mean(dim=1)
        embedding = self.proj(embedding)
        return F.normalize(
            embedding, dim=1)


# Demo

# Simulate 2 utterances: 3 sec
# and 5 sec at ~100 frames/sec

utt_long = torch.randn(1, 500, 40)

emb_short = model(utt_short)
emb_long = model(utt_long)

```

The averaging over time is what makes d-vectors length-invariant -- a 2-second clip and a 10-second clip both produce a 256-dimensional vector. Simple and effective, but the averaging loses temporal information. A speaker who emphasizes certain sounds differently at the beginning versus end of an utterance -- that nuance gets averaged away.

**X-vectors** (Snyder et al., 2018) replaced the LSTM with a **TDNN** (Time-Delay Neural Network) -- essentially 1D convolutions at different temporal strides -- followed by a **statistics pooling** layer that computes both the mean AND standard deviation across time:

```python
class XVectorModel(nn.Module):
    \

def __init__(self, n_mels=40,
                 embed_dim=512):
        super().__init__()
        # TDNN layers with increasing
        # temporal context
        self.tdnn1 = nn.Conv1d(
            n_mels, 512, 5, padding=2)
        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm1d(512)
        self.tdnn2 = nn.Conv1d(
            512, 512, 3,
            dilation=2, padding=2)
        self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm1d(512)
        self.tdnn3 = nn.Conv1d(
            512, 512, 3,
            dilation=3, padding=3)
        self.bn3 = nn.BatchNorm1d(512)
        self.tdnn4 = nn.Conv1d(
            512, 512, 1)
        self.bn4 = nn.BatchNorm1d(512)
        self.tdnn5 = nn.Conv1d(
            512, 1500, 1)
        self.bn5 = nn.BatchNorm1d(1500)

        # Stats pooling: mean + std
        # = 1500 * 2 = 3000 dim
        self.embed = nn.Linear(
            3000, embed_dim)

    def forward(self, mel):
        \

x = F.relu(self.bn1(
            self.tdnn1(mel)))
        x = F.relu(self.bn2(
            self.tdnn2(x)))
        x = F.relu(self.bn3(
            self.tdnn3(x)))
        x = F.relu(self.bn4(
            self.tdnn4(x)))
        x = F.relu(self.bn5(
            self.tdnn5(x)))

        # Statistics pooling
        mean = x.mean(dim=2)
        std = x.std(dim=2)
        pooled = torch.cat(
            [mean, std], dim=1)

        embedding = self.embed(pooled)
        return F.normalize(
            embedding, dim=1)


model = XVectorModel()
mel = torch.randn(2, 40, 300)
emb = model(mel)
print(f\

)
```

The **statistics pooling** is the key innovation here. By computing the standard deviation across time in addition to the mean, the model captures not just _what_ the voice sounds like on average but _how much it varies_. Some speakers have very consistent vocal characteristics across an utterance; others modulate pitch and energy dramatically. That variation pattern is itself an identity signal. None the less, the dilation factors in the TDNN layers (2, 3) give later layers progressively wider temporal context without increasing the number of parameters -- same idea as dilated convolutions in WaveNet (episode #94).

## Modern speaker embeddings: ECAPA-TDNN

Modern speaker embedding models like **ECAPA-TDNN** (Desplanques et al., 2020) improve on x-vectors with three additions: **channel attention** (Squeeze-and-Excitation blocks that let the network focus on the most informative frequency channels), **residual connections** (so gradients flow through deep networks), and **multi-layer feature aggregation** (combining features from multiple TDNN layers before pooling, rather than using only the last layer):

```python
class ChannelAttention(nn.Module):
    \

def __init__(self, ch):
        super().__init__()
        self.attn = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv1d(ch, 128, 1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv1d(128, ch, 1),
            nn.Softmax(dim=2))

    def forward(self, x):
        w = self.attn(x)
        mean = (x * w).sum(dim=2)
        var = ((x**2*w).sum(dim=2)
               - mean**2)
        std = torch.sqrt(
            var.clamp(min=1e-9))
        return torch.cat(
            [mean, std], dim=1)


class SimpleECAPATDNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_mels=80,
                 embed_dim=192):
        super().__init__()
        self.layer1 = nn.Conv1d(
            n_mels, 512, 5, padding=2)
        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm1d(512)
        self.se1 = ChannelAttention(512)
        self.layer2 = nn.Conv1d(
            512, 512, 3, dilation=2,
            padding=2)
        self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm1d(512)
        self.se2 = ChannelAttention(512)
        self.layer3 = nn.Conv1d(
            512, 512, 3, dilation=3,
            padding=3)
        self.bn3 = nn.BatchNorm1d(512)
        self.se3 = ChannelAttention(512)

The **attentive statistics pooling** learns which frames are most informative for speaker identity. Frames with clear speech get high attention; noisy or silent frames get low attention. This makes the model robust to variable-length inputs with noisy segments.

These models are trained with **angular margin losses** like **AAM-Softmax** -- the same ArcFace loss from episode #88 for face recognition. The loss pushes same-speaker embeddings closer on the unit hypersphere while enforcing angular margin between different speakers. Training datasets like **VoxCeleb** (7,000+ celebrities, 1M+ utterances from YouTube) provide the scale needed to generalize.

## Voice Activity Detection: where is speech?

Before you can identify speakers, you need to know where speech actually occurs. **Voice Activity Detection** (VAD) classifies each audio frame as speech or non-speech. It sounds trivial -- and for clean studio audio, it practically is. But in real-world recordings with background music, air conditioning hum, keyboard typing, and other non-speech sounds, VAD becomes a serious preprocessing challenge:

```python
import numpy as np


class SimpleVAD:
    \

def __init__(self, sr=16000,
                 frame_ms=25,
                 hop_ms=10):
        self.sr = sr
        self.frame_len = int(
            sr * frame_ms / 1000)
        self.hop_len = int(
            sr * hop_ms / 1000)

    def compute_energy(self, audio):
        \

n_frames = (
            (len(audio) - self.frame_len)
            // self.hop_len + 1)
        energy = np.zeros(n_frames)
        for i in range(n_frames):
            start = i * self.hop_len
            frame = audio[
                start:start+self.frame_len]
            rms = np.sqrt(
                np.mean(frame ** 2))
            energy[i] = 20 * np.log10(
                max(rms, 1e-10))
        return energy

    def detect(self, audio,
               energy_thresh_db=-30,
               min_speech_ms=200,
               min_silence_ms=100):
        \

energy = self.compute_energy(
            audio)
        speech = energy > energy_thresh_db

        hop_ms = (self.hop_len / self.sr
                  * 1000)
        min_speech = int(
            min_speech_ms / hop_ms)
        min_silence = int(
            min_silence_ms / hop_ms)

        # Fill short gaps
        result = speech.copy()
        in_gap = False
        gap_start = 0
        for i in range(len(result)):
            if not result[i] and (
                    not in_gap):
                gap_start = i
                in_gap = True
            elif result[i] and in_gap:
                if i - gap_start < (
                        min_silence):
                    result[
                        gap_start:i] = True
                in_gap = False

        # Remove short segments
        in_seg = False
        seg_start = 0
        for i in range(len(result)):
            if result[i] and not in_seg:

VAD might seem like a solved problem, but it's absolutly critical for downstream quality. Without it, silence and background noise get processed as speech, which wastes compute and (worse) contaminates speaker embeddings with non-speech features. Production systems like **Silero VAD** use small neural networks (just a few megabytes) trained on massive amounts of audio with precise speech/non-speech labels. They run in real-time on a CPU, processing hours of audio in seconds.

## Building a speaker verification system from scratch

Let's put the pieces together and build a complete speaker verification system. We'll synthesize multi-speaker audio, extract simple spectral features, compute embeddings, and verify speakers using cosine similarity:

```python
import numpy as np


class SpeakerVerificationSystem:
    \

def __init__(self, sr=16000,
                 n_mels=40,
                 embed_dim=64):
        self.sr = sr
        self.n_mels = n_mels
        self.embed_dim = embed_dim
        self.rng = np.random.RandomState(
            42)

    def synthesize_speaker(self,
                            f0_range,
                            formants,
                            duration=2.0,
                            n_utterances=5):
        \

utterances = []
        for _ in range(n_utterances):
            n = int(self.sr * duration)
            t = np.arange(n) / self.sr
            f0 = self.rng.uniform(
                *f0_range)
            signal = np.zeros(n)
            for f, a in formants:
                signal += a * np.sin(
                    2*np.pi*f*t)
            for h in range(2, 6):
                signal += (0.3/h) * np.sin(
                    2*np.pi*f0*h*t)
            signal *= (0.5 + 0.5 * np.sin(
                2*np.pi*4.5*t))
            signal += self.rng.randn(
                n) * 0.02
            utterances.append(signal)
        return utterances

    def mel_spectrogram(self, audio):
        \

n_fft = 512
        hop = 160
        n_frames = (
            len(audio) - n_fft) // hop
        spec = np.zeros(
            (self.n_mels, n_frames))
        window = np.hanning(n_fft)
        for i in range(n_frames):
            start = i * hop
            frame = audio[
                start:start + n_fft]
            fft_mag = np.abs(
                np.fft.rfft(
                    frame * window))
            # Simple Mel binning
            n_bins = len(fft_mag)
            mel_bins = np.linspace(
                0, n_bins,
                self.n_mels + 1,
                dtype=int)
            for m in range(self.n_mels):
                lo = mel_bins[m]
                hi = mel_bins[m + 1]
                if hi > lo:
                    spec[m, i] = np.mean(
                        fft_mag[lo:hi])
        return np.log(spec + 1e-9)

    def extract_embedding(self, mel):
        \

mean = np.mean(mel, axis=1)
        std = np.std(mel, axis=1)
        features = np.concatenate(
            [mean, std])
        # Random projection (in a real
        # system this is a learned
        # network)
        proj = self.rng.randn(
            self.embed_dim,
            len(features)) * 0.1
        emb = proj @ features
        norm = np.linalg.norm(emb)
        return emb / max(norm, 1e-9)

    def cosine_sim(self, a, b):
        return float(
            np.dot(a, b)
            / (np.linalg.norm(a)
               * np.linalg.norm(b)))

                    (950,.2), (2000,.1)]},
        }

        # Generate utterances

        for name, cfg in (
                speaker_configs.items()):
            utts = self.synthesize_speaker(
                cfg['f0_range'],
                cfg['formants'])
            speakers[name] = utts

        # Extract embeddings
        embeddings = {}
        for name, utts in (
                speakers.items()):
            embs = []

                    utt)
                emb = self.extract_embedding(
                    mel)
                embs.append(emb)
            embeddings[name] = embs

        # Enrollment: use first 3
        # utterances per speaker
        enrolled = {}
        for name, embs in (
                embeddings.items()):
            enrolled[name] = np.mean(
                embs[:3], axis=0)
            enrolled[name] /= (
                np.linalg.norm(
                    enrolled[name]))

        # Verification trials
        print(\

            ('Alice', 'Alice', 3),
            ('Alice', 'Alice', 4),

would be replaced by a trained neural network (d-vector LSTM or ECAPA-TDNN), but the pipeline structure is identical: synthesize/capture audio, extract Mel spectrogram, compute embedding, compare with cosine similarity. The threshold (0.6 in our demo) is the critical operating parameter -- too low and impostors get accepted (high false acceptance rate), too high and legitimate speakers get rejected (high false rejection rate).

## Speaker diarization: who spoke when?

**Diarization** segments a multi-speaker recording into speaker-homogenous regions. The output is a timeline showing which speaker is talking at each moment, without necessarily knowing who the speakers are (they're labeled as Speaker 0, Speaker 1, etc.). Think meeting recordings, podcast transcriptions, or courtroom audio analysis.

The traditional diarization pipeline looks like this:

```
Audio -> VAD -> Segmentation -> Embeddings -> Clustering -> Speaker labels
```

Let's build one:

```python
import numpy as np


class SpeakerDiarizer:
    \

def __init__(self, sr=16000,
                 seg_dur=1.5,
                 seg_hop=0.75):
        self.sr = sr
        self.seg_dur = seg_dur
        self.seg_hop = seg_hop
        self.rng = np.random.RandomState(
            42)

    def generate_meeting(self):
        \

dur = 20.0
        n = int(self.sr * dur)
        audio = self.rng.randn(n) * 0.005
        profiles = {
            0: (120, [500, 1000, 2200]),
            1: (200, [800, 1200, 2600]),
            2: (150, [650, 1100, 2400])}
        timeline = [
            (0, 0.5, 3.2), (1, 3.5, 6.0),
            (0, 6.3, 8.5), (2, 8.8, 12.0),
            (1, 12.3, 14.5),
            (2, 14.8, 17.0),
            (0, 17.2, 19.5)]
        for spk, start, end in timeline:
            f0, fmts = profiles[spk]
            s = int(start * self.sr)
            e = int(end * self.sr)
            t = np.arange(e-s) / self.sr
            sig = sum(0.2 * np.sin(
                2*np.pi*f*t) for f in fmts)
            for h in range(2, 5):
                sig += (0.15/h) * np.sin(
                    2*np.pi*f0*h*t)
            sig *= (0.5 + 0.5 * np.sin(
                2*np.pi*3*t))
            audio[s:e] += sig
        return audio, timeline

    def segment_audio(self, audio):
        \

seg_samples = int(
            self.seg_dur * self.sr)
        hop_samples = int(
            self.seg_hop * self.sr)
        segments = []
        starts = []
        i = 0
        while i + seg_samples <= (
                len(audio)):
            seg = audio[
                i:i + seg_samples]
            # Skip near-silent segments
            if np.sqrt(np.mean(
                    seg**2)) > 0.01:
                segments.append(seg)
                starts.append(
                    i / self.sr)
            i += hop_samples
        return segments, starts

    def extract_features(self, segment):
        \

n_fft = 512
        hop = 160
        n_frames = (
            len(segment) - n_fft) // hop
        if n_frames < 1:
            return np.zeros(80)
        spec = np.zeros(
            (40, n_frames))
        w = np.hanning(n_fft)
        for i in range(n_frames):
            s = i * hop
            fft = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(
                segment[s:s+n_fft] * w))
            bins = np.linspace(
                0, len(fft), 41,
                dtype=int)
            for m in range(40):
                if bins[m+1] > bins[m]:
                    spec[m, i] = np.mean(
                        fft[bins[m]:
                            bins[m+1]])
        spec = np.log(spec + 1e-9)
        mean = np.mean(spec, axis=1)
        std = np.std(spec, axis=1)
        return np.concatenate(
            [mean, std])

    def cluster_embeddings(self, embs,
                            n_clusters=3):
        \

# Initialize with K-means++
        centers = [embs[0].copy()]
        for _ in range(1, n_clusters):
            dists = np.array([
                min(np.linalg.norm(
                    e - c)**2
                    for c in centers)
                for e in embs])
            probs = dists / dists.sum()
            idx = self.rng.choice(
                len(embs), p=probs)
            centers.append(
                embs[idx].copy())
        centers = np.array(centers)

        # Iterate
        for _ in range(50):
            # Assign
            labels = np.array([
                np.argmin([
                    np.linalg.norm(e - c)
                    for c in centers])
                for e in embs])
            # Update
            new_centers = np.array([
                embs[labels == k].mean(
                    axis=0)
                if (labels == k).any()
                else centers[k]
                for k in range(
                    n_clusters)])
            if np.allclose(
                    centers, new_centers):
                break
            centers = new_centers

        return labels

    def run(self):
        audio, gt_timeline = (
            self.generate_meeting())
        print(f\
)\n        for spk, s, e in gt_timeline:\n            print(f\

)

        # Pipeline
        segments, starts = (
            self.segment_audio(audio))
        embs = np.array([
            self.extract_features(seg)
            for seg in segments])
        labels = self.cluster_embeddings(
            embs, n_clusters=3)

        print(f\

        # Simple DER at 100ms resolution
        gt_l = np.zeros(200)
        for spk, s, e in gt_timeline:
            gt_l[int(s*10):int(e*10)] = (
                spk + 1)
        pr_l = np.zeros(200)
        for start, label in zip(

            s = int(start * 10)
            e = min(int((start +
                self.seg_dur) * 10), 200)
            pr_l[s:e] = label + 1
        speech = (gt_l > 0).sum()
        confusion = ((gt_l > 0)
            & (pr_l > 0)
            & (gt_l != pr_l)).sum()

            & (pr_l > 0)).sum()
        der = ((confusion + missed + fa)

)
