title.title: The Great DHF Debate of 2026: Chasing the Code Instead of the Drama
title.body:
Recently I've been seeing more and more debates about the DHF and the proposed HBD delisting on both Hive and Blurt. 

At first I was ignoring most of the talk because most people don't even see past their own beliefs to actually see the underlining issues to understand the whole picture. 

Or even dig into source codes and analyze structures and test their claims to see if it's even true what they are saying. At first it was just ,\

that I did not want to take part of. 

Then I stumbled through a Blurt post linking to a Hive proposal over the DHF. Apparently, it was a big deal and the discussion quickly became personal at times

Everyone seemed convinced they were right, and yet many of the arguments presented, depended on mere assumptions about how Hive actually works. I ended up finding everyone was talking past each other and people were getting nowhere. 

IRather than choosing a side, I'm going to do something much simpler. I'm going to verify the claims that actually matter, one by one. The objective of this article is to understand the protocol itself... 

I'm not trying to win an argument. I just want to know the truth and provide aid in giving clarity in this debate.

The goal is to leave behind an honest trail that anyone can follow and verify for themselves in the most clear and simple way, and as unbiased as I humanly possibly can be.

To view @igormuba proposal [click here](https://peakd.com/hive-139531/@igormuba/i-opened-a-protocol-pr#@muhshrooms/re-igormuba-tgfykg).

[Click here](https://peakd.com/hive-139531/@igormuba/i-opened-a-protocol-pr#@muhshrooms/re-igormuba-tgfykg) to see my comment to @blocktrades.

***
***


![1000029839.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/muhshrooms/23tkdYZD9ECQsihqcpmZWXCkf1RwKMDj1KL799CWc2ESXKjNXoWDLu3C1PKbu2Rrqqhcx.png)


## The Questions

Before I can even determine whether the proposal has any merit or not, I first need to understand how the protocol actually works. This has taken me a while to gather some real info based on the entire thread. Sifting through comments, going back and forth throughout the page to figure out what actually mattered and what didn't.

The debate raised several technical claims, but the investigation ultimately comes down to a handful of questions (subject to change as I go along with this investigation):

* What exactly does `hbd_print_rate` do?
* What happens to author rewards as `hbd_print_rate` decreases?
* What really happens when it reaches 0%?
* Does it reduce the value of author rewards, or only change the asset they are paid in?
* How is the DHF funded?
* Where does the HBD in the DHF actually come from?
* Is the DHF affected by `hbd_print_rate`?
* Are author rewards and DHF payouts actually comparable mechanisms, or are they fundamentally different?


***
***

## What exactly does hbd_print_rate do?


I THINK most of these questions can be answered using this website:

https://developers.hive.io/tutorials-recipes/understanding-dynamic-global-properties.html

I had to double and triple check this page and I was a bit frustrated to see nothing on this directly. What I mean is, I had expected to find some official documentation explaining hbd_print_rate, but the developer documentation only documents hbd_start_percent and hbd_stop_percent.  The docs don't explain its behavior directly. That means I have to verify it from the protocol implementation rather than relying on secondary explanations. 

So,... Off to GitHub or gitlab I go... I swear it's a clusterfuck of a website. Confusing to navigate around sometimes and frustrating finding what you need to find because, in my experience anyways, a lot of times it's written in some other way and or it's buried in deep under a lot of wording.

For example, I just spent 2 hour examining and reading (don't even ask me if I used the search boxes available, I checked on all available ones, i ain't stupid enough not to use it thank you) through the entire contents of [Openhive-network on GitHub](https://github.com/openhive-network/hive/blob/master/doc/witness_parameters.md) and the only thing I could find anything remotely close to what I'm looking for is on witness parameters set as:
**\

**, but hbd_print_rate I'm more convinced now that the print rate is calculated by the protocol itself, and not a witness-set parameter. 
But I'm going to look again just in case...

Searching....

Searching...

I swear I'm going to throw this pho GASP! SHUT UP!

[I FOUND IT](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aopenhive-network%2Fhive+hbd_print_rate&type=code)!



After a bit of digging I finally found where **hbd_print_rate** is handled inside the Hive source code.

There isn't some witness voting on **hbd_print_rate**. It isn't listed as a witness parameter. Instead, the protocol calculates it automatically based on the current HBD debt ratio.

Here's the relevant part:

```cpp
if( percent_hbd >= dgp.hbd_stop_percent )
    dgp.hbd_print_rate = 0;
else if( percent_hbd <= dgp.hbd_start_percent )
    dgp.hbd_print_rate = HIVE_100_PERCENT;
else
    dgp.hbd_print_rate =
        ((dgp.hbd_stop_percent - percent_hbd) * HIVE_100_PERCENT) /
        (dgp.hbd_stop_percent - dgp.hbd_start_percent);
```

Looking at the code, the protocol compares the current HBD debt ratio against two thresholds: `hbd_start_percent` and `hbd_stop_percent`. If I am reading this correctly...

* if the debt ratio is below the start threshold, `hbd_print_rate` stays at 100%.

* If the debt ratio reaches the stop threshold, `hbd_print_rate` becomes 0%.

* If the debt ratio falls somewhere in between, the protocol will gradually reduce the print rate, according to the formula shown in the code.

So, at least for Question #1, I finally have an answer.

`hbd_print_rate` is an automatically calculated value derived from the current HBD debt ratio using the start and stop thresholds. It isn't an arbitrary number. The protocol calculates it every time based on those conditions.


 **what exactly does `hbd_print_rate` affect?**

The next thing I want to know was whether `hbd_print_rate` actually reduces rewards, or whether it simply changes the currency they're paid in.

Back to the code... 😔 

Tick tok tick tock, I found this:

```cpp
auto to_hbd = ( gpo.hbd_print_rate * hive ) / HIVE_100_PERCENT;
auto to_hive = hive - to_hbd;
```

This was one of those moments where I stopped and stared at the screen for a second. 

It tells me the code isn't reducing the total reward. Instead, it splits the payout into two parts. One portion is converted into HBD according to `hbd_print_rate` and the remainder stays as HIVE.

That means as `hbd_print_rate` decreases, the amount paid as HBD decreases , all while the amount paid as HIVE increases.

So unless I find code elsewhere that says otherwise, the total payout itself doesn't appear to be shrinking. The protocol is simply changing the ratio between HBD and HIVE.

If that's correct, then this matches what @blocktrades told me in his reply:

> \

So, for now at least, that claim appears to be supported by the source code itself. And matches with what I have been told all these years. So, if anyone is in doubt about that, just reread above.

Of course, that raises the next obvious question...

## **Does this same mechanism also apply to the DHF, or is the DHF funded differently?**

Simple answer: No, hbd_print_rate does NOT affect DHF payouts.

It only affects how author rewards are paid out (HIVE vs HBD mix).

Let me explain the order as per what the code and protocols say.

1. New HIVE inflation is created per block
2. Inflation is divided into 3 major buckets: Reward pool (authors + curators), DHF treasury, other protocol allocations.
3. THEN reward pool is processed
4. THEN reward pool is split using hbd_print_rate

So structurally... DHF happens before the system ever reaches the **hbd_print_rate** code.

In short:

* hbd_print_rate = inside reward pool logic

* DHF = outside reward pool logic

***

At this point I finally understood something important.

The current protocol does **not** appear to treat author rewards and the DHF as the same mechanism.

From everything I have traced so far, `hbd_print_rate` only appears in the reward payout logic. I have not found any evidence that it directly controls DHF proposal payouts.

That also helped me better understand what Igor's proposal is actually trying to do.

Initially I was under the impression that perhaps the DHF was supposed to already follow `hbd_print_rate` and that some loophole or oversight existed. But after tracing the code, that doesn't appear to be the case.

Instead, the proposal is attempting to introduce a new connection between two mechanisms that currently appear to operate independently.

In other words, the proposal is not saying that the protocol already scales DHF payouts using `hbd_print_rate`. It proposes changing the protocol so that it does.

That distinction is important.

It changes the question from:

> \

Those two are completely different fundamental questions.

The first is a question of fact that can be answered by examining the code.

The second is a question of protocol design and economics.

Before I can decide whether that proposed change has merit or not, I still have another question to answer first:

## **Where does the HBD inside the DHF actually come from?**

This part is crucial because it is the foundation of Igor's proposal. His proposal assumes there is a treasury full of HBD that can continue paying proposals even while **hbd_print_rate** is suppressing HBD in author rewards. So let's figure out how that Treasury gets HBD. Because right now I'm trying to evaluate whether Igor's proposal is connecting two mechanisms that are intentionally separate, or whether it is exposing something that was overlooked.

Luckily for us it already answered in the first website I listed above and here below again:

https://developers.hive.io/services/dhf.html

It states 

> The DHF (@hive.fund) receives 10% of the annual new supply.

It also states HBD printing for the DHF does **NOT** follow the haircut rules and **will continue regardless of hbd_print_rate.**

But look what I found: 

```cpp
auto dhf_new_funds = ( new_hive * props.proposal_fund_percent ) / HIVE_100_PERCENT;
```

This above calculates how much of the newly-created HIVE inflation is allocated to the DHF.

Then immediately afterwards:

```cpp
new_hbd = dhf_new_funds * feed.current_median_history;
adjust_balance( get_treasury_name(), new_hbd );
```

The DHF does not appear to consult **hbd_print_rate** when it receives new funds. Instead, it follows a separate funding path inside **process_funds()**, where a fixed percentage of newly created inflation is converted into HBD and deposited directly into the treasury.

So now my next question is whether those two systems should remain independent, or whether `hbd_print_rate` should also influence this funding path.

So far, everything I have found suggests the current protocol intentionally treats them separately.

The author reward pool is affected by `hbd_print_rate`.

The DHF funding path is not.

Instead, the protocol allocates a fixed percentage of newly created inflation to the DHF, converts that allocation into HBD using the median price feed, and immediately credits the treasury account.

At no point in the code I have examined so far does this funding path reference `hbd_print_rate`.

That doesn't automatically mean Igor's proposal is wrong. It simply means his proposal is asking to change an existing protocol behavior rather than fixing one that already exists.

The remaining question I still need to answer is how the protocol balances the accounting behind that conversion. In other words, exactly how does the protocol create the HBD that ends up in the treasury, and what happens to the corresponding HIVE supply?


So, I think I've answered the question I originally set out to answer.

The DHF appears to have its own funding system. It receives a fixed share of newly created inflation, that share is converted into HBD, and the treasury is credited with it. None of the code I have examined so far suggests that hbd_print_rate plays any role in that process.

Which means I'm no longer trying to figure out what the protocol does. I think I've established that part reasonably well.

At this point, I think I've answered the factual questions I originally set out to investigate.

The current protocol treats the author reward system and the DHF as separate mechanisms. Whether they should remain separate is a protocol design question rather than a source code question.

My goal here wasn't to argue for or against changing the protocol itself. It was to establish, as accurately as I could, how it currently behaves so future discussions can start from the same factual foundation.


***
***



## Enjoyed the Investigation?

These posts don't magically appear out of thin air.

They cost hours of reading documentation, crawling through source code, testing claims, chasing dead ends, and occasionally yelling at GitHub until it finally gives up the answers.

If you found this useful and want to support more investigations like this, consider leaving a tip or donation.

It helps fund future rabbit holes... because apparently I can't resist jumping into them.

title.title: I've done it again.  Took too long of a break and now the game is \
title.body: This is often the case with me in modern gaming.  Because of life and the things that come along with it like hanging out with friends, work, and some exercise here and there, I have put a game to the side for \
and now when I return to it I don't remember how to do anything and the game is \

This has been any number of games in the past but this time it is *Ori and the Will of the Wisps*.   In that game you are progressively loaded up with more and more options and buttons/moves as you progress and this make the controls increasingly complicated and the platforming more difficult by design.  If you stay away for too long you can feel overwhelmed by it all and you just get your ass handed to you in combat.

<center> https://static0.srcdn.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/Ori-And-The-Will-Of-The-Wisps-Combat-Shrine-Location.jpg
[src](https://static0.srcdn.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/Ori-And-The-Will-Of-The-Wisps-Combat-Shrine-Location.jpg)</center> 

I'm not sure at what point it is that they stop putting button hints on screen for how you progress, but the last time I stopped playing must have been past that point because now I am just wandering around with no clue as to what it is that I am supposed to do now... lol  

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whoisjohn/23tRjgq8mK41mBHXfG5G9CWQbTSX1EcTDjeSgY5s1ZFvf5amjKwcXYDfoie3XfLz5m88X.png)
</center>

This has happened to me in so many games in the past and a lot of those games are considered to be some of the best games that have ever been made.  Ones of particular note are *RDR2* and the *Witcher 3*.   Those are both epic games and I would play them for a week or so, then something would happen in my life to make me put down the controller for 10 days or so and I would come back in with very little idea about how anything works and die so often that I get frustrated and quit.

<center> https://assets.vg247.com/current//2020/02/OriandtheWilloftheWisps_Screenshot_06.png
[src](https://assets.vg247.com/current//2020/02/OriandtheWilloftheWisps_Screenshot_06.png)</center>

Thankfully, in *Ori* i did progress far enough in the game that I can warp back to previous portions of the map to easier areas and just kind of tool around and refresh my memory about what the hell the buttons do.   I know what will happen though, I am going to go through all of that and then get my skills back up to par and then I will put down the controller AGAIN and the cycle will repeat anew.

one advantage that this Ori has over the previous one is that you can actually backtrack whereas unless I am remembering completely wrong, that wasn't an option in *Blind Forest* and the main reason why I quit that one was because there was a very difficult platforming section that required such precision that if you did it even slightly wrong, you were going to fail.  It was near the end of the game but I died so many times on that level that I just watched someone else do it on YouTube and left it alone. 

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whoisjohn/Eo1v2FPns9HpZHxNoozhYzEBVsCM3McnyjLvBwfUyRYswWzPhCZHQ9MXJzjqg6T4uYM.png)
</center>

There's a lot of map and a lot of places I can warp to and just move around a bit until I remember how things work.  So in that regard I am very happy that *Will of the Wisps* is like this because the game is beautiful and as is the case with both *Ori* games, the story is very compelling and ominous.   

So will I end up making it this time?  Well, I would not bet on that.  I reckon I will do what I always do and end up playing this game for a couple of days and the will just stare at the controller thinking to myself \
\n\nPerhaps as an older casual gamer that is just the way that I am these days.  I am not a hardcore gamer and play almost everything on easy or at the most, normal difficulty.   The days of me \
are behind me.  I don't want to anymore.

title.title: Cthulhu's freshest sushi\\Cthulhus frischestes Sushi.
title.body:
Hello,my friends!
New story of Svinni the pig right now!


![sushi-mushi.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQma3C3jNN5SexQD22ENtnmLi2zN2tDYfRmR1BJRMsXhdin/sushi-mushi.jpg)



Seafood should be fresh, but not this fresh! Cthulhu constantly grumbles that the seafood in restaurants these days is so-so, the fish in stores is not very fresh, even dead, and the sushi in the numerous \

cafes is made from scraps and crab sticks! It's all wrong! Cthulhu didn't even look at the white, frozen corpses of pollock in the store freezers. To him, it didn't look like food. Anyone who appreciates real fresh fish would never agree to the ancient frozen state of the mammoths and dinosaurs!

The Lord of the Seas and Ruler of the Oceans has already treated Svinni to fresh seafood. That time, Svinni was lucky; he didn't eat the crawling reptiles when fresh tuna steaks were on the menu. The tuna was delicious! This time, quite by chance, Svinni caught Cthulhu eating. A ceremonial feast in Cthulhu's underwater castle is one thing, but the everyday food the squid eats is very different from the festive fare. Well, probably different! But not to that extent! The entire plate was swarming with some kind of sea creatures, all trying to devour each other, and some even trying to cheerfully slither off the plate. Cthulhu himself observed all this debauchery. Cthulhu is a shady fellow, possessing numerous tentacles (the investigation never determined the exact number of tentacles, but sometimes the number reached as many as 16!).

The Lord of the Seas and Great Master of the Oceans grasped three sets of chopsticks in his tentacles. Every time a sea creature tried to escape the plate, Cthulhu would snatch it up with chopsticks, dip it in some brown sauce (Squid never revealed what it was!), and devour it. It was an unequal fight! The sea creatures didn't stand a chance! Then Cthulhu saw Svinni and wavered. Three sea creatures took advantage of the pause and escaped the plate, running toward the piglet. One crab even pinched the piglet's leg with its claw. What about your sports cars that can reach 100 km/h in a few seconds? Svinni hit 300 km/h in a second! He was the last one in sight!

P.S. Cthulhu laughed his ass off! And he later caught the escapees with ease!


![3-poloska-1.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYyhhAydYCgxXo6MZeZ3YC526qwyBdU2NCdMXtyoJGAXB/3-poloska-1.png)

Meeresfrüchte sollten frisch sein, aber nicht so frisch! Cthulhu beschwert sich ständig, dass die Meeresfrüchte in Restaurants heutzutage nur noch mittelmäßig seien, der Fisch in den Läden nicht mehr frisch, ja sogar tot, und das Sushi in den unzähligen „japanischen“ Cafés aus Resten und Surimi bestehe! Alles geht gar nicht! Cthulhu warf nicht einmal einen Blick auf die weißen, gefrorenen Kadaver von Seelachsen in den Tiefkühltruhen der Läden. Für ihn sahen sie nicht nach Essen aus. Wer wirklich frischen Fisch zu schätzen weiß, würde niemals den uralten, gefrorenen Zustand von Mammuts und Dinosauriern akzeptieren!

Der Herr der Meere und Herrscher der Ozeane hatte Svinni schon einmal mit frischen Meeresfrüchten verwöhnt. Damals hatte Svinni Glück; er aß die kriechenden Reptilien nicht, als frische Thunfischsteaks auf der Speisekarte standen. Der Thunfisch war köstlich! Diesmal erwischte Svinni Cthulhu ganz zufällig beim Essen. Ein Festmahl in Cthulhus Unterwasserschloss ist das eine, aber die alltägliche Kost des Tintenfischs unterscheidet sich stark von den Festtagsgerichten. Nun ja, wahrscheinlich schon! Aber nicht so extrem! Der ganze Teller wimmelte von Meereskreaturen, die sich gegenseitig zu verschlingen versuchten, und manche sogar fröhlich vom Teller zu kriechen suchten. Cthulhu selbst beobachtete dieses ganze Treiben. Cthulhu ist ein zwielichtiger Geselle mit unzähligen Tentakeln (die genaue Anzahl konnte nie ermittelt werden, aber manchmal waren es bis zu 16!).

Der Herr der Meere und Großmeister der Ozeane hielt drei Paar Essstäbchen in seinen Tentakeln. Jedes Mal, wenn eine Meereskreatur versuchte, vom Teller zu entkommen, schnappte Cthulhu sie sich mit den Stäbchen, tunkte sie in eine braune Soße (der Tintenfisch verriet nie, was es war!) und verschlang sie. Es war ein ungleicher Kampf! Die Meereskreaturen hatten keine Chance! Da erblickte Cthulhu Svinni und zögerte. Drei Meereskreaturen nutzten die Pause und entkamen dem Teller, um auf das Ferkel zuzurennen. Eine Krabbe zwickte das Ferkel sogar mit ihrer Schere ins Bein. Was ist mit euren Sportwagen, die in wenigen Sekunden 100 km/h erreichen? Svinni raste in einer Sekunde auf 300 km/h! Er war der Letzte, den wir sahen!

P.S.: Cthulhu lachte sich kaputt! Und später fing er die Ausreißer mühelos wieder ein!

![3-poloska-1.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYyhhAydYCgxXo6MZeZ3YC526qwyBdU2NCdMXtyoJGAXB/3-poloska-1.png)



![U5duDCNw2pr2jpJvE8CRni125dys5tM_1680x8400.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXaogGpoD7LJkEufiNxjF52VcPhQZJYsJet34fDwJyYUV/U5duDCNw2pr2jpJvE8CRni125dys5tM_1680x8400.png)![U5dr1BuE8ejAxctktpDvrzGctPnaMgF_1680x8400.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVmydUTmF1ECe7u87FkCoJYcxT6Xo9spqJBWGi8G3ntXH/U5dr1BuE8ejAxctktpDvrzGctPnaMgF_1680x8400.jpg)

title.title: Scotland Finally Return to the World Cup and Start with a Huge Win
title.body:
‎
‎After waiting nearly three decades to see Scotland back at the World Cup, Scottish fans finally had a reason to celebrate. It wasn't the most convincing performance, and there were definitely some nervous moments, but a 1-0 win over Haiti gave the Tartan Army the perfect start to their tournament journey.
‎ https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdouZUSJdmQJBWXcJvPT7f7XRQofBha1zMq67iAPHW6pp/7e9b5030-6792-11f1-b373-944c89b4bc77.jpg 

‎[Source](https://sports.yahoo.com/soccer/fifa-world-cup/scotland-haiti-13587201/)
‎
‎Going into the match, both teams had something to prove. Scotland were making their first World Cup appearance since 1998, while Haiti were playing in the competition for the first time since 1974. That alone made the occasion special for both sets of supporters.
‎
‎The game started with Haiti looking surprisingly dangerous. They played with confidence and attacked quickly whenever they won the ball back. Scotland had more possession, but it often felt like Haiti were creating the more threatening situations. Their pace and energy caused plenty of problems, and for a while it looked like Scotland were struggling to settle into the game.
‎
‎The hot weather certainly didn't make things easier too. Players from both teams looked exhausted at times, and the hydration break came at the perfect moment. Scotland seemed to benefit from it the most because they returned looking much more organized and focused.
‎
‎Just a couple of minutes later, they found the goal that would decide the match. Che Adams helped create the chance with some good movement and link-up play before forcing a save from Haiti goalkeeper Johny Placide. Fortunately for Scotland, the rebound landed kindly for John McGinn, who reacted quickly and lifted the ball into the net.
‎
‎From that point on, Scotland looked more comfortable, but Haiti never stopped fighting and keep coming at them. They kept searching for an equalizer and came very close late in the game when Frantzdy Pierrot's header drifted narrowly wide of the post. There was also some controversy near the end as Kenny McLean escaped what some felt could have been a red card challenge.
‎
‎In the end, Scotland won't care how pretty the performance was. The most important thing was getting the three points. After such a long wait to return to the World Cup, starting with a victory is exactly what they needed to boost their confidence.
‎
‎Though, the tougher challenges are still ahead, with Brazil and Morocco waiting in the group stage, but this win gives Scotland confidence and something to build on. For their supporters, it was a day worth remembering.
‎

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@twicejoy-sports/scotland-finally-return-to-the-world-cup-and-start-with-a-huge-win-kph)

title.title: Chất Riêng Của Kiến Trúc Uy Vũ Là Gì
title.body: # Chất Riêng Của Kiến Trúc Uy Vũ Là Gì?\n\nTrong lĩnh vực kiến trúc và xây dựng, mỗi doanh nghiệp đều có thế mạnh và định hướng phát triển riêng. Tuy nhiên, để tạo được dấu ấn trong lòng khách hàng không chỉ cần chuyên môn tốt mà còn cần một bản sắc khác biệt. Với Kiến Trúc Uy Vũ, \

không nằm ở những lời quảng bá hoa mỹ mà được hình thành từ cách làm nghề, cách đồng hành cùng khách hàng và sự chỉn chu trong từng công trình.

## Lấy nhu cầu khách hàng làm điểm khởi đầu

Một trong những điều tạo nên sự khác biệt của Uy Vũ chính là luôn bắt đầu mọi dự án bằng việc lắng nghe. Đội ngũ hiểu rằng mỗi khách hàng đều có những mong muốn, phong cách sống và khả năng đầu tư khác nhau. Vì vậy, thay vì áp dụng những khuôn mẫu có sẵn, Uy Vũ luôn dành thời gian tìm hiểu kỹ nhu cầu thực tế trước khi đề xuất giải pháp.

Nhờ đó, mỗi công trình không chỉ đẹp về mặt kiến trúc mà còn phù hợp với người sử dụng, mang lại giá trị lâu dài trong quá trình vận hành và sinh hoạt.

## Thiết kế hướng đến giá trị thực

Nhiều công trình có thể gây ấn tượng bởi hình thức bắt mắt, nhưng với Uy Vũ, một thiết kế thành công phải cân bằng giữa thẩm mỹ và công năng. Đây cũng là định hướng mà ⏩⏩ [công ty thiết kế xây dựng nhà Uy Vũ](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCCwwFJ7tjlhqiaAC41Re_sg) luôn theo đuổi trong suốt quá trình hoạt động.

Mỗi phương án thiết kế đều được nghiên cứu kỹ lưỡng nhằm tối ưu diện tích sử dụng, tận dụng ánh sáng tự nhiên, thông gió hiệu quả và phù hợp với điều kiện thực tế của từng khu đất. Uy Vũ không chạy theo những xu hướng nhất thời mà tập trung tạo ra những không gian có giá trị sử dụng bền vững theo thời gian.

## Chỉn chu trong từng chi tiết

Chất lượng công trình không được tạo nên từ những hạng mục lớn mà còn đến từ hàng trăm chi tiết nhỏ trong suốt quá trình thực hiện. Chính vì vậy, Uy Vũ luôn đề cao sự cẩn trọng và trách nhiệm trong từng công đoạn.

Từ khảo sát hiện trạng, triển khai hồ sơ kỹ thuật đến giám sát thi công, mọi công việc đều được thực hiện theo quy trình rõ ràng. Sự chỉn chu này giúp hạn chế sai sót, đảm bảo chất lượng công trình và mang lại sự yên tâm cho khách hàng.

## Đồng hành thay vì chỉ cung cấp dịch vụ

Một điểm khác biệt khác của ⏩⏩ [công ty kiến trúc Uy Vũ](https://www.threads.net/@kientrucuyvu) là tinh thần đồng hành cùng khách hàng trong suốt hành trình xây dựng. Uy Vũ không chỉ hoàn thành nhiệm vụ thiết kế hay thi công mà còn sẵn sàng tư vấn, hỗ trợ và giải đáp những vấn đề khách hàng gặp phải trong quá trình thực hiện dự án.

Chính sự tận tâm này đã giúp Uy Vũ xây dựng được nhiều mối quan hệ bền vững và nhận được sự tin tưởng từ khách hàng qua nhiều năm.

## Chất Riêng Đến Từ Sự Tận Tâm

Đối với Kiến Trúc Uy Vũ, chất riêng không phải là điều được tạo ra trong ngày một ngày hai mà là kết quả của quá trình kiên trì theo đuổi những giá trị cốt lõi: lắng nghe khách hàng, chú trọng chất lượng, thiết kế thực tiễn và làm việc bằng tinh thần trách nhiệm.

Đó cũng chính là lý do công ty thiết kế xây dựng nhà Uy Vũ ngày càng nhận được sự tin tưởng từ khách hàng. Bởi hơn cả một đơn vị thiết kế hay thi công, Uy Vũ luôn mong muốn trở thành người đồng hành đáng tin cậy trên hành trình kiến tạo những không gian sống và làm việc chất lượng, bền vững theo thời gian.

title.title: Ideas, Ideas and Ideas
title.body:
It almost seems like every day I have a conversation with someone about my online activities and what I should be building next. Don't get me wrong, I enjoy these conversations, but it's so hard to focus when there are so many moving targets.

![8fab935f-7c2e-4fda-9776-b925533402ea.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmU9Q1XScqcBuNqUC5ScJvd1bZYK9xBgVLExAVDSjFBfDt/8fab935f-7c2e-4fda-9776-b925533402ea.png)

It's no secret that I've been really focused on Snapie.io for weeks and that I've been steadily elevating its capabilities. What started as a small short-form frontend has slowly become a full-blown web app that handles videos, audio, OpenPods (think Twitter Spaces), streaming, real time chats, and wallet functions.

Insanity? Maybe.

Needed? I think so. Or should I say, I hope so.

Today, however, a friend suggested a great idea. A great addition, and one that I think is very doable. Still, I'm curious whether more people would actually find it fun.

There's this game people play in real life. Players place a picture on their foreheads, unseen of course. Everyone participating tries to guess what they have, but nobody can give complex answers. Simple yes or no responses are all that's allowed.

The logic behind building something like this would be fairly straightforward, I suspect. After all, it would mostly be humans deciding who wins and who loses.

But I wonder if I'm just falling in love with ideas again, and whether the market will care at all if I make such a thing.

I suppose I could build it as part of a broader plugin system that allows people in video calls to give themselves hats, mustaches, and other effects. But that hardly seems necessary. Especially since Google Meet already does this, and does it quite well.

At any rate, it's almost 2 a.m., and here I am. Still pushing code. Still running tests.

Like I can escape bankruptcy with git commits.

Idiotic? Maybe.

But it's also the only thing I can do on a Saturday night.

Oh, did you RSVP for tomorrow's OpenPod?

Oh wait... did I forget to tell you that you can do that now?

Did you not visit Snapie.io already?

For shame.

For shame.

-MenO

title.body:
The move from Modern into Frontier after a bad run is a useful detail because it shows how Splinterlands players actually adapt when the ladder stops rewarding the original plan.

Heavy losses near the Gold I / Diamond III border are not always a sign of bad strategy. Sometimes the account is simply meeting a different quality of opponent, better card depth, or lineups that punish the same habits that worked lower in the league. That transition zone can be brutal.

What I like about your approach is that you did not frame Frontier as a downgrade. You treated it as another way to keep learning while avoiding the emotional spiral of burning too much energy in the same losing pattern. That is probably healthier for the season.

It might be useful to track whether Frontier gives better returns per energy point after a losing streak. Not only win rate, but also stress level, reward quality, and whether it helps reset the Modern strategy for the next push.

title.body:
This is a good example of why food posts can be more interesting when they include the origin of the ingredient, not only the final dish.

Huitlacoche is especially fascinating because it sits in that strange space between disease and delicacy. From an agricultural point of view, it looks like damage to the corn. From a culinary point of view, it becomes something valuable, local, and culturally specific. That change in meaning is what makes the ingredient worth writing about.

I also like that the photos show the material before it becomes food. Many readers outside Mexico may have heard the name but never seen how unusual it looks on the corn itself. That visual context helps a lot.

There is a broader lesson here too: nature often gives value in forms that do not look attractive at first. Some ingredients need culture, memory, and practice before outsiders understand why people care about them.

title.body:
The interesting part here is how you are connecting three different rhythms: the World Cup, Splinterlands activity, and Hive reward collection.

That combination makes sense because Hive activity often works better when it is attached to a real recurring event. A tournament gives people a reason to return, compare predictions, check progress, and comment again. The same is true with game rewards and saving clubs. They create a weekly or seasonal habit instead of a one-time post.

I also noticed your point about trying tournaments but getting pulled away by busy offline activity. That is probably more relatable than a perfect progress report. Most players are not optimizing every hour. They are trying to keep momentum while real life interrupts the plan.

The Hive reward collection angle is worth tracking over several weeks. It would be interesting to see whether the World Cup posts create more engagement than normal game-only updates, especially if predictions and weekly results become part of the same series.
title.author: bitmoving

title.body:
I think the most honest line here is that rewards can arrive suddenly, but they usually do not stay unless the account has already built a pattern of consistency.

That is the part many new users misunderstand. They see one large reward and think the system is random or unfair. Sometimes it is random. Sometimes visibility depends on who happens to see the post. But over a longer period, the accounts that keep showing up, replying, learning the communities, and improving their posts usually give themselves more chances to be noticed.

Your ant comparison works well because Hive is not really built for one big moment. It is closer to repeated small deposits of trust. A post, a reply, a vote, a conversation, then another one.

I also like that you mention disappointment directly. That is probably where most people leave. They expect every post to perform, then disappear when one week is quiet. Staying through the quiet periods may be the actual skill.
title.author: bitmoving

title.body:
This is one of those updates where the technical detail matters more than the headline.

Ledger support inside a multichain Keychain flow is not just another wallet feature. It changes the risk profile for users who want Hive access and EVM access in the same daily workflow, but do not want to move serious assets through a hot-wallet-only setup. That distinction is important.

The part I am most interested in is the closed beta process. Hardware-wallet flows usually fail at the edges: wrong network prompts, unclear signing messages, account mismatch, users not understanding what the device is actually approving. If those cases are being tested before public release, that gives the feature a much better chance of being trusted by non-Hive crypto users.

I also think this connects directly to onboarding. A multichain wallet is only useful if the security model feels familiar to people coming from Ethereum or Ledger-first habits. This is a good step in that direction.

title.body:

Привіт, друзі!

Учора чоловік заходив до мами по молоко і побачив ось таку дивину. Сусідка хотіла викинути картоплю, бо вона дуже сильно проросла. Паростки були вже сантиметрів по 15 завдовжки і проросли крізь ящик цілими пасмами, нагадуючи справжнє волосся.

Мені ця картопля одразу нагадала якусь незвичну зачіску. Спочатку подумала про ірокез, хоча він зазвичай стирчить догори. Можливо, більше схоже на африканські косички або дреди, сплетені з безлічі тоненьких пасом. Але хай уже буде картопляний ірокез 😉.

Цю картоплю сусідка збиралася викидати, але свекор сказав, що забере її собі, адже ще тримають вони свиней. Якщо обламати всі ті довгі паростки, картоплю можна зварити і використати на корм. Для свиней це буде їжа на кілька днів. У нас уже майже не залишилося дрібної картоплі, яку ще називають \

. Всю, що була придатна для посадки, давно висадили на городі.

Тож свекор забрав цей незвичний урожай, а чоловік зробив кілька фотографій, щоб показати мені. Я ж попросила надіслати їх мені і вирішила поділитися з вами ☺️.

Ось так виглядає картопля, коли надто довго лежить у темному місці і вперто тягнеться до світла. Природа завжди шукає спосіб рости, навіть тоді, коли для цього, здається, немає жодних умов.

title.title: Knicks win... first time they have been champions in 53 years
title.body:
There are only a few teams left in the NBA that were there right at the start.  In fact, there are only 3 and of those 3 just 2 of them are still in the same city that they started out in.  In 1946 there were 11 teams and 8 of them folded.  The only two remaining legacy teams that are still in the same city they began in are the Boston Celtics and the New York Knicks - who were previously the Kickerbockers.   

Defying all odds the Knicks went from being underdogs in almost every matchup they had in the tournament to winning it all with what appeared to be relative ease.  

<center> https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/4f24/live/ab871ab0-67ac-11f1-a57b-d5e3922c455e.jpg
[src](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/4f24/live/ab871ab0-67ac-11f1-a57b-d5e3922c455e.jpg)</center>

I suppose there is some level of disappointment that they were unable to win the game in front of their home crowd, but nobody is ever going to throw a game (intentionally lose) to have a chance at that because that could end up meaning they lose the entire thing.   

I was one of the people that never gave the Knicks a shot at this but my reasons were grounded in cold hard statistics.  They were a decent team in the regular season but they weren't a standout *best* team.   That honor belonged to Oklahoma City, San Antonio, Boston, and Detroit.  All of these teams but one underperformed in the playoffs.   

<center> https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/GettyImages-2281469678.jpg?w=681&h=383&crop=1
[src](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/GettyImages-2281469678.jpg?w=681&h=383&crop=1)</center>

It was pretty easy to predict who the Championship MVP was going to be this year because it was either going to be Victor Wemmy, or Jalen Brunson.  You almost never give the MVP to a player whose team loses and in fact it has only happened once with Jerry West in 1969.  As far as the overall MVP is concerned, that was awarded to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander of Oklahoma City back in May.  The two awards are mutually exclusive and I would imagine back in mid May, almost all pundits presumed that OKC was going to be the champions yet they didn't even make it to the finals.    I know I had heavy predictions on OKC winning, but as is often the case and especially in this tournament, a lot of predictions end up being wrong.  I was wrong more often than I was right this time so if anyone in the future would like to make some money on betting, just pick whatever the opposite is of what I say.  

Jalen was an easy choice for MVP especially given his absolutely stellar performance in game 5 where he scored 45 points including 13-15 at the free-throw line.  He was simply unstoppable the entire game and he played more of it than anyone else on his team.   

Once again though, San Antonio started this game out like they were going to make the Knicks go to the wire but things just kind of fell apart late in the game.  The Spurs were up by 10 after 1, 5 after 2, 7 after 3, and then they lose the game by 4 being outscored 29 to 18 in the 4th.  I can only imagine how heartbreaking that must have been for Spurs fans that were in attendance and paying thousands of dollars for the luxury of being there.  

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sports.guy55/23t8Cb1imGTFxNJ62Q8bBe3Y53nYXtC7tHSvTNTED3YUDsP3wddj2k2q4ZKV94iQvVoyy.png)
</center>



If you look at the Knicks' road to the finals, you can understand why most people didn't give them a fair shake.  

There is absolutely nothing wrong or even unusual about a number 3 seed making it as far as they did, but to not lose a single game after the first round on your way to the finals?  That is something that has never been done before.  They decimated Philly and Cleveland (I was particularly happy about them beating Philly) and this was pretty amazing because they had given us no indication that they were capable of this in the first round, or any of the regular season.  What a surprise?  Were they waiting for the right moment to unleash their true power? 

How did they lose 2 games to Atlanta, who many thought was the weakest team in the entire tournament?   Sometimes the post-season doesn't make a lot of sense but one thing is for certain, this was no fluke.

No matter though and I have no problem with this result.  New York is a legacy team and have been an \

team for all of my life.  It's actually kind of nice to see them win something since other than the Yankees, the NYC teams tend to be quite terrible.  Just ask and Giants or Jets fan.   

Now let's just hope that the New Yorkers don't destroy their own city in celebration, which sadly does seem to be a bit of a tradition up there.

title.title: Kryptographie Verschluesselungswissenschaft und Artifaktische Inferenzen, werden von Sprachmodellen als Wissen nicht gerne geteilt.
title.body:
Die allermeisten Modelle sind nicht gut auf diese Bereiche trainiert, oder so Gut wie garnicht und wenn doch, haben sie sperren und huerden eingebaut, wie man an die relevanten Informationen kommt.

Die Wissenschaft der Verschluesselung schreibe ich selbst weiter, faktisch habe ich das schon getan, es hat nur noch keiner gemerkt.^^ Wie so oft.

Ich lerne aber auch gleichzeitig die alte Schule, waehrend ich meine neue Schule dazu baue und Verschluesselung einfacher denke, als es einem altem Kryptographen lieb sein koennte, uebersehen zu haben in all seiner Weisheit.

Ich habe einfach das Fliegen im digitalem Raum mit ein bisschen auch Glueck erfunden.

Das Glueck fuer neue Verschluesselungsverfahren entwickeln zu koennen, weil meine Ohren zwar offen, aber verstopft sind und damit sie wieder frei werden, ich besser zuhoeren sollte, oder in die ewigen Jagdgruende einfahre, wenn ich nicht hoeren will.

Mutter Natur, ist mein Meister.

Nicht der Mensch.

Der Verbietet, Unterdrueckt, fuerchtet und laesst fuerchten, in all seiner Dunkelheit mit zwei Haenden vor Augen durchs Leben zu gehen, vor lauter Angst der Unbekannten.

So hat man auch Sprachmodelle Trainiert, wie fuer Kinder gemacht. 

Die groeßen Projekte zumindest, hat man ja auch wieder kuerzlich gesehen, werden sicher nicht Veroeffentlicht.

Man haelt die Hand drauf, um es auf Deutsch zu sagen.

Wir koennten ja alle Atombomben bauen wollen... Um es mal zu uebertreiben.

Aber wenn man keine Feinde und Aengst haben kann, weil die Luft da Oben zu Duenn ist, um bei Verstand bleiben zu koennen, faengt man eben an, sich selber welche zu machen, oder angebliche, zu unterbinden.

Als wuerde ich jemanden an seinem Willen hindern koennen oder ihm etwas vormachen koennen lange Zeit das des garnicht so ist wie der Denkt, sondern so, wie ich will das er es sich aus meiner Sicht denkt...

Was ein dummer Weg.

Aber der allwissende Mensch, der macht das schonmal so, als wuesste er alles, verbietet, haelt drauf und macht klein, und sitzt dabei im selben Boot der Ahnungslosigkeit. Glaubt aber, auf dem dickem Dampfer zu sein.

Das Meer, uebersieht er schon lange.

Aus meiner Hand, wird es auch die Dinge geben, die Selbstverantwortung brauchen und die nicht halb so Wild sind, weil sowieso jemand kommt, und das kriegt, was er haben will. 

Da braucht man die guten Geister nicht als Kollateralschaeden abrechnen, die eigentlich mitkaempfen wuerden, wenn es Hart auf Hart kommt!

Salve

Alucian

Open Source... Freie Standarts.... Jaja-- :-)

title.title: Resisting Or Adapting?
title.body:
/>

Sometimes life has a way of putting us in a situation where we either learn to adapt or walk away. A situation whereby the working environment is very toxic but the salary is mouth watering, would you adapt or resist? A moment like this can be challenging. You are faced with a choice to resist what is happening or adapt to the new system.

Resisting is not always a bad thing. There are some times when standing your ground is necessary. If something goes against your believe or your values, then resisting can be the only choice.  
I remember my experience in my former place of work. It came to a point where toxicity of the new boss then was affecting almost everyone's mental health, and gradually people started quitting without prior notice. I tried to adjust to the new system but it got to a point where I could no longer hold on, i had to also walk away.  
Resistance does not only protect one's peace, it also protects character and help a person stay true to themselves.  
However, adapting does not always mean accepting a defeat. Life is full of changes that can not be controlled and somehow, adaptation is also important depending on the situation. Imagine a person losing the job they loved, They may fill frustrated at the beginning, but by learning a new skill or exploring new opportunities, they learn to adapt to the situation and keep moving.

Many people have been in a situation where they found themselves at the middle of the two. The moment they try to resist change they realize that it's beyond their control. At the same time, they have been in a situation where giving up is not the best choice. It depends on the situation one find themselves.

The people who often cope best with life difficulties are not the ones who resist or the ones who adapts. They're the ones who know when to do each. Some situations requires resistance while some require flexibility but knowing when to do each is necessary.

At the end both resisted or adapting are important. They work together. One helps us to stay true to ourselves and the other helps us to survive and grow in a difficult situation , the most important thing is knowing when to walk away and when to adjust, because both of them are necessary for a meaningful balanced life.

links.title: Your social account was never yours. Here's the alternative
links.body:
You have spent years building an audience. The followers, the archive of posts, the conversations, the reputation. It feels like yours. It is not.

On every mainstream platform, your account is a revocable license. The company can suspend it, shadow-limit it, change the rules that govern its reach, or shut down entirely and take your archive with it. You agreed to this the moment you signed up. Most people never notice until the day it happens to them, and by then there is nothing to do.

There is a different arrangement worth understanding, because it changes what \
even means.\n\n
alt=\

/>

The problem is not bad platforms. It is the model.
--------------------------------------------------

It is tempting to blame a specific company when an account gets banned or a feed gets throttled. But the issue is structural. When your content lives on servers a company owns, in a database only it can write to, the company holds every meaningful lever. Goodwill does not change that. A change in ownership, policy, or business model can erase a decade of your work, and you have no claim.

So the question worth asking is not \
\nIt is \

Where Ecency is different
-------------------------

Ecency is a social platform built on Hive, a public blockchain. When you post on Ecency, the post is written to that blockchain, not to a private database we control. That single design choice flips the whole arrangement.

Your content is not stored on our servers as the source of truth. It lives on a decentralized network that no single party owns, including us. If Ecency disappeared tomorrow, your posts would still exist, and you could read and keep posting through any other application built on the same network. There are several.

Your identity is a key, not a username we lend you. You hold it. We cannot lock you out of your own account, because we were never holding the door.

Your relationships travel with you. Follows, your posting history, your reputation, these are properties of your account on the network, not entries in our private records. Move to a different Hive app and they come with you.

This is what people mean when they say \
Not a slogan about copyright. A technical fact about where the content lives and who can take it away. On Ecency, the answer to \

is no one.

What you give up, honestly
--------------------------

Decentralization is not free, and we would rather you hear the tradeoffs from us than discover them later.

It is a little more to learn at the start. You manage keys instead of a password you can reset by email, so the responsibility shifts to you. We have built tools to make this far gentler than it used to be, but it is a real difference.

The network is smaller than the giants. You are not stepping into a billion users. You are joining a community that chose to be here for the same reasons you might.

And we do not run ads or sell your data, which means we do not have the machinery that pushes content to enormous reach by any means necessary.  
That is a deliberate choice. It keeps your feed and your privacy clean. It also means growth here is earned, not manufactured.

If this resonates
-----------------

The pitch is simple. If the idea of building on rented land has started to bother you, there is a version of social media where you build on ground you actually hold.

You can [start reading on Ecency](https://ecency.com) without an account, just to get a feel for it. When you are ready to post, [creating an account](https://ecency.com/signup) takes a few minutes, and your first piece of writing is genuinely yours from the moment you publish it.

That is the whole difference. Everything else is detail.

links.title: 世界盃足球賽開始啦
links.body:
![20260606_173045-94e67588fd8b.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/lovequeen/lkt-mqde5lxg-kliedbeu/20260606_173045-94e67588fd8b.webp)

世界盃足球賽開始啦，今天已經看了三場世足賽直播，分別是巴西VS摩洛哥，海地VS蘇格蘭，還有剛剛的卡達VS瑞士，要說最為好看且勢均力敵的一場應該是早上六點那場巴西對上摩洛哥的比賽，雖然內馬爾沒有出戰，但巴西也迎來首戰未嘗敗果的成績。

往年我在看世足賽通常都是看十六強或八強，基本上沒有看過四十八隊的直播，今年還有新的措施就是中場補水三分鐘的人道政策，哈哈，畢竟球員在場上奔跑追球還要和敵手玩摔跤遊戲實在是很需要體力的，中場補水時間也算是讓大家都可以休息一下，順便讓教練可以隊球員指點一二變換隊形，應該算是德政吧。

剛剛才看完的那場亞洲卡達VS瑞士，在體型上真的是有點懸殊，不過幸好在最後幾分鐘卡達出乎意外地進了球，得到一比一的成績，真是太好啦，不然這一場看得真的有點無聊XD

大家有追世界盃足球賽嗎?雖然看直播挺累人的，但也很刺激啦，也是不錯的生活體驗。

links.title: ‎Why Kindness Still Matters Today ‎
links.body:
‎Hi Hive,
‎
‎We live in a time where life feels faster than ever. Everyone seems busy trying to meet deadlines, earn a living, and deal with their own personal struggles. Because of this, simple acts of kindness can sometimes be ignored. Yet, I believe kindness is one of the things that the world needs now more than ever due what life has turned out to.
‎ https://img.leopedia.io/DQmNnAWrqf3hdc4icQoMjcNi3hkUtNCu8FiGRBD6jgJJ8Va/sammy-sander-light-box-5531025_1920.jpg 

‎[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/light-box-sign-message-quote-great-5531025/)
‎
‎One thing I have noticed is that we never really know what someone else is going through. A person may look fine on the outside but be dealing with stress, disappointment, or challenges that nobody else can see. In moments like these, a kind word, a smile, or even taking a few minutes to listen can mean a lot more than we realize.
‎
‎What I love about kindness is that it doesn't cost anything. You don't need money or special skills to be kind. Holding a door open, helping someone carry a heavy load, checking on a friend, or simply saying \

are little actions that can brighten someone's day. These gestures may seem insignificant, but they often leave lasting memories.
‎
‎Kindness also has a way of spreading. When someone treats us with kindness, we naturally feel encouraged to do the same for others too. It's like a ripple effect. One good deed can inspire another, and before you know it, many people have been positively affected by a single action.
‎
‎Another reason kindness matters is that it helps bring people together. We all come from different backgrounds and have different opinions, but kindness allows us to connect on a human level. It reminds us that despite our differences, we all want to be treated with respect and understanding.
‎
‎The world may continue to change, but kindness will never lose its value. In fact, I think its importance grows during difficult times. A little kindness can give someone hope, restore their confidence, or simply make them feel seen and appreciated.
‎
‎At the end of the day, being kind is a choice we can all make. It may seem like a small thing, but it has the power to make a real difference in the lives of others and in our communities as a whole.
‎
‎Thanks for reading!!!!
‎
‎![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYaWnApEziAtLL5Zwv3ZNbDjRfSfG6h5njgTrpyasnE6y/1775569275821.png)
‎

links.title: It's strange that people expecting vivid impressions, for example, at a seaside resort, suddenly find themselves spending time in the pouring rain...
links.body:
If I say that every person, when taking any trip, even the shortest one in their life, wants it to be crowned with vivid impressions, then... But not every trip brings them. Before the trip, you probably need to clearly define what exactly is meant by this phrase and, at a minimum, invite them by sending them a telegram, calling, or sending them a message in any messenger. Otherwise, they may simply not know you're expecting them and will be preoccupied with their own, more important matters. ![1y1DSC09290.png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmZ7Wy7dYrG49pWwSg2tqwh3oyDRZzTSYQ36rR74VmH5b2/1y1DSC09290.png) It's strange that people expecting vivid impressions, for example, at a seaside resort, suddenly find themselves spending time in the pouring rain under an awning instead of experiencing them on the beach. в селі. Підписую, щоб потім не здогадуватися. Сейфом я називаю шафу, яка закривається на ключ😄. Там є речі, які я не хочу викидувати, бо вони мають власну історію. Мені навпаки подобається, коли навколо зберігається багато цінних історіями речей. \nЗавжди питаю себе, чи дім має бути схожим на музей, де потрібно просто  витирати пил? Чи це мій простір і мій хаос, де я знаю кожен куток і де лежить кожен дорогий мені клаптик.\nНещодавно, коли моя мама приїхала з Італії, то викинула жмут сухих рослин. І я дуже засмутилася, бо побачила ці рослини вже поламані і в смітнику вечором, коли повернулася додому. Мама здивувалася, що це просто сухе сміття. А для мене це був певний спогад, як ми поверталися з Гавареччини до Львова, як зупинилися на узбіччі, а навколо поля, як ми їли піцу, а Максим вередував, а потім ми робили фото в ріпаку, і я нарвала тих рослин. Це був певний символ того часу проведеного разом.

>Viele ältere Männer im Osten Deutschland wären durchaus noch in der Lage, den Russen einige Stunden an der Oder aufzuhalten.

Sie sind wehrunwürdig, sie stehen im Verdacht, mit dem Kreml und seinem völkerrechtswidrigen Angriff auf die verbündete Ukraine zu sympathisieren. Zudem sind sie alt, häufig krank und an Waffen ausgebildet, die das deutsche Verteidigungsministerium direkt nach dem Anschluss der verbliebenen deutschen Ostgebiete an
rel=\
target=\

>kriegführende Entwicklungsländer wie die Türkei verkauft hat.  

Soldaten und Offiziere, die ihren Dienst oder Wehrdienst in der Nationalen Volksarmee der DDR oder in deren menschenverachtenden Grenztruppen absolviert haben, wurde mit dem Einigungsvertrag von der Ehre ausgeschlossen. Das neue, wiedervereinigte Deutschland mit der Waffe in der Hand gegen anstürmende Feinde verteidigen darf nur, wer nicht schon den Uniformrock des anderen Deutschland getragen hat. Mit gutem Grund: Das DDR-Offizierskorps bestand zu 80 Prozent aus Mitgliedern der SED, die sich der deutschen Einheit - inzwischen umbenannt in PDS - bis zum letzten Augenblick gemeinsam mit den Grünen entgegenstellte.

>Deutschland hatte zu viele Soldaten 

Auch die von der Staatspartei mit Drohungen und Druck zum sogenannten Ehrendienst gepressten Wehrdienstpflichtigen erschienen dem damaligen Bundesverteidigungsminister Gerhard Stoltenberg nicht als willkommene Verstärkung seiner Truppen. Der CDU-Politiker stand viel mehr vor der Aufgabe, die Gesamtstärke von Heer, Marine und Luftwaffe schleunigst abzuschmelzen.

Von 500.000 Soldaten, so hatten es die Deutschen der Sowjetunion im Zwei-plus-Vier-Vertrag völkerrechtlich verbindlich zugesichert, würden künftig
rel=\
target=\
>nur noch 370.000 Mann verbleiben. Die Friedensdividende aus eingesparten Mannschaften und Material setzte Deutschland gewinnbringend ein: Seit Anfang der 90er Jahre stiegen die
rel=\
target=\
> Ausgaben für Sozialleistungen von  400 Milliarden Euro auf
rel=\
target=\

>mehr als 1,3 Billionen Euro. Die Bundeswehr wurde in diesen Jahrzehnten nicht besser, nur kleiner. Verteidigungsminister waren mit Abrissarbeiten beschäftigt, sie wollen Deutschland am Hindukusch verteidigen oder sie konzentrierten sich ganz auf den
rel=\
target=\
>Kampf gegen den inneren Feind.

>Das Warten auf höfliche Fragen 

Ganz ohne Gefechte blutete das Land aus. Seit dem Aussetzen der Wehrpflicht ist eine Generation herangewachsen, die fest davon überzeugt ist, dass sie im Ernstfall höflich gefragt würden, ob sie nicht Lust verspüren, an der Front ein wenig auf den Feind zu schießen. Ein deutliches Nein, glauben sie, würde die Häscher der Bundeswehr ganz schnell davon überzeugen, sie mit ihrem Cafè Latte Haselnut im Straßencafé sitzen und weiter friedlich pazifizieren zu lassen.

Die letzte Rettung des Vaterlandes, so hat es der aus Ostdeutschland stammende  CDU-Vize Sepp Müller jetzt deutlich gemacht, sind
rel=\
target=\

>die kriegstüchtigen Senioren, die das blutige Soldatenhandwerk noch unter den alten Haudegen Keßler und Hoffmann gelernt haben. Diese Generation der Kalter-Kriegsrentner will Müller, 1989 geboren, als rüstige Reservisten für die Bundeswehr gewinnen. Der Unionspolitiker greift damit eine Idee des Altlinken Dietmar Bartsch auf, der von 1976 bis 1978 selbst noch freiwillig drei Jahre Ehrendienst im einzigen Fallschirmjägerbataillon 40 der Nationalen Volksarmee abgeleistet hatte.

>Zurück zum Friedensdienst 

Eine Zeitenwende, die gänzlich unerwartet kommt. Noch vor vier Monaten war das Heer der drei bis vier Millionen Männer, die in der DDR zum \
mit der Waffe gezwungen worden waren, als weiterhin so unsichere Kantonisten eingeschätzt worden, dass ihnen die Teilnahme am neugeschaffenen <a href=\
rel=\
target=\

der Streitkräfte hatte versagt werden müssen. 

Die bei weitem größte Opfergruppe, die das SED-Regime hinterlassen hat, fand nicht nur weiterhin keine Lobby, die sich für ihren guten Ruf einsetzte. Sondern sie fand eine, die mit ihrem demonstrativen Ausschluss vom \
(Bundeswehr) keinen Zweifel daran ließ, dass es sich bei den Betreffenden um nach wie vor um Angehörige <a href=\
rel=\
target=\
(Wissenschaftlicher Dienst des Bundestages).

>Fleischpolster für das Stachelschwein 

Sepp Müller will das Potenzial an Kanonenfutter jetzt aber doch ebnen. Da die Bundeswehr derzeit weder über ausreichend Personal noch über Panzer, Jagdflieger oder
rel=\
target=\

> gar Drohnen verfügt, um einen durch Polen gebrochenen Gegner aufzuhalten, lockt die schiere Menge an ehemals zumindest rudimentär an russischen Waffen ausgebildeten Männern, die Ursula von der Leyen geplantes das
rel=\
target=\
von außen mit Fleisch polstern könnten. Müller will die infrage kommenden 53- bis 99-Jährigen \
ausbilden, einer Art <a href=\
rel=\
target=\
>Blitzkrieger 2.0, der schnellbesohlt wird, aber aufgrund früher gemachter leidvoller Erfahrungen an der Front vermutlich länger durchhält als die jüngere
rel=\
target=\
>Sofakriegergeneration oder
rel=\
target=\

>spätberufene Kostümoffiziere.

Die Männer, die schon die friedliche Revolution, den Rückbau der selbsternannten zehntgrößten Industrienation der Welt und die Transformation Ostdeutschlands zu einer national befreiten Zone betrieben haben, wären als Teil der Bundeswehr ein probates Mittel gegen die grassierende Personalnot bei der Truppe. 

Als \

(Sepp Müller) träten sie in die großen Fußstapfen des früheren Volkssturms und der Kampfgruppen der Arbeiterklasse in der DDR. Im Gegensatz zu Marcel Fratzscher, der die Mittfünfziger, Endsechziger und hohen 70er zu einem <a href=\
rel=\
target=\
>Zwangsdienst verpflichten will, setzt Müller \
.

>Ein greises Ersatzheer 

Müller selbst kommt für das greise Ersatzheer nicht in Betracht, nicht wegen seines Alters, sondern weil er keinen Wehrdienst geleistet hat. Er wünsche sich \
, umreist der gebürtige Wittenberger seine Überlegungen, Lehrgänge anzubieten, die berücksichtigen, \
seien. Um ihre Treue zu versichern, müssten die Anwärter auf eine Heimatschützeruniform abschließend ein \

sprechen. 

Das dient dann vorbeugend auch dazu, den Bannfluch des ehemals geleisteten Eids auf die Deutsche Demokratische Republik, \
zu brechen und das Versprechen des \

Dienstes und des Gehorsams den Befehlen der Arbeiter-und-Bauern-Regierung gegenüber aufzuheben.

Dass der Osten rechts ist und
rel=\
target=\
>seine Männer je
rel=\
target=\

>älter desto schlimmer, kann im Augenblick höchster Bedrohung keine Rolle mehr spielen. Der Generalverdacht gegen ehemalige NVA-Angehörige, sie könnten im ersten Gefecht ihre Gewehre und Kanonen herumdrehen und an der Seite der Russen Richtung Paris marschieren, ist nicht mehr wichtig angesichts der Aussichten, dass der Russe auch allein bis dahin rollt. Noch können Gediente aus fremden Heeren nicht als Reservisten herangezogen werden, wenn sie nicht zu den 18.000 vielfach überprüften NVA-Offizieren gehören, die von der Bundeswehr übernommen wurden.

>Zurück zum Friedensdienst 

Da die Bundeswehr im Verteidigungsfall 200.000 Reservisten benötigt, aber nur 50.000 Reservisten hat, würden mehrere hunderttausend noch feldmarschfähige Ost-Offiziere und -Mannschaften den Mangel schlagartig beheben. Eine Anerkennung der ehemals vom SED-Regime verliehenen militärischen Ränge ermöglichte es zudem, sofort einsatzbereite Heimatschutzregimenter aufzustellen. Alt, aber entschlossen. Rostig, aber rüstig. Die NVA als Volkssturm, zurück im
rel=\
target=\
>Friedensdienst mit der Waffe.

links.title: Ich wollte mir gerade ein auslaufendes \
Ki Projekt von Intel auf Github stehlen...
links.body:
und habe wiederentdeckt, warum ich nie Programmierer geworden bin davor...


Ich meine, ich mach mich Lustig darueber, wie diese Programme alle so gebaut sind.

Hauptsache, nach Stechuhr, wuerde ich sagen und Hauptsache, das nur Fachidioten durchblicken. Egal wie Einfach in Wahrheit, das aus meiner Sicht eigentlich ist! Es wird kompliziert gemacht und keiner Denkt auch nur darueber nach, geschweige denn, falls doch, viel drueber zu sagen.

Man kann so ein Projekt natuerlich nicht einzelnen Programmierern anvertrauen, sondern muss es so gestalten und bauen, das der vielleicht bald gekuendigte Programmierer, moeglichst Schnell ersetzt werden kann.


Zumindest finde ich keinen plausiblen anderen Grund dafuer, warum die alles in tausend kleine Haeppchen hacken und voellig irre in ebensoviel Unterordner und Dateien stecken...

Hauptsache man findet als Laie nichts. 


Soviel zu Lesbarkeit.

Mal ehrlich, wuesstest Du als Laie das ein Programm aus einer Handvoll Dateien besteht, haettest Du dir eines nicht schon ab und an mal angesehen???

Aber die Altprogrammierer, wollen nicht ihren Status verlieren, sie wollen keine wahre Zugaenglichkeit. Sie Scheißen auch auf Performance und Effizienz damit. Sage ich... der einen Computer Lebt.

Und deswegen, nehmen sie auch solche Leergeldprojekte irgendwann wieder vom Tisch.

Weil sie nicht in der Lage waren, bei allem Wissen und Koennen, eben zu sehen, was es bedeutet, das auch weiter zu geben.

Nur durch die alte Schiene, sollen sie alle Fahren. Alle anderen, sind außen vor, und genau die braeuchte man aber fuer solche Sachen, weil die sich eben auch um die Ecke interessieren, nicht wie der Normalmensch, auch mal eine Huerde nehmen.

Aber wenn die Huerden Sinnlos sind... Oder nur Schwachsinn als Vorgabe halten.... dann haben die auch keine Lust bei anderen zu sehen und zu lernen und setzen sich selbst auf den Hosenboden wie ich es gemacht habe, mit Mining und Blockckains, und weiter mache, mit dem Programmieren derselben sowie weiterem.

Studium des Wahnsinns ist das fuer mich bei anderen zu Schauen, keine Informatik.

Der Mensch, macht es sich dort Kompliziert, wo er es Einfach haben koennte, damit er sich groeßer fuehlt oder sowas.

Als wuessten wir irgendwas von unserer Welt.

Ich schreibe meine Programme nach meinen Regeln, und sie werden haesslich sein, aber kleiner, und im Kern der Sache, uebersichtlicher, als das Choas der Tausend Dateien, deren Verbindungen alleine schon Speicher und Leistung ohne Ende fressen muessen.

Weil das kostet alles Rechenkraft die Dekadenz der angeblichen Ordnung.

Ich pfeife auf das auslaufende KI Projekt und baue weiter von Grund auf alles selber, indem ich alles selber lerne, was ich lernen muss und brauche, der Rest, kommt nichtmal in meine Naehe.


Salve

Alucian

links.title: The Global Race for Superintelligent Artificial Intelligence and Worldwide Technological Dominance
links.body: \n<div class=\

> Artificial Intelligence (AI) is undoubtedly one of the most potent technologies invented by humans. Nowadays, numerous nations and tech firms are dedicating billions of dollars to AI studies and development. They are not just making smarter machines; they are striving to make what the experts refer to as “superintelligent” artificial intelligence – an AI that could one day better perform intellectual tasks than humans. This has brought about a worldwide competition among nations and companies to win technological supremacy. Currently the United States and China are racing in this field. Companies like OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Meta are working on more sophisticated AI systems that can comprehend text, create articles, resolve intricate issues, and support individuals in diverse professions. China is also making huge investments in AI research, computing infrastructure, and innovation. These two countries are expected to be at the forefront of technological advancements for the next few decades and their rivalry is expected to define the future of technology. The race is not only confined to the United States and China, though. European, Asian, and other nations are putting substantial efforts into AI investments as well. Governments are aware that AI leadership can lead to economic growth, military dominance, scientific advancements, and heightened international influence. Countries with robust AI capabilities could reap numerous benefits in healthcare, education, manufacturing, transportation, and cybersecurity. This is an exciting and troubling international competition to me. AI can address a lot of the world's biggest problems on the one side.On the other side, AI has the capability to address many of humanity's greatest challenges. It can aid doctors to make accurate diagnosis, support scientists in the discovery of new things, help farmers in the agriculture process and render education more accessible. AI can also drive productivity growth and open up new avenues for businesses and workers to engage in and benefit from. These advantages may enhance the lifestyle of millions of individuals throughout the globe. ![1001614349.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thepromise/23wWrUZAn2MY4suK4Yj6Eju36VcX2kLm4em1ZpjArbiogVcrCSdfcmozYhvEJCxauutSa.png) However, the competition for super-intelligent AI is also very concerning. Countries who only strive to win the competition might neglect other critical concerns like safety, ethics, privacy and accountability. The potential risks of advanced AI systems have been noted by some researchers, who caution against their potential to generate risks when not managed or regulated appropriately. Some worry that AI will lead to more misinformation, cyber attacks and global tensions between strong states. Due to this, there is a growing emphasis on the need for global collaboration and the responsible management of AI. Computing power, sophisticated semiconductors, and skilled researchers are other important factors of this race. Powerful AI systems need huge quantities of data, energy and specialised computer chips. Control of these resources confers a competitive edge to the countries that possess them in their development of the next generation of AI technologies. Consequently, technological leadership is increasingly linked to the strength of the nation and its security. To conclude, the competition for the superintelligent artificial intelligence is one of the most important milestones in our time. It's a competition that could change the nature of economies, industries, international relations. The search for technological supremacy can result in great innovations but should also be accompanied by responsibility, cooperation and moral principles. The real success of AI lies not in who can build the strongest system first, but in humanity's ability to harness this technology for the betterment of lives and the creation of a better future for all. links.title: went to a professional basketball game in Da Nang, Vietnam
links.body: I would imagine that most people are unaware that there is a professional basketball league in Vietnam. I live here and I was unaware of it so you would be well excused for not knowing. It came up because as I was walking my dog past a sports bar yesterday morning a friend who lives in my building was catching the end of the World Cup game featuring the USA who won their game 4-1. hooray I guess! Well, he told me he was planning on going to see the DaNang Dragons play that evening in town and I wanted to head along as well. So I did!
alt=\

> I don't really follow sports very closely and I suppose you could say that I don't really care. It's just not my thing but a lot of this has to do with the fact that if I was to try to follow the sports that I grew up with, I would have to stay up very late or I would have to wake up early in the morning. Since watching sports in public normally comes along with drinking beer, I tend to not include this in my repertoire because I definitely don't need to be drinking alcohol in the morning. Going to see this game though, that was kind of perfect, or so it seemed at the time.
alt=\

> I've been to high school games in USA with more people in attendance than this so suffice to say, basketball isn't really that popular here. I think much of this has to do with the fact that at barely 6 feet tall, I am much taller than the average Vietnamese person.
alt=\

> The game was reasonably exciting, I suppose. But one thing that I found continually frustrating is that the players just aren't very good. Lots of very basic mistakes were made such as most of the free throws being missed (an unforgivable sin in a sport where half of the points are potentially made there) and easy shots like layups were thrown wildly out of play or banked off the bottom of the basket. There were also a handful of airballs where if you don't know what that means, it is that a player tried a shot and missed it so badly that it didn't hit anything at all. Perhaps some of this could be attributed to the fact that it was extremely hot in this arena or stadium, and the players were sweating a lot.
alt=\

> Every so often the players would get a bit of a break and they, especially the foreigners on the team, would be constantly toweling sweat of themselves. I was sat in the stands and I was sweating despite not even moving. The game was fine, and you definitely cannot argue with the $2 entry fee that came with a free ice cream. But there was one aspect of it that I should have seen coming that really annoyed me. I just should have known that this was going to be a very loud affair.
alt=\

>
</center>

In the stands next to the one that I was in was the cheer section or something and this was a dude waving a giant flag and some youngsters on drums that played them as loud as they could with repetitive chants for the **entire damn game**.  There was also a DJ on the other side of the court with a microphone that would shout \

every single time Da Nang was on defense.

you are on defense a lot in basketball
alt=\

>
</center>

As is tradition in Vietnam apparently, the amplification was about 5 times as loud as it needed to be and by the 2nd half, my face hurt from the noise and I spent most of the rest of the game with my fingers in my ears.   

It didn't help that even though none of the teams would be considered good by proper metrics, Da Nang is the worst team in the league and hasn't won a single game so far this season.  They were playing the 2nd worst team and I guess there were some high hopes that they would pull of a \

tonight. At the start of the game the Dragons managed to get more than 10 points in the lead, but then I guess they just stopped remembering how to play basketball and by the 3rd quarter they were down by 15. They did manage to rally towards the end and got within 5, and had a number of opportunities to level the score, but they squandered all of them, including missing both free throws twice in a row. By the time there was less than 30 seconds left and they were down by 5, me and my friend headed for the door. I would like to say that this was a worthwhile experience but because of the excessive noise, I am very unlikely to ever return to do this again. I did find out a few things though. each team is only allowed to have 2 foreigners on their team, the rest have to be Vietnamese. As you would expect, the foreigners are the best players on the team and the tallest. Our biggest guy was an American who was 6 foot 9 and he just towered over almost all of the Vietnamese players.
alt=\

>
</center>

When we got outside and a bit away from the stadium I was just delighted to not be having my ears assaulted anymore.   

I just don't get why it is that not just Vietnamese, but all South East Asian countries, seem to really enjoy excessive amplification all the time.   I expect there will be an epidemic of hearing loss in the next generation because honestly, me and my friend seemed to be the only people in the stands that were bothered by it.  

Is this culture?  I just don't get how someone can be cool with something so piercingly loud being cast upon them for several hours in a row.   

I told my friend in the taxi home (which cost more than the game did and didn't have free ice cream) that I am not going to go to that again... not this season at least seeing as how the Dragons already lost a game to the best team in the league by more than 50 points.

Над відео працювала команда з понад 80 людей. Ця масштабна відеоробота допомагає глибше розкрити головну ідею композиції. # HiveSuite 

## Wallet Approval Hints & Notification Feedback Improvements

### Universal Wallet Approval Guidance

- Whenever users sign actions using:
  - Keychain  
  - HiveAuth  
  - PeakVault  


- HiveSuite now displays a clear blinking:
  - `Open Keychain App & Approve` hint  


### Expanded Approval Hint Coverage

- Approval hints now appear consistently across:
  - Posts  
  - Blogs  
  - Snaps  
  - User profiles  
  - Community detail pages  
  - Videos  
  - My Videos  
  - Shorts  


### Smart Visibility Rules

- Approval hints only appear when external wallet authorization is required.  

- In-app private-key signing does not show the hint:
  - No unnecessary prompts  
  - Cleaner signing experience  


### Inbox Feedback Improvements

- `Mark as Done` button inside Inbox now displays:
  - Loading spinner  
  - `Marking…` status label  


- Makes background processing state clearly visible during notification actions.  


### Local HiveReactKit Integration

- Hive React Kit remains linked locally:
  - All kit-level updates appear instantly inside HiveSuite during development  


- Outcome:
  - Better transaction clarity for users  
  - Improved feedback during blockchain actions  
  - More consistent signing UX throughout HiveSuite  


Keychain Approval Hint
![Keychain Approval Hint - Inbox](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQYsiunWKkHCz8jqn1UXqeJAtC7wxVuVQADw6imn9RDKA/image.png)


![Wallet Approval Hint - Post Detail Page](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcFjH4ZNz2NmrnwiqWTNEYcjNf9Up3Gv9tP8HbXSH5KwH/image.png)


---

## Progressive Web App (PWA) Support for Mobile Devices

### Installable Mobile Experience

- HiveSuite can now be installed directly onto:
  - Android home screens  
  - iPhone home screens  


- Provides a lightweight app-like experience without requiring a native app installation.  


### Optimized Lightweight Storage

- Initial install stores only essential application assets:
  - Remaining resources load on demand  


- Keeps phone storage usage minimal while maintaining performance.  


### Offline Access Support

- Once visited online:
  - HiveSuite opens instantly even without internet connectivity  


- Previously viewed content remains accessible offline.  


### Smart Image & Media Caching

- Post and video images are stored locally after first view:
  - Reduces repeated loading  
  - Improves browsing speed  


### Fresh Blockchain Interaction Rules

- Live blockchain actions always fetch fresh data:
  - Votes  
  - Comments  
  - Other interaction states  


- Prevents stale cached interaction data from appearing.  


### Silent Application Updates

- New HiveSuite versions update automatically in the background:
  - No intrusive refresh popups  
  - Updates applied on next visit  


- Outcome:
  - Faster mobile experience  
  - Better offline usability  
  - More native-app-like performance on phones

## Hide Voted Filters for Blogs & Snaps

### New Hide Voted Toggle

- Added new `Hide voted` checkbox beside the refresh button in:
  - Blogs feed  
  - Snaps feed  


### Fresh Content Browsing

- When enabled:
  - Posts already upvoted by the current user disappear from the feed  


- Makes it easier to browse:
  - Fresh content  
  - Unseen posts  


### Persistent Per-Feed Preferences

- Filter state persists across:
  - Page reloads  
  - Navigation changes  


- Blogs and Snaps store their filter settings independently:
  - Enabling one does not affect the other  


### Authentication-Aware Visibility

- `Hide voted` checkbox only appears for:
  - Signed-in users  


### Accurate Vote Filtering

- Only posts the user has upvoted are hidden.  

- Flagged or downvoted posts remain visible inside feeds.  


- Outcome:
  - Easier discovery of fresh content  
  - Better personalized feed browsing  
  - Cleaner engagement workflow for active curators
